title: sycl: opt-in grouped XMX expert GEMM for the prompt path (STRATA_PF_XMX), with a parity test
body:
Adds an opt-in grouped XMX GEMM for the prompt path's routed experts on Intel Arc. With `STRATA_PF_XMX` unset, the default path does not change.

## What it changes

- `STRATA_PF_XMX=1`: dequantizes a group of up to 16 routed experts to FP16, then runs one `joint_matrix` launch per product. A standalone measurement against oneMKL on uneven routing: down 1.75–6x faster, gate/up 0.8–3x. Above `STRATA_PF_XMX_GU_MAX=250` tokens per expert, gate/up stays on oneMKL.
- `STRATA_PF_XMX=2`: the same GEMM, but the kernel decodes the IQ3_XXS / IQ3_S / IQ2_S / IQ4_XS gate/up rows and the IQ4_NL / Q2_0 down rows itself, so there is no FP16 staging pass.
- New `xmx_group_parity` test (built with `STRATA_SYCL_PARITY=ON`): checks every supported type against dequant+oneMKL.

The third commit (8f4ddb1) makes both kernels build and run on Xe2 (Battlemage). There they use 16×16×16 tiles with sub-group 16, following @maxious's retile; DG2 keeps 8×8×16 with sub-group 8. A JIT build picks per device, and an AOT build carries only the 16×16 kernel (`sycl/include/strata/xmx_tile.hpp`).

The second commit fixes the in-kernel decode after rebasing onto current `main`. `main` now has the IQ2/IQ3/IQ4_NL/IQ1_M decoders write values `[8·tid, 8·tid+8)` in coalesced runs. The grouped kernel was still passing the old `sub*8 + o32/32` thread index, so four of the six types decoded garbage (relative error ≈10). It now passes `tid = o >> 3` for every type except IQ4_XS, which keeps its own layout.

## Measured

On an Arc A770 16 GB (xe driver, oneAPI 2025.3, Linux 7.0), `xmx_group_parity` on this branch:

```
type 18 gate/up rows 1365: dequant+oneMKL 2.593 ms | fused xmx 1.800 ms (1.44x) relerr 9.9e-07 OK
type 21 gate/up rows 1365: dequant+oneMKL 1.507 ms | fused xmx 1.765 ms (0.85x) relerr 1.1e-06 OK
type 22 gate/up rows 1365: dequant+oneMKL 1.238 ms | fused xmx 1.330 ms (0.93x) relerr 1.5e-06 OK
type 23 gate/up rows 1365: dequant+oneMKL 2.498 ms | fused xmx 1.516 ms (1.65x) relerr 1.8e-06 OK
type 20 down    rows 1365: dequant+oneMKL 0.825 ms | fused xmx 0.773 ms (1.07x) relerr 4.6e-07 OK
type 42 down    rows 1365: dequant+oneMKL 0.700 ms | fused xmx 0.603 ms (1.16x) relerr 1.5e-07 OK
all OK
```

Without the second commit, types 18, 21, 22 and 20 fail with relative error ≈10.

End to end, on the Coder IQ1_M model with an 8K prompt:
- Earlier local measurements, before the rebase: 0.5–3K-token prompts were 14–29% faster with `STRATA_PF_XMX=2`, and 8K/32K prompts 2–5% faster. These were not repeated on this branch.
- This branch, `main` + #1602 on the A770: a same-day 8K run did not show a gain.

So it stays opt-in.

On the same A770 with this branch: 2,058-token code prompt, greedy decoding, 128 new tokens. `STRATA_PF_XMX=0` gave 847.8 and 832.6 tok/s prompt, `=2` gave 847.3 and 825.3, `=1` gave 835.7, all with identical output. On an Arc Pro B60, @maxious measured the fused path at about 2.9x slower than the default (505.5 vs 177.3 tok/s prompt). It stays opt-in and off by default.

## Not tested

- Running on B-series here: AOT `bmg-g21` links on this branch, but I have no Battlemage card. @maxious ran the 16×16 kernels on a B60.
- Other Alchemist cards.
- The CUDA and HIP builds: these files are SYCL only (`sycl/`), plus one declaration in `include/strata/kernels/iq_kernels.hpp` and a new `include/strata/prefill/xmx_moe.hpp`, neither of which the CUDA/HIP sources include.
- A full logit comparison end to end with `STRATA_PF_XMX=2`. The parity test covers the kernel only.

title: 0.1.41: 128K decode is 18% slower than 0.1.40.3 on an RTX 4090 (sm_89); STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0 gives all of it back
body:
**On a Windows RTX 4090 (sm_89, IQ3_S pack) the 128K-context decode drops from 90.3–95.4 tok/s on v0.1.40.3 to 73.2–78.4 on v0.1.41 — four runs, no overlap between the arms — while prefill at the same context is unchanged (3705.5–3774.7 vs 3745.0–3749.4). On the same v0.1.41 binary, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0` restores 90.7 and 91.9 tok/s, inside the v0.1.40.3 band, and short-context decode keeps its v0.1.41 gain (8K per-request decode 105.3–118.6 with IL off, 89.2–109.6 with IL on, 63.6–83.3 on v0.1.40.3). The engine's own table says why this card in particular: `native_mmvq.cu:2510` — "sm_89 (Ada) has none yet: nobody measured it (we have no such card), so it takes the shared table", and that shared table was read off an RTX 3060 (sm_86) and an RTX 5070 (sm_120) with the rule "the worse of the two cards still takes at least 3% off `native_mmvq`'s time". Limits: one 4090 rig, one quant, one model; the same A/B on an A100-class A30 (sm_80, UD-Q4_K_XL, Linux) shows **no effect at all**, so this is a table-tuning miss on an unmeasured card, not a general regression.**
## Setup
Windows 11, RTX 4090 24 GB (+ a GTX 1660 Ti holding only the vision encoder), 128 GB RAM, CUDA 12.9, engine from the release zip (`source: release`, `experimental: true`).
- v0.1.41 `strata.exe` md5 `39898e491e796c51b7d042783817d2ae`; v0.1.40.3 md5 `5ad3617a7a9a5c7fb330e6add75fc87c`.
- Pack: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S. Engine args (identical in both arms, verified from the startup block, which is byte-identical apart from the version string): `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp <rt> --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --ple-io ram --pcie-frac 0.0 --vram-reserve-mib 700 --vision` → `8251 slots / 15.65 GiB`, `424 MiB of VRAM free`, `verify: window up to 6 tokens`, `draft head over 106299 tokens`.
- Method: `tools/staged_bench.py` with **one salt label across all arms**, so the prompt bytes are identical; arms alternate order per round; each arm's binary is re-checked by md5 after the swap. Decode is the engine's own per-request line right after the 128K prefill (48 tokens, `--ask` = the prime list).
## The 128K decode, six samples
| arm | 48 tokens | decode tok/s | verify windows (steps) | ms per step |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| v0.1.41, IL on (default) r1 | 656 ms | 73.2 | 45 | 14.6 |
| v0.1.41, IL on (default) r2 | 612 ms | 78.4 | 42 | 14.6 |
| **v0.1.41 + `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0`** direct | **529 ms** | **90.7** | 41 | 12.9 |
| **v0.1.41 + `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0`** via a proxy | **522 ms** | **91.9** | 37 | 14.1 |
| v0.1.40.3 r1 / r2 | 503 / 532 ms | 95.4 / 90.3 | 37 / 41 | 13.6 / 13.0 |
The step count is **not** the effect: across all six samples it moves 37–45 on its own (48 tokens is a small sample), so read it aligned — at 41 steps IL-on gives 78.4 and IL-off gives 90.7 (+15.7%). The per-step cost is the effect, and that is also what kills the natural first guess: **this is not KV streaming or bandwidth.** The KV ledger is the same in every arm (`KV streaming: 88.77% of 382044 block reads hit VRAM, 172.8 MiB read from RAM` in the IL-off run; 88.4–89.3% in the IL-on runs), the expert hit rate is the same (85.5–90.1%), and prefill at 128K never moves (3786.0 / 3788.0 tok/s with IL off).
## The A30 (sm_80) is unaffected — same A/B, env-only arms on one binary
A100-class A30 24 GB, Xeon Gold 5320, Linux, CUDA 12.4 build, UD-Q4_K_XL pack, `0c085b0de2386b30e8c11cbb6a21974c`, 5184 slots, 2 rounds × 2 arms, order alternated, same salt:
| A30 | IL on (default) | `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0` |
|---|---|---|
| 128K prefill tok/s | 1566.4 / 1554.3 | 1553.8 / 1552.9 |
| **128K decode tok/s** | **63.0 / 62.8** | **62.1 / 63.4** |
| 512 / 1k / 8K prefill | 438.6 / 561.7 / 1170.6 | 439.3 / 561.2 / 1168.5 |
| decode best (3 × 128 at 8K) | 79.4 | 79.3 |
So the same default-on path is free on sm_80 and costs ~18% on sm_89 at long context.
## Why I think it is the table, not the kernel
`native_mmvq_il_supported()` gates IL to types IQ4_XS / Q4_K / Q5_K / Q6_K, 2–4 columns, sm_80+ (or sm_70 with the opt-in), and `g_multi_exact`. The rows-a-warp choice comes from `native_mmvq_il_rows_for(cc, …)`, whose only per-architecture entry is `kIlRows_70`; **every other sm_80+ card, sm_89 and sm_80 included, uses `kIlRowsShared`**, measured on an RTX 3060 and an RTX 5070 with a "worse card still ≥3% faster" rule. A 4090 is neither card, and the cells that matter for a decode window are exactly the 2–4-column dense projections. The source comment even names the fix and the no-rebuild override: `mmvq_il_parity --bench --emit-table` → paste as `kIlRows_89`, or `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_ROWS="type:ncols:r0,r1,r2,r3,r4;…"`.
## Ruled out
- Draft acceptance / speculative depth: the acceptance column is equal or better on 0.1.41 in every context bucket over 3,240 production requests on this box; `--spec 4` identical; coupled drafting and `STRATA_SPEC_PROB` / `SPEC_GUMBEL` / `SPEC_MIN_TEMP` are off by default and not enabled here.
- Every other new long-context path in 0.1.41 is gated away on this card: PDL and the decode top-k thread-block cluster need sm_90+; the FP32 tiled block scorer needs <sm_80 and `STRATA_SELECT_SIMT=1`; the pre75 attention kernel needs <sm_75; `STRATA_PIN_GUARD` / `PIN_RESERVE_GIB` are inside `#if defined(__linux__)`; `file_cache_keeps`' hot fraction explicitly keeps the Windows rule; `STAGE_PIN` is `STAGE_PIN_DEFAULT 0`.
- KV residency and expert cache: identical args, identical hit rates, identical `VRAM free` line.
- The `3 × 128 at 8K` decode metric cannot see this at all: it reads 132.5–138.1 on 0.1.41 and 134.9–142.5 on 0.1.40.3, i.e. "no difference", while the 128K decode is 18% down. Worth saying about the release gate: it caught `STRATA_PIN_GUARD`/`STAGE_PIN` corrupting IQ3_S decode, but a default-on decode kernel that costs 18% only at long context passes it, because the gate's decode number is a short-context one.
## What I am asking
1. Is IL default-on intended for sm_80+ cards that have no measured table, or only for the shapes where the shared table was actually measured? On this 4090 the honest answer for long-context decode is that the shared table is a guess that loses ~18%.
2. Would a measured `kIlRows_89` (and an sm_80 entry, since the A30 also inherits the shared table) be welcome? We own a 4090 and an A30 and can run `mmvq_il_parity --bench --emit-table` if a Windows/CUDA 12.9 build recipe for that binary is documented (`docs/MMVQ_IL_TABLE.md` is referenced in the source comment).
3. If a table is not coming soon, is `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_ROWS` with the 4090's costly cells set to 0 the intended interim answer? We are running `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0` in production on this box now, which is coarser than needed.
We can also sweep `STRATA_MMVQ_IL_ROWS` per type on this 4090 (four 128K decode runs, ~2 minutes each) and report which cells cost, if that helps narrow it without an Ada card in your lab.
Engine log lines for all six 128K runs are attached (`strata-iq3_s.log`, the `prompt 158896 tokens = …` lines with their `drafts accepted A of B` and `KV streaming:` follow-ups).

title: serve: an opt-in VRAM headroom for --expert-cache auto (#1549)
body:
## What this changes

`--expert-cache auto` sizes the VRAM-resident expert tier to every byte the card reports free. On a card
that ends up nearly full that is wrong by a lot: the prompt path then reads tens of times slower while
doing exactly the same work.

It adds one opt-in setting and **changes no default**:

```
STRATA_EXPERT_CACHE_HEADROOM=<fraction>    # "1/6", "0.17", or "0" for the sizing you have today
```

the share of free device memory `auto` keeps for the session's other buffers instead of experts. The
helper is `strata::core::expert_cache_headroom()` in `include/strata/core/expert_cache.hpp`, read by
the CUDA/HIP sizing in `src/program/generate.cpp`.

**What it leaves alone.** The default is zero, so every backend keeps the sizing it always had and the
default path is byte-identical to the last release: with the variable unset, the old expression is
evaluated. An explicit `--expert-cache N` is the user's own budget and is never cut. When the headroom
would leave no room at all, the old sizing stands. Nothing in the prompt, decode or expert paths is
touched - the cache is just sized smaller.

## Why, and what it was measured on

An Arc Pro B70 (32 GB, driver 32.0.101.8976), the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS pack, OpenCL backend,
eager, `--prefill 4096`, greedy, 64-token prompt. The same 3,668 gate/up and 3,668 down naive GEMM calls
at every cache size - only the cache size and the memory left over change:

| expert cache | VRAM of experts | prefill | ms per expert GEMM call |
|---|---|---|---|
| 17,687 slots (`auto` before) | 28.82 GiB | 426 s | 111 |
| 15,382 slots | 24.95 GiB | 472 s | 122 |
| 14,704 slots | 23.87 GiB | 9.7 s | 2.32 |
| 10,698 slots | 17.36 GiB | 10.3 s | 2.39 |

A cliff, not a slope: every size up to 14,704 slots is stable at ~10 s and every size from 15,382 up
takes minutes. The two expert GEMM phases are 95.8% of the GPU timeline in the slow arm, and the phase
waiting for the host-to-device staging copies is **34 ms of 957,283** - the bytes are not the problem.
Memory during the slow pass peaks at 31.2 GiB of dedicated memory (the card full) and holds ~15 GiB
shared; the fast one peaks at 30.08 GiB dedicated and ~3.4 GiB shared. That is consistent with WDDM
paging an over-subscribed allocation to system memory, which the engine's own comment at the sizing
describes, but it is not proven.

Ruled out, each measured: the host mirror (35% of the same pack mirrored over PCIe costs nothing, 2.05
ms per call against 2.01 with every expert resident); the prompt length (the cost is fixed per expert
call, not per token); subnormals in the dequantized weights or activations (none in either pack);
`--kv-resident` (7,589 ms against 7,587 ms). The kernel calls and their shapes are identical in every
arm. No accuracy cost: the cut and the uncut sizing give identical greedy output tokens - eight tokens,
`271 71093 271 550 18381 198 12 1510`, from a scrambled 48-token prompt.

`docs/EXPERT_CACHE_HEADROOM.md` has the full findings, the A/B protocol for a card this has not been
measured on, and what each outcome would mean; `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` gets a row for it.

## How I checked it

- With the variable unset, `free_room` is the expression the last release evaluates - no code path
  changes.
- With `1/6` set on the B70, the knob reproduces the measurement: 14,688 slots (23.83 GiB) against
  17,687 (28.82 GiB) unset, with identical output tokens.
- The header compiles: the SYCL build includes it and passes.
- **Not compiled:** this machine has no `nvcc` or `hipcc`, so the CUDA/HIP sources in this pull request
  were not built where the change was written. The call site is the same statement the SYCL port makes
  against the same helper.

## What this is not

This is not a claim that the effect is real on NVIDIA or AMD. It is Windows/WDDM evidence from one
Intel card, offered as a knob so it can be measured elsewhere. If it turns out to be a no-op on CUDA
the default stays zero, and if the cliff is real there the numbers from the A/B are what would justify
turning it on.

Closes the sizing half of #1549.

title: Windows: native Intel Arc build and setup (OpenCL), plus three Windows-SDK macro fixes
body:
### What



Native Windows support for the SYCL port (`setup --backend sycl`): no Docker, the engine is built from source with

Intel oneAPI (`sycl\tools\build.bat`) and run directly (`sycl\serve\strata-sycl.bat`). Plus the fixes the port needs

to compile on Windows at all, and the no-command-graph paths ΓÇö this Windows driver exposes no user-mode Level Zero

adapter, so the OpenCL adapter has no Graph extension.



Replaces #1295: that branch predates 0.1.40.2, and the release merged most of its forward-port (and has its own

`STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER` window replay), so this one carries the Windows deltas only ΓÇö 4 commits.



## Measured



Arc Pro B70 32 GB, Windows 10, driver 32.0.101.8976, i9-9900 / 64 GB, conda-forge `dpcpp_win-64` 2026.1.1, OpenCL

backend, `STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1`. Coder IQ1_M, 12,288/12,288 experts resident, `--stream-experts`, INT8 KV, greedy.

Each row is this branch's engine (0.1.40-sycl) against the previous 0.1.39-based build of this port, run

**interleaved** from the command line (v1, v2, v1, v2, ΓÇª), which is how the numbers in docs/INTEL.md were taken:



| | 0.1.39-sycl | 0.1.40-sycl (this PR) | Linux / Level Zero / graphs |

|---|---|---|---|

| decode, 256 tokens, `--spec 4 --mtp`, 3 pairs | 69.6-69.9 (median 69.7) | **77.2-77.3 (median 77.3)** | 78.2 |

| decode, 128 tokens after a 2,048-token prompt, 2 pairs | 37.6 | **38.2-41.1 (median 39.6)** | ΓÇö |

| decode, 256 tokens, `--spec 2` (no draft layer), 3 pairs | 53.4-53.9 (median 53.6) | **22.0-22.9 (median 22.3)** | 33.6 |

| prompt reading, 2,048 tokens | 8.0-14.5 tok/s | **71-73 tok/s** | 790-1,002 tok/s |

| `quantize_act_parity --selftest`, `sampler_parity` | byte-exact, 0 failures | byte-exact, 0 failures | ΓÇö |



**Two traps in measuring this backend, both worth passing on.** With a 2,048-token prompt the engine is not

run-to-run deterministic: the same binary diverges at token 60 and its state hash differs between two runs. And the

web app answers a `temperature: 0.0` request with its own Chat defaults (temperature 1.0, top_p 0.95), so a "greedy"

run through it is sampled. The kernel-level self-tests and the CLI's `--greedy` are the checks that hold.



**And short runs are not comparable on this backend.** The same build and mode gave 48.9 and

67.5 tok/s on two consecutive 128-token runs, and a 155-token answer through the API contradicted a 256-token run by

25%. My first pass at this table used those short runs and wrongly read as a ~25% regression; interleaved medians over

256 tokens are the numbers above.



**The one reproducible regression is `--spec 2`** ΓÇö 22.3 against 53.6 tok/s, interleaved, same card and flags. It is

the no-draft-layer path, so it is either the drafter-free window or the suffix drafter's cost; not attributed.



`STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1` puts 24 of a 65 ms 4-token window in the GDN hyper-connection read, nearly flat from T=2

(23.6 ms) to T=6 (25.6 ms): a per-layer *fixed* cost of ~0.5 ms over 48 layers ΓÇö kernel dispatch, not arithmetic.

`sycl-ls` lists only `opencl:gpu` here, so there is neither the Graph extension nor sysman's free-VRAM query.



## Two things a fresh Windows build needs, both found by building it clean



- **The DLLs to start at all.** `strata.exe` statically imports `libmmd.dll` (Intel's runtime, beside `icx`), and the

  UR adapters load `ur_loader.dll` / `ur_win_proxy_loader.dll` from beside the exe. Without those three staged the

  engine exits `0xC0000135` (STATUS_DLL_NOT_FOUND) before printing anything ΓÇö it only ran in my earlier build

  directory by accident. `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` now stages all three with the rest.

- **`sycl/tools/build.bat` finds `libircmt.lib` through the build dir's CMakeCache** when the shell has no `icx` on

  PATH, so the script works from a plain prompt; otherwise the link fails `LNK1104`.



## Three compile bugs in the port's own code



`<sycl/sycl.hpp>` reaches the Windows SDK, whose headers define `OUT` (minwindef.h), `small` (rpcndr.h) and `near`

(windef.h) as macros. An identifier with one of those names is macro-expanded away:



- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.dp.cpp`: `template <bool OUT>` loses its parameter, so every use becomes

  `error: expected expression`. Renamed `WRITE_OUT`.

- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: `const int64_t small` becomes `const int64_t char`; `memmem` is POSIX (now

  `std::search` over the same bytes).

- `sycl/src/kernels/sampler_parity.cpp`: `const bool near`.



## Without command graphs



`STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1` (set by `sycl/serve\strata-sycl.bat`) replays the window, the commit and the drafter's

chains on the queue instead of launching captured graphs:



- `record_commit()` is the commit graph's body; `capture_*()` record it where there is a graph backend.

- The `capture_round` / `capture_step` / `capture_prefill` bodies became `record_*()` functions the drafter

  replays. `prepare_chain()` refuses: its per-step events only exist inside a recorded graph.

- Eager replay **refuses a host-served expert plan** instead of running it ΓÇö the mid-record waits expire into stale

  plans, which is silently wrong rather than slow.

- oneMKL SYCL BLAS has no OpenCL Xe2 backend and the failed attempt poisons the queue, so the prompt GEMM is a

  plain SYCL kernel there - and the first version of that kernel read the whole weight matrix once **per row** (a

  2,048-row chunk of one 2,560 x 4,096 projection moved 86 GB of weights). `fallback_gemm_tiled` blocks a 64 x 64

  corner of Y per work-group and walks K in 16-wide tiles with the operands in local memory: **8.0-14.5 -> 71-73

  tok/s** on a 2,048-token prompt, decode unchanged. Same arithmetic - both kernels accumulate over k in ascending

  order with the fma spelled out - and `STRATA_FALLBACK_SELFTEST=1` runs both over a problem that crosses every tile

  edge and prints the bitwise difference: **0 of 4,189 values, largest 0**.

- `sampler_parity`'s fixture 18 skips its graph half without the extension instead of ending the process.



## Also



- Setup names the Intel Arc on Windows (display adapters + the display-class registry's 64-bit VRAM, which is the

  true VRAM ΓÇö WMI's `AdapterRAM` stops at 4 GB), and `--backend sycl` hands over to `sycl/setup_intel.py` there too.

- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: IntelLLVM / MSVC flag branches (`/fp:precise` is load-bearing ΓÇö `quantize_act_parity` goes

  from byte-exact to 303k mismatches without it), installer-free oneMKL, and the runtime DLLs staged beside

  `strata.exe`.

- `GgufExpertSource` reads at an offset through `OVERLAPPED` (there is no `pread` on Windows).

- The free-VRAM query needs Level Zero sysman, so setup writes `STRATA_DEVICE_FREE_MIB` / `_TOTAL_MIB` from the

  registry, and keeps them across a rewrite when detection flakes.



## The expert mirror on Windows (a model that does not fit in VRAM)

The mirror's default size came from `/proc/meminfo`, which does not exist here, so nothing was ever mirrored on
Windows: a model that does not fit entirely in VRAM refused to run ("6889 experts are neither in VRAM nor mirrored").
`GlobalMemoryStatusEx` is the same reading the process stats already take there, so with it IQ3_XXS runs on the B70
(17,687 of 24,576 experts in VRAM, the other 6,889 - 11.15 GiB - in pinned host memory the GPU reads over PCIe).

| | decode @2,048 | decode, short prompt | **prompt reading @2,048** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Coder IQ1_M, 23.42 GiB of experts, all resident | 43.6 tok/s | 76.4 tok/s | **74.7 tok/s** |
| IQ3_XXS, 39.97 GiB of experts, 72% resident | 30.0 tok/s | 19.2 tok/s | **1.03 tok/s** |

Decode absorbs the misses; the prompt does not, and not at the bandwidth bound (535 GiB over PCIe in 1,988 s is
~2% of the link). Reported with the profile that would settle it as
[#1549](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1549).

## The Monitor tab on this card

GPU load and VRAM come from the counters Windows keeps for every WDDM adapter - `GPU Engine` (per process, per engine,
summed per card as Task Manager does) and `GPU Adapter Memory` (dedicated bytes) - filtered to the LUID of the adapter
holding the most dedicated memory, so an iGPU beside the card does not add to the numbers. Measured through the API on
the B70: 2.9% idle, 100% while decoding, 30.01 of 32.00 GiB in use (the 23.4 GiB of experts, the KV and the driver's
own buffers), which agrees with the engine's own "12,288 of 12,288 experts resident".

Temperature, power and the PCIe link have no Windows counter at all, so those three tiles stay empty - now with the
dashboard saying why instead of showing a bare dash.

Two traps in that path, both found by measuring rather than reading, both in the commit message: PDH's wildcard API
answers `PDH_INVALID_ARGUMENT` on this machine for *every* path (core counters included), so instances come from
`Get-Counter -ListSet` and each gets its own counter; and a byte counter must be asked for as `PDH_FMT_LARGE`, because
with `PDH_FMT_DOUBLE` PDH fills the union with a double and 4.4 GB comes out as 4,437,051,947 GB.

## Limits



- Needs an admin account for VS Build Tools and the Intel driver; the conda + VS + PyPI/NuGet oneMKL pieces install

  per-user.

- A model whose experts do not all fit needs a RAM mirror (`STRATA_MIRROR_MIB`) or all-resident sizing; IQ3_XXS

  (17,687/24,576 experts resident here) stalls without one.

- Windows-SDK macro names have to be avoided as identifiers in the port.

`tools/test_setup_choices.py` ΓÇö 87 pass, no GPU and no network.

title: Model writing a literal </think> emits the special token: quoted tag ends the reasoning mid-sentence and the turn stops (finish_reason=stop)
body:
Follow-up on the output side of #537. On 0.1.41 (Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 2×3090), a long agent session about parsing </think> had 4 turns in a row cut after 100–200 tokens with finish_reason: stop, right after a backtick in the reasoning.
What I changed in serve/ (patch attached):
Only the model's own end-of-thinking token closes the thinking. Service.run() now tells the parser when it is that token, so a </think> the model writes with ordinary text tokens stays reasoning text.A special <think>/</think> token that can't be a real marker is swapped for the tag's text tokens, and generation continues. That covers the answer, and quoted or mid-line tags in the thinking. It reuses the #123 continuation path.If the model stops right after opening an inline code span in its thinking, the tag is written as text and generation continues.
It's capped at 64 swaps per reply, behind a literal_think_guard flag (on by default), with 12 new tests.
What worked for me: asking the model to write the tag, repeating answer: 42</think> and a tool result containing the tag now all give full reasoning and a correct answer. A prompt that returned no answer 2/6 times returned 0/3. Decode speed is unchanged (120.3 vs 120.4 tok/s).

title: [Feature]: resident RAM mode — let the RAM copy follow the conversation when it cannot hold every expert (opt-in, PR #1838)
body:
### What do you want to do?

Make decode faster on a PC whose RAM cannot hold every expert the GPU does not.

In the resident RAM mode the RAM copy is chosen once, at start, from the expert profile. The adaptive tier then moves
experts between RAM and VRAM, but nothing moves between the file and RAM. So an expert outside the copy is read from the
SSD every time the conversation routes to it - even one routed to in every window - while RAM places are held by experts
the conversation never uses.

**Proposal:** let the RAM copy follow the conversation as the VRAM tier does (opt-in, `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=<n>`). The
implementation, a unit test and all the measurements are in **#1838**.

RTX 3060 12 GB, 32 GB of RAM, Linux, IQ2_XS (about 6,000 of the 24,576 experts on the file tier), against v0.1.41;
decode tok/s, median of three fresh-process runs per arm:

| adaptive tier | verify window | v0.1.41 | `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | |
|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `--adapt-async 1` | `--spec 3` | 35.22 | 41.01 | **+16.4%** |
| blocking | `--spec 3` | 31.42 | 35.69 | **+13.6%** |
| `--adapt-async 1` | `--spec 2` | 32.63 | 38.28 | **+17.3%** |
| blocking | `--spec 2` | 28.13 | 31.49 | **+11.9%** |

Prompt speed does not change (463-465 tok/s without, 464-468 with).

The four prompts of a run are in four languages, one after another. Decode tok/s per prompt (`--adapt-async 1`,
`--spec 3`, mean of the three runs):

| | English | Japanese | Chinese | German |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| v0.1.41 | 40.7 | 36.0 | 34.5 | 31.5 |
| `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | 42.2 | 38.6 | 42.1 | 41.5 |

**How:** before a decode window, while no adaptive round is in flight, a file-tier expert the windows keep routing to
(the adaptive tier's own decayed count, 2 or more) takes the RAM place of an expert of its own layer that is not routed
to (count below 0.5); at most `n` per window. The RAM stays the same size; the routing, the weights and the VRAM tier's
rule are untouched, and nothing runs when the variable is unset (checked: same answer hash as v0.1.41).

**Related:** #1324 (`--resident-lru-gib`) answers the same observation with a separate LRU pool inside the RAM budget.
Built and measured on this machine with the same workload and total RAM, its branch gives +7% / +10% / +12% decode with
a 1 / 2 / 4 GiB LRU against its own baseline; the numbers are in #1838.

**Not tested:** HIP, SYCL, Windows, a layer split, a peer or helper GPU, `--batch` (the code does nothing in those
cases), other quantizations, and RAM sizes other than 32 GB. `docs/TEST_REQUESTS.md` asks for results from a Linux host
with 32 GB of RAM or less; this is one.

title: serve: a reply that ends inside its thinking with no answer is continued (#1814)
body:
Fixes #1814. I reproduced it on an RTX 3090 with Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_XXS on 0.1.41 and dumped the raw turns with `STRATA_DEBUG=1`.

## What I see

The model is about to write its closing thinking tag and the **turn-end token comes instead**:

```
[strata] raw: 'We need to respond to user: "In a markdown code fence, show exactly how the closing
thinking tag looks ... inside prose."\n\nNeed likely show closing thinking tag: <|im_end|>'
```

`finish_reason` is `stop`, the reasoning stops mid-sentence, no answer is produced, and the client gets an empty reply.

My trigger runs (temperature 0, production config: 250K context, `--kv int8`, MTP speculative decoding):

| runs | empty replies |
| --- | --- |
| first set, 9 runs (streaming and whole, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE` on and off) | 6 of 9 |
| same prompts, later run, 5 runs | 3 of 5 |
| same prompts again, later run, 6 runs | 0 of 6 |

So it is not deterministic: the same prompt can answer normally on one pass and end with nothing on the next. The prompt has to make the model reach for its closing tag (asking it to show/parse/quote the tag), and the cut lands right where the tag would start, or right after a backtick - which matches what danirebollo describes in the issue.

Five real turns are in `serve/fixtures/literal_think_specimens.json`. Each carries a `kind`: `no-answer` is this bug, `answered` reached its answer, `length-cut` ended on max_tokens instead.

## Why the parser cannot catch it

In this model's tokenizer the tag is not a special token: it is eight ordinary text tokens (`<`, `/`, `t`, `h`, `i`, `n`, `k`, `>`), and the stop token that ends the turn is the ordinary end-of-turn token. A turn that ends inside its thinking therefore looks exactly like a turn that ended inside its thinking - there is nothing in the stream that says "I meant that". That is also why #537's mark/unmark work (the input side) does not cover it.

## The fix

`Service.run()`: when the turn ends with `finish_reason == "stop"` inside the thinking with no answer, the reply is continued with the thinking closed, the way #123's wrap-up closes it (`REASONING_CLOSE`). The next pass's prompt is the one that produced this reply plus what it generated plus that close, so the engine continues from the prefix it already holds and the model answers. `parser.state == "content"` is the same end seen from the other side - the model wrote the tag as text, the parser took it as the marker and nothing followed - and there the tag goes back into the reasoning text first (`OutputParser.reopen_reasoning()`).

This is #1053's continuation, so it is opt-in in the same way:

* `"literal_think_guard": true` in `strata-<model>.json`, or `STRATA_LITERAL_THINK_GUARD=1`
* capped per reply (`LITERAL_THINK_RETRIES = 2`), so a model that keeps doing it cannot loop
* a counter in the request status/trace (`literal_think_retries`) and one log line per continuation

I left it opt-in rather than on by default because #1053 is opt-in and this changes what a reply contains (the close is appended to the prompt), so it should be the same deliberate choice. It works with `reasoning_close_retry` on or off: whichever fires first sets `close_retried`.

## Tests

`serve/test_literal_think_guard.py` replays the five real turns through a mock engine: every `no-answer` specimen gets the answer with exactly one continuation, an `answered` specimen and a `length-cut` specimen are not touched, the guard is off by default, and the cap holds (1 + `LITERAL_THINK_RETRIES` passes at most, with both continuations visible in the log).

`python -m unittest discover -s serve -t . -p "test_*.py"` -> 604 tests, 11 skipped. The only failure I see is `test_responses.py`'s telemetry `(_loop)` thread count, which is flaky here and unrelated: it fails on this checkout without my change too (OK, FAILED, FAILED across three runs of that module alone).

I have it running on this machine (one 3090, IQ3_XXS, the same config the issue reports) with the flag on.

title: fix(serve): preserve literal closing thinking tags
body:
Follow-up to #537 and related to #1814. When ordinary text tokens spell `</think>` during reasoning, the parser must keep those bytes as reasoning text; only the tokenizer's dedicated end-of-thinking token should close the block. This change makes parser transitions depend on token identity.

The bounded `literal_think_guard` handles dedicated `<think>` / `</think>` tokens in answer text or inside reasoning code spans by rendering the tag with ordinary text-token IDs and resuming from the preserved prefix. If end-of-turn arrives inside an unclosed reasoning code span before any answer or tool call, it similarly inserts literal `</think>` text and resumes. The guard is enabled by default to match #1814 and can be disabled with `"literal_think_guard": false`. It is capped at 64 repairs per reply, respects client stops, and accounts for inserted tokens against the output budget.

### Evidence

- Controlled ordinary-text tag case: the original parser misrouted the tag in 12/12 requests; token-identity parsing handled all 12 with the same generated token IDs.
- A live RTX PRO 6000 run naturally emitted dedicated closing-tag IDs inside reasoning code. The guard replaced them and continued from the verified prefix, but those replies reached their output cap while still reasoning; this verifies repair mechanics, not complete answers.
- A Linux stress test with 4,106- and 8,370-token parser/tool histories produced one baseline stop after an opening backtick in 8 requests. No dedicated closing-tag ID appeared in any of 16 baseline/guard requests. Its synthetic history included the expected symptom, so it is not an independent reproduction of the reporter's agent session.
- We could not test the reported two RTX 3090 GPUs, and the exact dedicated-token-then-stop sequence remains unobserved.

### Validation

- Focused parser/service/HTTP tests: 30 passed on Windows and Linux.
- Full Windows serving suite: 623 passed, 10 skipped (438.513s).
- Full Linux serving suite from a native WSL filesystem with `regex` and `jsonschema` available: 623 passed, 12 skipped (339.043s).

Related but separate work: [#1818](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1818) covers CPU IQ expert dispatch and draft-grouping independence; [#1813](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1813) covers speculative/TCP parity; [#1773](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1773) covers Q8 TCP parity/timings.

title: Resident RAM mode: the RAM copy follows the conversation (`STRATA_RAM_ADAPT`, opt-in)
body:
## Title Issue: Resolves #1837 ## Summary In the resident RAM mode the RAM copy is chosen once, at start. On a PC whose RAM cannot hold every expert the GPU does not, an expert outside the copy is read from the SSD every time the conversation routes to it - even one routed to in every window - because the adaptive tier only moves experts between RAM and VRAM. `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=` (opt-in) lets the RAM copy follow the conversation as the VRAM tier does. RTX 3060 12 GB, 32 GB of RAM, IQ2_XS, against v0.1.41; decode tok/s, median of three fresh-process runs per arm: | adaptive tier | verify window | v0.1.41 | `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | | |---|---|---:|---:|---:| | `--adapt-async 1` | `--spec 3` | 35.22 | 41.01 | **+16.4%** | | blocking | `--spec 3` | 31.42 | 35.69 | **+13.6%** | | `--adapt-async 1` | `--spec 2` | 32.63 | 38.28 | **+17.3%** | | blocking | `--spec 2` | 28.13 | 31.49 | **+11.9%** | Prompt speed does not change (463-465 tok/s without, 464-468 with). Blob reads from the file fall from 67K-76K to 26K-35K per run. What it does, seen request by request: the four prompts of a run are in four languages, one after another. Decode tok/s (`--adapt-async 1`, `--spec 3`, mean of the three runs): | | English | Japanese | Chinese | German | |---|---:|---:|---:|---:| | v0.1.41 | 40.7 | 36.0 | 34.5 | 31.5 | | `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | 42.2 | 38.6 | 42.1 | 41.5 | **How it works** 1. **When:** before a decode window, while no adaptive round is in flight (not in a request's first window). 2. **What it reads:** the adaptive tier's own decayed routing counts. Nothing new is counted. 3. **The choice:** per layer, the file-tier expert with the highest count (2 or more, the tier's candidate floor) and the RAM expert with the lowest (below 0.5). The pairs with the largest difference first, at most `n` per window. 4. **The move:** the incoming blob is read from the file beside the copy, then written into the outgoing expert's place. Experts of one layer have one size, so the RAM stays the same size. The outgoing expert is on the file tier again and can come back the same way. The routing, the weights and what the VRAM tier swaps are untouched. **Checked** - **Off = main.** With the variable unset: the same 4,487-token prompt, 256 new tokens, greedy, the blocking tier, `STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1`, a fresh engine each time, v0.1.41 / this PR / v0.1.41 / this PR - four answers, one SHA-256. - **Unit test** (`file_expert_source_test --rotation-gpu`, pinned and pageable): the moved-in bytes are the file's, the moved-out expert is read from the file again, a refused call changes nothing, and an exchange with the VRAM tier still works after a move. - **Soak:** 61 minutes back to back with the option on - 140 requests, none failed, 22,065 experts moved, decode 45.1-46.4 tok/s by ten-minute slice, engine RSS 23.65 -> 23.68 GiB, no error line. - **All 24 runs of the table:** 96 requests, none failed. ## What changed - `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`, `src/core/expert_source.cpp`: `FileExpertSource::replace_resident(layer, in, out)`. It refuses when `out` is not in the copy, `in` already is, an exchange is staged, either has an exchange override, or `STRATA_EXCHANGE_ROTATE` is active; a failed read leaves the copy as it was. `ram_adapts()` counts the moves. - `src/program/generate.cpp`: the choice above, in the serial `--serve` decode loop before `adapt_tick`, and one line in the per-request stats once an expert has moved. It does nothing with a layer split, a peer GPU, a helper cache or batch slots. - `tests/core/file_expert_source_test.cpp`: `test_replace_resident`. - `docs/DETAILS.md`: the option, beside `--adapt-async`. Left alone: the routing, the weights, the VRAM tier's rule, the expert profile and `--expert-profile-save`, the prompt path (its routing is not counted, so a prompt reads what it read before), every default. ## Extra Notes **Not tested / limits** - Built and run on CUDA and Linux only. Not built: HIP, SYCL, Windows - the changed files are the backends' common code, but I have no machine to build them on. - One machine, one quantization. With every expert in RAM or VRAM there is no file-tier candidate, so nothing moves. - The two thresholds (2 and 0.5) were not tuned; `n` = 8 and 32 measured the same on my own workload. - Each move is a blocking read of one blob (about 0.4 ms here) on the decode thread, at most `n` per window. - `--pipeline-windows 2` runs another loop, which this PR does not touch. - Answers were not graded. The moved bytes are the file's.
Machine and settings RTX 3060 12 GB connected over OCuLink (PCIe 4.0 x4, 170 W limit); Ryzen 7 7840HS engineering sample (8 cores / 16 threads, reported as `AMD Eng Sample: 100-000000964-50_Y`, 3.5 GHz maximum); 32 GB LPDDR5-6400; Samsung PM981 512 GB NVMe (MZVLB512HAJQ, PCIe 3.0 x4). Ubuntu 26.04, kernel 7.0, on the power-saver profile (`amd-pstate-epp`, `powersave` governor, EPP `power`) for every run of both arms; driver 615.78, CUDA 13.4, source build (`STRATA_NATIVE_EXPERTS`, `STRATA_MMQ_KQUANTS`, sm_86). Model: ISTA-DASLab Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS (revision ed59f92), the repository's `data/expert-profile.bin`, no learned profile. 20.5 GiB of experts in RAM, 3,970 expert slots in VRAM, about 6,000 experts on the file tier. Both arms: `--expert-cache 4200 --resident-budget-gib 20.5 --mmap-experts --kv k8v4 --max-context 131072 --prefill auto:16384 --pool-workers 7 --ple-io direct --greedy --vision --prompt-cache 2 --conversation-cache-mib 1536 --conversation-cache-slots 3`, `STRATA_UNBUFFERED_LOAD=1`, `STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=8`, `STRATA_LOOKAHEAD=1`, `STRATA_PREFILL_CPU_SHARE=auto`, and the adaptive tier and verify window of the table's row (`--spec 3` is `--spec 3 --mtp-max-t 3 --spec-min-p 0.5`; `--spec 2` is `--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 2`). The timing variables `STRATA_PREFILL_TIMING`, `STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE` and `STRATA_DECODE_TIMING` were set in both arms. The only difference between the arms is the binary and `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8`.
Workload and every run A small script (not in this PR; I can add it under `bench/results/` or post it here if wanted): four prompts cut from this repository (`docs/DETAILS.md`, `README.ja.md`, `README.zh-CN.md`, `README.de.md`, 12,000 characters each, 4.2K-4.5K tokens), each with a unique first line so nothing is reused, 768 new tokens, greedy, reasoning off. Requests go through a local OpenAI-compatible server in front of the engine, the same one for both arms. Speeds are the engine's own `strata serve: prompt ...` lines. A run is a freshly started engine; the arms were interleaved (main, on, main, on, main, on). Decode tok/s, each run, then the median: | adaptive tier | verify window | v0.1.41 (`fb58e0d`) | this PR, `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | |---|---|---|---| | `--adapt-async 1` | `--spec 3` | 35.74 / 35.20 / 35.22 (35.22) | 40.70 / 41.42 / 41.01 (41.01) | | blocking | `--spec 3` | 30.97 / 31.42 / 31.42 (31.42) | 35.69 / 35.82 / 35.60 (35.69) | | `--adapt-async 1` | `--spec 2` | 32.63 / 32.47 / 32.66 (32.63) | 37.97 / 38.28 / 38.47 (38.28) | | blocking | `--spec 2` | 28.17 / 28.13 / 28.00 (28.13) | 31.77 / 31.49 / 31.32 (31.49) | The first row in full: | | run 1 | run 2 | run 3 | |---|---:|---:|---:| | v0.1.41, prompt tok/s | 465.1 | 462.9 | 462.4 | | this PR, prompt tok/s | 467.4 | 468.6 | 466.3 | | v0.1.41, blob reads from the file | 66,896 | 68,110 | 69,088 | | this PR, blob reads from the file | 35,066 | 31,554 | 32,354 | | this PR, experts moved into RAM | 2,203 | 2,147 | 2,175 | A second workload, 47 recorded requests of my own Open WebUI use (Korean, tool calls, 6.5K-27K-token prompts; not attached, they are private): v0.1.41 35.2 and 35.2 tok/s, this PR with the option off 35.5, on 43.2; one run each. The soak's prompts repeat, so the RAM copy settles on them: it shows stability, not a speed to expect.
Related: #1324 (--resident-lru-gib), measured on the same machine #1324 starts from the same observation - the RAM copy is filled once from the profile, so a conversation keeps reading experts that are cold in the profile and hot for it - and answers it with a separate LRU pool inside the RAM budget. This PR changes which experts the existing copy holds instead: no second pool and no size to choose. I built #1324's branch (`4b28dc1`, on 0.1.40.2) here and ran the same workload with the same total RAM (20.5 GiB), three fresh-process runs per arm, the LRU off and on in that one binary: | | decode tok/s (median) | | prompt tok/s | |---|---|---:|---| | #1324 branch, no LRU | 35.53 / 34.86 / 35.50 (35.50) | | 465-466 | | #1324, 19.5 GiB + 1 GiB LRU | 37.96 / 38.18 / 37.97 (37.97) | +7.0% | 465 | | #1324, 18.5 GiB + 2 GiB LRU | 39.16 / 38.94 / 39.84 (39.16) | +10.3% | 472-473 | | #1324, 16.5 GiB + 4 GiB LRU | 40.01 / 39.85 / 39.85 (39.85) | +12.3% | 480-482 | | this PR (on 0.1.41), `STRATA_RAM_ADAPT=8` | 40.70 / 41.42 / 41.01 (41.01) | +16.4% over 35.22 | 466-469 | Both work on a 32 GB Linux machine. The two baselines are different releases (35.50 and 35.22 tok/s), so compare the gains, not the last digit: here this PR is a little ahead on decode without a size to pick, and #1324 at 4 GiB reads prompts about 3% faster (its prompt path copies from the LRU). I did not try the two together, #1324's elastic watcher, or other LRU sizes.

title: V100 (sm_70): prompt experts on FP16 tensor cores (+10% prompt) and three existing decode kernels as defaults (-6.8% GPU per window)
body:
## Title
V100 (sm_70): prompt experts on FP16 tensor cores (+10% prompt speed) and three existing decode kernels as Volta's defaults (-6.8% GPU work per window)

## Summary
Two parts, both picked only on sm_70 (every other card runs what it ran), each with a switch back to the old path.

**Prompt (+9.6% / +10.3%).** MMQ's integer products are `dp4a` on Volta. `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` runs an MMQ expert group per launch on the FP16 tensor cores (WMMA, FP32 sums): each weight superblock dequantized once into shared memory with `dq_dispatch` (the FP16 path's formulas), FP16 activations streamed through, the next tile prefetched. It also takes the IQ1_M layers through MMQ's grouping (they were on the per-expert FP16 path). V100-SXM2, setup's IQ2_XS and config, 3 alternating rounds: 26,359-token prompt 1,467 -> 1,608 tok/s, 6,345-token prompt 1,390 -> 1,534 tok/s (rounds within 1%). `STRATA_PF_WMMA=0`: MMQ.

**Decode (bitwise).** Three kernels Strata already has for other cards: gfx906's expert mode 8 for the routed experts in VRAM, `native_mmvq_il` with a Volta rows table, gfx906's latency-hidden hyper-connection up. GPU work per verify window 22.80 -> 21.24 ms (engine stage table, 3 rounds); decode tok/s +3-11% against the same-binary control on this rig, whose CPU pool makes decode noisy. `STRATA_EXP_MODE=0`, `STRATA_MMVQ_IL=0`, `STRATA_GR_FAST=0`.

Numbers, method, raw data: `bench/results/2026-10-07-v100-prompt-experts/` and `bench/results/2026-10-07-v100-decode-kernels/`.

## What changed
- `src/kernels/cuda/iq_kernels.cu`: `gemm_iq_f16_grouped` (CUDA; a stub on HIP); the AMD grouped-expert layouts (`STRATA_EXP_MODE`) build for CUDA, sm_70 defaults to mode 8, IQ2_XXS gate/up joins the shared-memory kernels on CUDA, a strided call (the window's PCIe call) and a format without an LDS kernel keep the CUDA layout. gfx906 unchanged.
- `src/prefill/prefill.cpp`: `pf_wmma()` (sm_70 default), IQ1_M layers in MMQ's grouping for it, the FP16 activation gather instead of the q8_1 quantization on those layers, the group's two tile launches + an FP16 SwiGLU (`src/prefill/kernels.cu: swiglu_split_f16`).
- `src/kernels/cuda/native_mmvq.cu`: the interleaved 2-4 column kernel on sm_70 with its own rows table (read off `mmvq_il_parity --bench` on the V100 by the existing table's rule).
- `src/kernels/cuda/fused_gr.cu`: gfx906's fast norm/up build for CUDA, default on sm_70; `gr_up_fast_kernel` now writes the QFUSE q8_1 tail like `gr_up_multi_kernel` (this also fixes gfx906 with `STRATA_QFUSE=1`).
- Tests/tools/docs: `src/kernels/pf_wmma_parity.cpp` (+ ctest), `tools/ab_engine.py`, `docs/NVIDIA_V100.md`, the two bench result folders.

## Extra Notes
- Prompt accuracy: `pf_wmma_parity` against a double reference over the same FP16 weights: max error ~5e-6 of the output scale. Teacher-forced (`STRATA_LOGPOS`, a continuation after a 26K / 12.6K prompt): against MMQ, KL 0.0083 (prose) and 0.031 (code) - the same size as MMQ against itself with another chunk size (0.0084-0.0177 prose, 0.025 code). MMQ is not a reference (q8_1 activations); a full-precision reference run was not made.
- Decode changes are bitwise the kernels they replace (`native_expert_bench` on all 48 layers, `native_grouped_parity`, `mmvq_il_parity`, `mmvq_multi_parity`, `fused_gr_bench`, `gr_multi_parity`, `gr_parity`).
- Full `ctest` on the V100: all pass except 3 that fail on this rig only (no AVX512-VNNI, `mlock` in a container, the Q2_0 shard `ple_parity` wants); `prefill_fused_*` skip below sm_80.
- Not measured: a PCIe V100, other packs (Q2_0 / IQ3_S / UD-IQ4_XS take the same code; the prompt kernel needs a Q2_0 down product, so UD-IQ4_XS's IQ4_NL down keeps MMQ), HIP builds (unchanged by construction, not built here).
- The history has one change reverted in place (the FP16 path for 16K+ chunks, superseded by the tensor-core kernel); squash-merge reads cleanest.
- Pointed at by 1Cat-vLLM's SM70 GGUF kernels (shared-memory lattice codebooks, tensor-core expert GEMMs); no code was taken from it.

title: serve: a Chinese / English language switch for the web app (adapted to v0.1.41)
body:
Adapted to **Strata v0.1.41**: the dictionary and the rules are current for the web interface of 0.1.41 (re-checked against every `app.js` change since this branch's base — see Coverage), and the branch is rebased onto today's `main` (`fb58e0d`, the v0.1.41 release). The branch is a single commit.

*(History: this supersedes #682, which GitHub closed automatically when the history was rewritten, and #1204, which was closed when its fork was deleted and re-created — same commit, same content, nothing changed but the PR number.)*

## What this adds

An optional **Chinese / English language switch** for the web app, with a `Language` button at the left of the header: **English / Simplified Chinese / Chinese + English**.

It is opt-in and reversible: the stock interface is what you get until someone picks another language.

## Coverage: the whole 0.1.41 web interface is translated

Not a partial pass — every user-facing string in the two pages of this release, including the views added in 0.1.40 and the two strings 0.1.40.2 added:

- the header, the three tabs and the status pill;
- **Chat**: the empty state, the composer and its buttons, the toasts, the attachments, the tool-call blocks, the per-message meta line, the export and copy labels;
- **Monitor**: the state badges, the eight metric cards, the context gauge, the request table (headers, status badges, `+N% PCIe`), the totals line, and the new **Conversation cache** panel — its bars, its four facts rows and both of its notes;
- **About**: the model/engine facts, the hardware facts, the API addresses, the settings — and the sentence the page composes from the engine's `cvec` value, the experimental speed projection's line (`Projection control vector on layers 4–44. Per chat in Sampling. …` → 在第 4～44 层上投影控制向量。…), which a rule matches because the mode (project / additive) and the layer numbers come from the engine at run time;
- the **sampling drawer**: thinking levels, temperature, Top-p, Top-k, Max tokens, Seed, the three switches;
- the new **Model settings** view: the help sentence of all 15 editable keys (those sentences come from `runconfig.py` and are matched as data), *and* the two pieces of the form that are not sentences — the `<option>` text of its dropdowns (`default` / `on` / `off` render as 默认 / 开 / 关; an enum choice keeps its config word with the meaning beside it: `model（按模型习惯）`, `start（开头）` …) and the monospace config key beside each field, which keeps the key untouched and gets a short gloss after it (`sampling.top_p（核采样范围）`, `reasoning_budget_tokens（思考长度上限）` …). The key names and the `value` attributes are never rewritten, so what a save writes to the run config stays exactly the English keys the server expects;
- and the strings only a screen reader or a hover would show: every `title`, `placeholder` and `aria-label`.

How that was verified: every string literal and text node was extracted from `index.html`, `monitor.html`, `app.js`, `monitor.js` and the `EDITABLE` list in `runconfig.py` (~264 candidates), then compared against the dictionary and the rules, with HTML line-wrapping normalised; every `<option>` label the settings form can render is checked against the option and general tables, and the short enum words are asserted *absent* from the general dictionary. For every later release the diff of `serve/web/` was re-checked the same way: 0.1.40.2 added exactly two strings (`not available`, `not available on Windows AMD yet` — the GPU-fact placeholders shown on Windows AMD), both now in the dictionary, and **0.1.40.3 and 0.1.41 changed nothing in `serve/web/` at all**, so the coverage above carries over unchanged. The projection sentence the About page composes from the engine's `cvec` (`Projection control vector on layers 4–44. …`) is covered by a rule. The remaining unlisted items are CSS class names, code fragments, Python docstrings and proper nouns (e.g. `Top-p`, `Strata`, `Tok/s`) — nothing a user reads.

A new string added upstream later shows up untranslated rather than breaking anything, so this list only ever grows.

## Files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `serve/web/i18n-zh.js` | new, self-contained |
| `serve/web/index.html` | one `<script>` tag |
| `serve/web/monitor.html` | one `<script>` tag |

No existing function is modified, there is no new dependency, no server-side change and no API change (`/health`, `/v1/...` are untouched — only the two HTML pages load the new file). Removing the feature is deleting one line per page.

## How it works

- A dictionary covers the fixed labels; a list of regex rules covers the strings the app builds at run time (token counts, `tok/s`, the request table, the `Since …` totals line, the conversation-cache statistics, the composed per-message meta line, the projection sentence built from the engine's `cvec`, and so on).
- A `MutationObserver` re-translates after the app re-renders, so the live Monitor — the status pill included — keeps updating in the chosen language, and it does so before the next paint, so nothing flickers back to English. Every write is guarded (`if (el.textContent !== next)`), which makes the observer converge: a second `translateAll()` over the same page performs zero DOM writes (asserted in a test), so it can never feed itself into a loop.
- The Chinese and the English text both live in the DOM; a `data-lang` attribute on `<html>` plus CSS decides which one is shown. Switching is instant and does not re-run the translation.
- The button's own label and menu follow the chosen language (`Language` / `语言` / `语言 Language`), and the choice is kept in `localStorage` (`strata.lang`).

## Guarantees

- **The model's output is never rewritten.** Chat text, reasoning, code blocks and MCP tool arguments and results are explicitly excluded. Checked by asking the model for an English answer and confirming the bubble, the reasoning and the code read exactly as the model produced them in every language mode.
- **`English` restores the stock interface**, attributes included: every translated `title`, `placeholder` and `aria-label` keeps its original value in a `data-i18n-orig-*` attribute, and every `<option>` and `<code>` key its original text in `data-i18n-orig-text`.
- Text with no dictionary entry or rule is left alone, so a partial translation never breaks the page.

## Tested

On Windows 11, engine 0.1.40.3 and 0.1.41, in a real browser against a running server (a headless Edge dump of the live DOM — not a mock — plus the interactive page), on Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ2_XS and IQ3_XXS: all three modes on the Chat, Monitor and About tabs, in the sampling drawer and in the Model settings view; switching back and forth without a reload; reloading to confirm the stored choice comes back; the composed projection sentence on the About page; and the model-output check above.

## Notes

- The dictionary is deliberately data rather than code: another language is another table, and the rules are shared.
- Happy to rework any of it — a different button position, the dictionary split into its own file, a different default — if you would rather have it another way.

title: Chinese output collapses into a token loop after a few hundred tokens
body:
# IQ3_S (unpruned): Chinese output collapses into a token loop after a few hundred tokens; English unaffected — deterministic, 5/5 on greedy

## Summary

Long Chinese answers degrade into a repeated-token collapse partway through generation. The same
model and engine produce clean English at nearly 2x the length. It is fully deterministic on greedy
(5/5 byte-identical outputs), it is not a reasoning loop, and sampling penalties do not help.

The collapse is always in the same semantic cluster — the model gets stuck emitting `颊` and its
English glosses (`cheek`, `blush`, `face`, `扑`) interleaved, after producing several hundred
otherwise-correct tokens.

This is the symptom of #438, but on an **unpruned** IQ3_S pack, so the pruning explanation from that
issue does not apply here.

## Environment

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Model | `ISTA-DASLab/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`, **IQ3_S**, the original unpruned files |
| Strata | 0.1.41 (`setup.sh` @ `d311345`), engine `BUILD.json`: `{"source":"local","version":"0.1.41","archs":[89],"src":"62eb4907c92a8cb7"}` |
| Engine build | compiled from source, nvcc **13.3.73**, GNU 13.3.0, `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=89` (no Linux prebuilt exists for any release, so this is the normal path) |
| GPUs | 2× RTX 4090 **48 GB** (modded), driver 595.99.02, layer split `auto` |
| GPU links | CUDA0 **PCIe 4.0 x4** — engine probe `6.1 GB/s -> miss cost x3.27`; CUDA1 PCIe 4.0 x16 — `25.7 GB/s -> x1.00` |
| CPU / RAM | Ryzen 7 3800XT (AVX2, no AVX-512), **61 GB** RAM |
| OS | Ubuntu 26.04 (glibc 2.43), Python 3.14.4 |
| Storage | NVMe SSD for both the pack and the GGUFs |
| Server args | `--pack packs/iq3_s --native …-00001-of-00002.gguf --ple-gguf …-00002-of-00002.gguf --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp mtp/rt --max-context 131072 --kv int8 --resident-experts` |
| Config keys added | `"reasoning_loop_recovery": "recover"`, `"reasoning_budget_tokens": 8192` (see "Guards" below) |

Experts are **fully resident**: the engine log reports
`resident RAM: 0.00 GiB of experts in RAM, 0 exchanged with the VRAM tier, 0 blob reads from the file`
and start-up filled `12288 experts, 22.14 GiB of VRAM` per card (48 MoE layers × 512 experts = 24,576 total,
12,288 per card). So there are no expert file reads and no VRAM/RAM swaps during these runs.

## Symptom

Prompt `你是谁，详细介绍一下`, default sampling (greedy), `max_tokens: 4096`. `finish_reason` is
`stop` — the model ends the turn itself, it is not truncated.

The first ~400 tokens are correct and well formed. The tail of the same answer:

```
… 如果你在学习某个概念，我可以把它讲 face-to-face 颊 cheek颊颊扑 cheek颊颊 cheek face-to-face face-to-face
```

Reasoning for the same request is short (124 characters) and clean.

## Reproduction

```bash
curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8080/v1/chat/completions \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"strata","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"你是谁，详细介绍一下"}],"max_tokens":4096}'
```

Run 5 times back to back: **5/5 byte-identical**, 474 completion tokens, `finish_reason=stop`, same
collapsed tail.

## Measured matrix

`重复度` below is `1 - unique/total` over character 8-grams of the answer (0 = no repetition).

| Case | tokens | `finish_reason` | result | tail |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Chinese, defaults | 474 | `stop` | **collapsed** | `…讲 face-to-face 颊 cheek颊颊扑 cheek颊颊 cheek face-to-face face-to-face` |
| Chinese, `max_tokens: 200` | 200 | `length` | **clean** | `…- 日常问答 - 知识解释 - 写作与润色 - 翻译` (truncated before the collapse point) |
| Chinese, `temperature: 0.8, seed: 7` | 1084 | `stop` | **collapsed** | `…整颊颊颊颊颊横扑颊 face cheeky  face cheecky cheeks cheeks cheeks.` |
| Chinese, `reasoning_effort: "none"` | 685 | `stop` | **collapsed, worse** | `…颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊颊…` (60+ consecutive `颊`) |
| **English** control — `Who are you? Please introduce yourself in detail.` | **1885** | `stop` | **clean** | `… can be a thoughtful, flexible, and capable assistant when used carefully and effectively.` |
| Chinese, other topic — `介绍一下杭州的历史和文化` | 1436 | `length` | **collapsed** | `… cheek cheek cheek cheek cheek cheek cheek …` |

Two things follow from this table:

* **It is language-specific.** English is clean at 1,885 tokens; Chinese collapses at 429–1,436 tokens
  in every case tried. A general numerical fault (NaN, a miscompiled kernel) would hit English too.
* **It is not a reasoning loop.** Turning reasoning *off* makes it worse (60+ consecutive `颊`), and the
  collapse is in the answer body.

## Sampling penalties do not help

Same prompt, same session:

| Sampling | tokens | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| baseline | 474 | collapsed |
| `repetition_penalty: 1.05` | 801 | collapsed — `face face face … face颊 cheek` |
| `repetition_penalty: 1.10` | 429 | collapsed — `把复杂概念讲 face颊红脸上的 cheek blush 扑 cheek blush cheek blush` |
| `repetition_penalty: 1.1` + `frequency_penalty: 0.3` | 319 | collapsed — `颊 cheek颊 cheek颊 cheek颊 … cheeks cheeks cheeks` |

The penalties change the *shape* of the collapse, not its occurrence.

## Existing guards do not fire, and why

* `repeat_stop_tokens` (default 256) — the run of `颊` is only ~60 long and is interleaved with Latin
  tokens (`cheek`, `face`), so the single-token run counter never reaches 256.
* `reasoning_loop_recovery: "recover"` and `reasoning_budget_tokens: 8192` — both were set in
  `strata-iq3_s.json` for these tests and neither applies: the guard watches the **reasoning** span,
  while the collapse is in the answer, and the reasoning here is only 124 characters.

So at present nothing in the server bounds this failure mode: `finish_reason` is `stop`, so a client
cannot even tell the answer is corrupt.

## What I ruled out

* **#438 (CJK wrong at IQ1_M, Coder)** — the official explanation was expert pruning, with the fix
  being "use the unpruned sizes (Q2_0, IQ2_XS, IQ3_S)". This pack *is* the unpruned original
  (`IQ3_S/`, both shards, sizes verified against the repo), and the symptom reproduces anyway. The
  collapse signature (`我是通（通通通通通…`) is also the same family as ours.
* **#137 (draft_vocab has almost no CJK)** — checked the shipped file: `data/draft_vocab.bin` is
  425,196 bytes, which matches the 106,299-id post-fix size, not the 40,525-id broken one. Also MTP
  acceptance on Chinese in these runs is 0.76–0.86, not the 0.22 of #137.
* **#879 (all-logits-NaN) / #892 (CUDA miscompile)** — both are described as making *every* answer
  wrong. Here English is clean at 1,885 tokens and the Chinese answers are correct for the first few
  hundred tokens, so the logits are not globally broken.

## Variables I am disclosing about this setup

I do not know whether any of these matter, but they are unusual and may help triage:

1. **Two-GPU layer split with `--resident-experts`**, experts 100% resident, `0 blob reads from the
   file`, `0 exchanged with the VRAM tier`. I have no data point for this model on a single GPU yet.
2. **Asymmetric links** — CUDA0 is physically x4 (6.1 GB/s, engine's own `miss cost x3.27`) against
   CUDA1 at x16. The split search does see it (`CUDA0 link 6.1 GB/s -> miss cost x3.27`).
3. **The engine binary was compiled on a different machine** and copied over (that build machine was
   a Haswell Xeon, also AVX2-only, same CUDA 13.3.73, same `archs=[89]`). I can recompile on the
   target if that is worth excluding.
4. `--max-context 131072 --kv int8`, MTP `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5` with the fetched MTP adapter.

## Questions

1. Is the answer-body collapse (as opposed to the reasoning loop of #728 / #1622) a known failure
   mode? I could not find an open issue that matches "correct for N hundred tokens, then a
   repeated-token collapse, CJK only, greedy, unpruned".
2. Is there a knob to bound it? `repeat_stop_tokens` counts a *single* token's run, so an interleaved
   `颊 / cheek / face` cycle is invisible to it — something like the `repeat_stop_period` discussed in
   #1613 would catch this shape.
3. Would you like me to run a control on the same engine with a different size (IQ2_XS or
   UD-Q4_K_XL) to separate "IQ3_S dequant path" from "engine-wide CJK path"? I can also recompile on
   the target host, or bisect CUDA versions if #892's miscompile family is still open on sm_89.

title: stager-transient-regression
body:
# Prefill: the "transient source" heuristic makes RAM-resident Q8 prefill 4-7x slower

First bad commit: `361537b` — *"prefill: UD-Q4_K_XL prompts 2.8x faster (16K: 57 -> 160 tok/s on an RTX 5070) - 32 stager threads and a 128-deep ring when the experts are read from the GGUF in place; MMQ for its Q4_K / Q5_K / Q5_1 experts"*.

The heuristic is still in `v0.1.40.1` (`src/prefill/prefill.cpp:861-862`, unchanged).

## Environment

| | |
|---|---|
| GPU | NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5090, 32607 MiB (driver 580.173.02); a second card (RTX 2080 SUPER, 8192 MiB) is present and idle |
| System RAM | 376 GiB |
| Host -> device | 13.8 GB/s (engine's own PCIe probe) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, Q8_0 — pack `qwen38-q8_0` plus the native `Q8_0-0000x-of-00006.gguf` shards |
| Engine args | `--resident-budget-gib 240 --expert-cache 1944 --prefill auto --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 262144` |
| OS | Linux |

The experts are **pinned in system RAM** (`--resident-budget-gib 240`), not read from the SSD during prefill.

## Symptom

A 128k-token prompt (123,885 tokens) on a fully warm page cache:

| Engine | Prefill | 128k prompt |
|---|---|---|
| `v0.1.31` | 390-427 tok/s | 4.8-5.3 min |
| `v0.1.32` | 107.5 tok/s | 19.2 min |
| `v0.1.33` | 109.3 tok/s | 18.9 min |
| `v0.1.34` | 95.4 tok/s | 21.7 min |
| `v0.1.37` | 53.9 tok/s | 38.3 min |
| `v0.1.40.1` | 57.8 tok/s | 35.7 min |

Every run: same machine, same model, same prompt, same seed (707), page cache preloaded with `vmtouch -t` before each start, KV streaming and expert-cache hit rates identical (78.01% / 35-38%). Only the engine binary differs.

## Bisection

`git bisect` in a detached worktree, `v0.1.31` good / `v0.1.32` bad, one variable at a time (each candidate built with `-DSTRATA_ENABLE_CUDA=ON -DCMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=120`, measured with the same warm-cache harness):

| Commit | Description | tok/s | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| `505e5e9` | PLE: the n-gram table in FP8 E4M3 | 433.7 | good |
| `ee1e18e` | serve: model aliases (#297) | 426.7 | good |
| `5ba8c5b` | docs only (`docs/DETAILS.md`, `docs/UNSLOTH_Q4.md`) | — | good |
| `d058fde` | setup only (`setup.py`, docs, tests) | — | good |
| **`361537b`** | **prefill: 32 stager threads and a 128-deep ring when the experts are read from the GGUF in place** | **107.6** | **bad** |
| `5080b92` | Merge branch 'f-132-amd' | 87.2 | bad |
| `d434c02` | Merge branch 'f-132-q4' (`v0.1.32`) | 107.1 | bad |

`361537b` is the first bad commit.

## Mechanism

The commit adds this to `prefill.cpp` (identical in `v0.1.40.1`, lines 861-862):

```cpp
bool files = false;
for (int64_t l = 0; src != nullptr && !files && l < g.n_layers; ++l)
    for (int64_t e = 0; !files && e < g.n_expert; ++e) files = src->transient(l, e);
const int threads = stv ? std::clamp(std::atoi(stv), 1, 32) : files ? 32 : std::max(2, std::min(4, hw / 4));
if (files && std::getenv("STRATA_STAGER_RING") == nullptr) m.stager->kRing = 4 * threads;
```

The comment states the intent: *"most of a chunk's blobs are page faults on the SSD, so the copies need many reads in flight"*. That is right for the target case — Unsloth's UD-Q4_K_XL read in place beyond its RAM budget.

The check, however, only asks **whether** an expert source is `transient()`, never **where the bytes come from**. Our Q8 setup answers `transient() == true` while every blob is already pinned in RAM. It therefore gets the SSD profile — 32 copy threads and a 128-deep ring — and on this machine that is 4x slower than the 4-thread / 16-deep default the same commit keeps "for every other source".

A second, smaller effect points the same way: `ring_slots()` chose 384 slots in `v0.1.31` (`g_pinned_share >= 0.9 ? 384 : 96`) and picks 1024 in `v0.1.37+` (`fused_ring() ? 1024 : 384`). The 1024 ring is sized for the fused Q2_0 layouts, not for a Q8 pack.

## Verified workaround (no rebuild)

All three switches already exist in `v0.1.37` and `v0.1.40.1`. Restoring the `v0.1.31` values on the **same** engine binary:

| Engine | default | `STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=4` `STRATA_STAGER_RING=16` | `+ STRATA_PREFILL_RING=384` |
|---|---|---|---|
| `v0.1.37` | 53.9 | 355.9 | **412.8** |
| `v0.1.40.1` | 57.8 | — | **350.3** |

`v0.1.37` with the three variables reaches `v0.1.31` level (412.8 against 390-427 tok/s), 128k in 5.0 min instead of 38.3 min.

Ruled out as the cause, each measured on `v0.1.37` with the stager fix in place:

- `--pcie-frac 0.29` (the value `v0.1.31`'s probe derived): 355.9 — no change.
- `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=0` (staged hyper-connection off): 360.3 — no change.

## Proposed patch (not built, not measured — a suggestion)

The heuristic should ask where the bytes come from, not only whether the source is transient. `g_pinned_share` is already available at that point in the file:

```diff
-        const int threads = stv ? std::clamp(std::atoi(stv), 1, 32) : files ? 32 : std::max(2, std::min(4, hw / 4));
-        if (files && std::getenv("STRATA_STAGER_RING") == nullptr) m.stager->kRing = 4 * threads;
+        // 32 threads and a deep ring pay off when the blobs are page faults on the SSD. A RAM-resident layout
+        // answers transient() as well, but its copies come from pinned memory, where the old defaults measured
+        // 4x faster (128k prompt: 412.8 against 107.6 tok/s on an RTX 5090 / 376 GiB RAM).
+        const bool ssd = files && g_pinned_share < 0.9;
+        const int threads = stv ? std::clamp(std::atoi(stv), 1, 32) : ssd ? 32 : std::max(2, std::min(4, hw / 4));
+        if (ssd && std::getenv("STRATA_STAGER_RING") == nullptr) m.stager->kRing = 4 * threads;
```

This keeps the UD-Q4_K_XL in-place path untouched for the machines it was written for. We have not compiled or benchmarked it — the numbers above are from the existing environment variables, which is what we run in production today.

## Secondary finding

With the workaround applied, `v0.1.40.1` still runs about 15% behind `v0.1.37` (350.3 against 412.8 tok/s) on this model and prompt. That gap is independent of the stager and is a separate, much smaller regression somewhere between `v0.1.37` and `v0.1.40.1`; we have not bisected it.

## How to reproduce

1. Q8_0 pack + native shards, `--resident-budget-gib 240 --expert-cache 1944 --prefill auto --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`.
2. Preload the model files into the page cache (`vmtouch -t <files>`) so the measurement does not include SSD reads.
3. Send a ~124k-token prompt with a fixed seed, `max_tokens: 1`, and read `prompt eval count` / `prompt eval duration` from the usage block.
4. Compare `v0.1.31` with any engine from `v0.1.32` up; then re-run the newer engine with `STRATA_STAGER_THREADS=4 STRATA_STAGER_RING=16 STRATA_PREFILL_RING=384`.

[stager-transient-fix.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/33151911/stager-transient-fix.patch)

title: CPU expert-pool 20 ms spin can hurt GPU-heavy decode; 100 µs gives ~15% higher TG and ~4× lower CPU usage on dual RTX 4090
body:
I found a potentially large performance issue with the default CPU expert-pool spin-before-sleep policy 
on a GPU-heavy / mostly-resident configuration.

This is not a correctness issue. The existing `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US` test knob is enough to reproduce 
the effect, so I am filing this without a patch — the right upstream fix may be a different default, 
adaptive parking, or another policy.

## System / configuration

- 2× RTX 4090 24 GiB
- Ryzen 9 7950X3D
- VM with 16 vCPUs
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next IQ3_S
- current Strata v0.1.39-era source/binary
- layer split K=25
- `pcie-frac=0.28`
- 15 CPU expert-pool workers
- MTP `spec=4`, `spec-min-p=0.5`
- suffix lookup off
- prompt reuse off
- serial requests
- 4096 output tokens

The comparison below uses the **same executable**. The only relevant change is:

```bash
STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US=100
```

instead of the default 20 ms spin-before-sleep.

Each point has 3 valid measured requests after the same warmup.

## Result

| Total context | Default TG median | 100 us TG median | Change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 32K | 155.9 tok/s | **178.5 tok/s** | **+14.5%** |
| 128K | 133.2 tok/s | **154.0 tok/s** | **+15.6%** |

The individual 100 us TG runs were:

- 32K: `178.2 / 178.6 / 178.5`
- 128K: `144.1 / 154.0 / 165.4`

Median request wall time fell by approximately 11% at both context sizes.

## CPU utilization

The more surprising result is CPU usage during decode:

| Total context | Default VM CPU | 100 us VM CPU |
|---:|---:|---:|
| 32K | ~99.2% | **~28.0%** |
| 128K | ~97.9% | **~25.8%** |

GPU utilization remained roughly unchanged.

The generated output, MTP behavior, expert-cache capacities and normal routing counters were identical in the paired comparison, so the speed difference is not explained by a different greedy/MTP trajectory or by giving the candidate more cache.

## What seems to be happening

The current pool has:

```cpp
static constexpr std::chrono::milliseconds kSpinBeforeSleep{20};
```

and `STRATA_POOL_SPIN_US` overrides it.

On this configuration most expert work is already handled by the GPUs. Many layers therefore have little or no CPU expert work, but the worker pool can continue spinning for up to 20 ms after becoming idle.

With 15 workers this keeps almost the entire VM CPU busy even when those cores are not doing useful expert computation.

Reducing the spin period to 100 us lets the workers park much sooner and substantially reduces CPU contention.

This appears to improve GPU-side inference throughput as well, rather than merely reducing power/CPU usage.

## Important trade-off

100 us is not free.

In separate selected-layer diagnostics, CPU-positive completion-wait medians increased from roughly:

- **4–6 us** with the default policy

to roughly:

- **59–72 us** with the 100 us setting.

All-local wait floors remained around 4–5 us.

So I would not suggest simply changing the global default from 20 ms to 100 us without more workload coverage.

This probably depends on how often the CPU expert pool is actually needed.

## Possible upstream direction

An adaptive policy may be preferable to one fixed spin duration.

For example:

- park quickly after mostly/all-local GPU layers,
- retain a longer spin window when CPU expert work has recently occurred or jobs are pending,
- possibly adapt from recent CPU-positive frequency / completion latency.

The important observation is that VM-wide ~100% CPU in this configuration was mostly not useful expert computation: reducing the idle-spin window both lowered CPU use dramatically and increased decode throughput.

## Reproducibility / caveat

The clean benchmark used one long repository-maintenance workload at 32K and 128K total context limits.

The result therefore does **not** establish a universal +15% improvement yet, especially for workloads with substantially more CPU misses.

I am currently validating the 100 us setting on independent code/math/structured workloads, including more CPU-positive cases.

The current evidence is strong enough that I thought the fixed 20 ms default was worth reporting now.

title: Regression: automatic GPU ordering in be8db787 reduces decode throughput ~15% on dual RTX 5070 Ti
body:
Possibly related to #1352.

The automatic GPU ordering introduced in `be8db787c233acdde3e5887b652a87df23f0445a` causes a reproducible decode performance regression on my dual RTX 5070 Ti setup.

## Hardware

- Windows 11
- 2 × NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti 16 GB
- Same model, config and prompt used for all tests
- IQ3_S model

## Performance

| Version / setting | Decode speed |
|---|---:|
| `v0.1.40.4` | ~91 tok/s |
| `v0.1.41` / latest with automatic GPU ordering | ~77 tok/s |
| latest + `"gpu_order": "as_given"` | ~91 tok/s |

So the automatic ordering causes roughly a 15% decode throughput regression on this machine, while opting out restores the previous performance completely.

## Git bisect

I bisected between:

- good: `v0.1.40.4`
- bad: `v0.1.41`

Result:

```text
be8db787c233acdde3e5887b652a87df23f0445a is the first 'bad' commit

serve: card order for an auto layer split, faster card last
(SMs x clock), gpu_order as_given opts out (#1352)
```

## GPU scores and resulting order

Using Strata's own `gpu_speed_scores()` / `ordered_gpus()`:

```text
scores: {0: 173740000.0, 1: 171640000.0}

[strata] layer split: card order 1,0
(the faster card last; "gpu_order": "as_given" keeps 0,1, #1352)

auto order: [1, 0]
as_given: [0, 1]
```

For comparison, `nvidia-smi` reports the same maximum SM clock for both cards:

```text
index, name, clocks.max.sm [MHz], pci.bus_id
0, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti, 3090 MHz, 00000000:01:00.0
1, NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5070 Ti, 3090 MHz, 00000000:03:00.0
```

The CUDA-derived scores differ only slightly, but that is enough for the new heuristic to reorder the cards from `[0,1]` to `[1,0]`.

On this system, that reorder reduces decode throughput from ~91 tok/s to ~77 tok/s.

## Workaround

Adding this to the model config restores the previous performance on the latest version:

```json
"gpu_order": "as_given"
```

With that setting enabled, decode throughput returns to ~91 tok/s.

## Notes

Because both GPUs are effectively the same model and the score difference is very small, it may be worth avoiding automatic reordering when scores are very close.

More generally, `SM count × clock` alone may not be enough to choose the optimal order, since actual performance can also depend on PCIe topology, display usage, device placement and the work assigned to the final pipeline stage.

title: Add locally bundled MathJax rendering to web chat
body:
Depends on #1829 (shared LaTeX/web math core). This branch builds directly on that core; its commits remain visible against main until the core merges. Addresses #1769 and #1780.

Replaces the placeholder adapter with MathJax 4.1.3 and local New Computer Modern font assets. Enable **Render math** in Chat's sampling drawer and Apply to typeset inline and display equations. Rendering starts disabled. Code stays literal; invalid or unsupported equations retain their source. Copy, export, history, and model requests preserve the original text.

Validated in Chromium, Firefox, and Playwright WebKit on Windows, including streaming, currency/code handling, macro isolation, deadlines, stale results, source preservation, and narrow layouts. WebKit coverage is not a physical Safari/iPhone test; semantic markup checks are not a manual screen-reader audit.
