title: sycl/CMakeLists.txt test registration lags the top-level one: iq_parity and ple_parity fail on every checkout
body:
**Environment**
- Ubuntu 26.04.1, kernel 7.0.0-34, 2× Intel Arc Pro B70 (`xe`)
- compute-runtime 26.31.39395.14, oneAPI DPC++ 2026.1.1
- Native build (no Docker), AOT `-DSTRATA_SYCL_AOT=bmg-g31`
- Strata `fb58e0d` (v0.1.41)

**Summary**
The SYCL port registers both tests in its generic parity loop as `<test> --selftest`, run from the build tree:

- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt:227-233`: `foreach(p IN ITEMS dequant_s2 s2_gemv iq ... ple ...)` …
  `add_test(NAME ${p}_parity COMMAND ${p}_parity --selftest)`

The top-level `CMakeLists.txt` registers each of them on its own, with what it needs. The SYCL copy never followed.
So both fail on every checkout of the port, for reasons unrelated to the kernels they test. Every port `ctest` run
then reports two red tests that mean nothing, which hides real ones.

| | top-level `CMakeLists.txt` (CUDA/HIP) | `sycl/CMakeLists.txt` |
|---|---|---|
| `iq_parity` | `iq_parity_fixtures` runs `tools/iq_fixture.py` as a CTest fixture; `iq_parity <build>/iq_fixture`; skip code 3 without numpy (`:666-710`, from #264, 0.1.31) | `iq_parity --selftest`, no fixture step |
| `ple_parity` | `--in/--out` from `STRATA_PLE_FIXTURE_DIR`, `WORKING_DIRECTORY` = source tree (`:914-925`) | `ple_parity --selftest`, working directory = build tree |

### a. `iq_parity` treats `--selftest` as its fixture directory

`iq_parity` has no flags: `sycl/src/kernels/iq_parity.cpp:29` reads
`const std::string dir = argc > 1 ? argv[1] : "logs/iq_fixture";`. The tool's documented use (`:3`) is
`python tools/iq_fixture.py --out <dir> && build/iq_parity <dir>`, and each missing fixture counts as a failure
(`:37-45`). Nothing in the SYCL build runs `tools/iq_fixture.py`.

**Actual**, on all ten types:
```
IQ2_XXS  missing fixture: --selftest/IQ2_XXS.bin or --selftest/IQ2_XXS.f32 - generate the fixtures first with python tools/iq_fixture.py --out --selftest ...
```

### b. `ple_parity` looks for its GGUF relative to the build tree

`sycl/src/kernels/ple_parity.cpp:305-307`:
```cpp
// --gguf, else $STRATA_PLE_GGUF, else the development layout (run from the engine root)
std::string gguf = std::getenv("STRATA_PLE_GGUF") ? std::getenv("STRATA_PLE_GGUF")
                                                  : "../../Q2_0/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf";
```
The comment says "run from the engine root", but CTest runs the test from the build tree. With `--selftest`, a
missing table returns `2` (`:330-334`), and so does a missing `dense.bin` pack (`:336-341`). No CMake variable reaches
the test, and `STRATA_PLE_GGUF` appears in the source but not in the docs.

**Actual:**
`ple_parity: required PLE table is missing or incompatible: ../../Q2_0/Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-Q2_0-00002-of-00002.gguf (...)`

This issue does **not** ask for `ple_parity` to skip. The top-level CMake keeps a missing input as a hard error on
purpose ("A test that passes by finding nothing to compare is the failure mode this project keeps re-learning",
`CMakeLists.txt:914-917`), and #568's fixture-free rewrite was declined. The ask is only that the port get the same
contract: a hard error, but one a user can satisfy.

**Repro (both)**
```
cmake -S sycl -B build-sycl-aot -DSTRATA_SYCL_AOT=bmg-g31 && cmake --build build-sycl-aot -j
ctest --test-dir build-sycl-aot -R '^(iq|ple)_parity$' -V
```

**Expected:** the same behaviour as the CUDA build. `iq_parity` generates its fixtures and runs (or skips without
numpy). `ple_parity` can be pointed at its inputs at configure time, and its relative defaults resolve against the
engine root.

**Suggested fix:** take `iq` and `ple` out of the `foreach` at `sycl/CMakeLists.txt:227` and port the top-level
registrations:
```cmake
# iq: as CMakeLists.txt:700-706 (with the _iq_python interpreter probe from :669-699)
add_test(NAME iq_parity_fixtures COMMAND ${_iq_python} ${STRATA_ROOT}/tools/iq_fixture.py --out ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/iq_fixture)
set_tests_properties(iq_parity_fixtures PROPERTIES FIXTURES_SETUP iq_fixture_data SKIP_RETURN_CODE 3)
add_test(NAME iq_parity COMMAND iq_parity ${CMAKE_CURRENT_BINARY_DIR}/iq_fixture)
set_tests_properties(iq_parity PROPERTIES FIXTURES_REQUIRED iq_fixture_data SKIP_RETURN_CODE 3)

# ple: as CMakeLists.txt:921-925, plus a variable for the GGUF the SYCL copy reads
set(STRATA_PLE_GGUF "" CACHE FILEPATH "Q2_0 shard 2 GGUF for ple_parity")
add_test(NAME ple_parity COMMAND ple_parity --selftest $<$<BOOL:${STRATA_PLE_GGUF}>:--gguf;${STRATA_PLE_GGUF}>
         WORKING_DIRECTORY ${STRATA_ROOT} COMMAND_EXPAND_LISTS)
```
Add the `--pack` and `--in/--out` inputs (via `STRATA_PLE_FIXTURE_DIR`) the same way if the SYCL copy needs them.
Then name the variables in `docs/INTEL.md`'s build section, so a port user knows `ple_parity` needs the Q2_0 model.

**Related:** #264 (the `iq_parity` fix, top-level only); #568 (the stream-sync half was taken in 0.1.40.2, the
fixture-free `ple_parity` rewrite was declined).

title: Windows HIP: START-HERE.bat --calibrate works on RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100) - ~15% decode gain
body:
﻿
(Reporting per docs/AMD_HIP.md "Reporting a Windows AMD run"; calibration on HIP is tracked in #566, the Windows
section says "no calibration" â€” it does run, so here is the data.)

## Machine

- Windows 11 (64-bit), AMD Ryzen 9 7900X (12 cores), 64 GB DDR5 (63 GB per hardware key), NVMe
- **RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100)**, driver 32.0.31041.1004 (2026-08-16) â€” drives the desktop

title: qwen35moe follow-ups: VRAM cap + quality mode, MTP for F16 draft tensors, chunked GDN, 256/8 route-resident
body:
## What this is

A **stacked PR on top of #1402** (qwen35moe support). It contains the qwen35moe follow-up work we built
and measured while validating that PR on one machine (RTX 3080 10 GB, Windows 11, CUDA 13.2, sm_86):

- MTP for third-party single-file GGUFs whose draft block is stored as **F16**;
- an **opt-in VRAM fraction cap** (`--vram-frac`) and a **quality cap mode** (`--vram-cap-mode quality`)
  that keeps every expert miss on the same GPU kernel as a hit;
- opt-in **chunked DeltaNet prefill** for qwen35moe;
- **route-resident routing generalized to 256-expert / top-8 models** (the #1737 warp-shuffle idea,
  merged with our 256/8 implementation);
- the determinism fixes the auto expert cache needed on Windows/WDDM;
- setup-family and SYCL follow-ups.

Base: #1402 head `48534f3`. The first commits in the diff are #1402's; the 16 commits listed below are
this PR's content. The five upstream PRs we also adopted locally (#1700, #1660, #1659, #1696, #1720) are
**deliberately not included** — they are separate PRs and should land on their own.

The repo's guide is *one change per pull request*. This is a stack of related qwen35moe follow-ups; I am
happy to split it into separate PRs (MTP-F16; cap+quality; chunked GDN; route-resident 256/8) if that is
easier to review. The MTP F16 commit is the smallest and probably the most valuable on its own.

## Commits

**MTP for third-party GGUFs**
- `MTP: accept F16 draft tensors in a single-file GGUF` — the draft-layer loader took F32 for norms and
  BF16/F32 for routers, so a single-file GGUF whose MTP block keeps `ffn_gate_inp.weight` at F16 refused to
  start. F16→F32 is exact; F16→BF16 uses the same round-to-nearest-even as the F32 path. The finite cases
  check out over all 65,536 half bit patterns; NaN needed a later fix (the first checker skipped NaNs, and
  the rounded addition carried them into infinity/signed zero — see the follow-up commit below). Measured on
  the Huihui Q4_K file: **62.5 tok/s vs 26.0** without MTP, 21/25 drafts accepted.
- `Gate Huihui MTP on the F16 draft loader capability` — setup only offers MTP for that family when the
  loader supports it.

**Opt-in VRAM cap + quality mode**
- `Add opt-in total VRAM fraction cap through cache reserves` — `--vram-frac F` sizes the expert cache so
  the engine's own use stays under F of the card; a floor is kept free and the plan is frozen pre-touch
  (post-touch readings only accept or refuse; no resize).
- `Add opt-in uniform-GPU VRAM cap quality mode` — `--vram-cap-mode quality` routes every expert miss
  through the grouped GPU kernel, no CPU fallback. Measured **20/20 token-identical** outputs vs the
  uncapped run, 6,759 vs 9,397 MiB peak.
- `Book late VRAM and refuse serve requests that cross the floor` + `cap booking: keep the named late
  allocations, leave graphs to the slack + refusal` — books the chunked-GDN scratch and MTP prefill records
  in the frozen budget, re-checks the floor on the serve path and after `cudaGraphInstantiate`, and logs
  free memory at READY / first capture / first chunked launch / first checkpoint. Validated: free
  3,511–3,577 MiB against the 2,048 MiB floor, no refusals, prefix reuse intact.

**qwen35moe prefill and routing**
- `Port opt-in chunked DeltaNet recurrence to qwen35moe` — opt-in (`STRATA_GDN_CHUNKED`), parity-checked
  against the default recurrence.
- `Use qwen35moe active expert count for router lookahead` — width 8 instead of qwen4exp's 10.
- `Port opt-in route-resident routing to 256-expert top-8 models` — the 256/8 counterpart of #1737.
- `route-resident: one warp per token for the 512/10 and 256/8 swap` — merges #1737's warp-shuffle swap
  with the 256/8 implementation into one templated kernel (`route_resident_impl<NE,K>`). This commit can
  replace #1737 if preferred: it contains its approach for 512/10 and adds 256/8.

**Determinism, setup, SYCL**
- `Make expert-cache auto use one fixed 1 GiB haircut` + `Bucket the qwen35moe auto-cache haircut and check
  the reserve` — fixes the auto-cache non-reproducibility on Windows/WDDM (2,974 vs 3,494 slots between
  identical runs) and refuses cleanly instead of stalling under low headroom.
- `Add Huihui abliterated Qwen3.6 setup family` — the family in `setup.py` with tests.
- `Keep the shared Qwen36 setup test harness offline on Windows`.
- `qsa: mirror the dense-attention validate() fix into the SYCL twin` — the CUDA fix in #1402 did not touch
  the SYCL twin.
- `SYCL generate: explicitly refuse the CUDA-only VRAM cap flags` — fail closed instead of ignoring them.

## Validation (RTX 3080 10 GB, Windows 11, CUDA 13.2, sm_86)

**Measured on this exact branch** (stacked on `48534f3`):
- Build: VS 18 / Ninja / Release / sm_86, exit 0.
- Full `ctest`: 96 passed, 1 skipped (`expert_multi_test`), 1 failed (`ple_parity`, missing Flash-Next
  **Q2_0** fixture, not present on this machine). The two cap tests are `vram_cap_test` (169 CPU checks)
  and `vram_cap_quality_test` (2,529 CPU checks); the other suites are the repo's own.
- Capped quality + MTP smoke on the Huihui Q4_K file: exit 0, output token ids identical to the validated
  line (64/64), `--expert-cache 3200` capped to 1430 slots, free 3,513 MiB after the first capture.

**Measured on the integrated line this work sits in** (`95f205d` + the cap-floor fix, sha `d58e8ded`;
it also contains the five upstream PRs we adopted locally — #1700/#1660/#1659/#1696/#1720 — which this PR
deliberately excludes):
- Cap + quality: 20/20 token-identical vs uncapped, 6,759 vs 9,397 MiB peak.
- MTP: 62.5 vs 26.0 tok/s (2.4×), 21/25 accepted; server path 71.1 tok/s.
- Full stack (cap + quality + MTP + chunked + route-resident): 10/10 arms exit 0, whole-card peaks
  7,269–7,371 MiB under the 8,192 ceiling; server prefix reuse 1,005/1,012 with TTFT 1.89 s → 0.098 s;
  chunked kernel launches confirmed under Nsight Systems; HumanEval 39/40 at 2,048 and **39/40 at 4,096**
  (no truncations; the single miss is HumanEval/132's wrong implementation).
- Determinism: byte-identical outputs across repeated runs **at a fixed cache geometry**; the bucketed
  haircut reduces but cannot eliminate sensitivity when the pre-touch reading crosses a bucket boundary, so
  a run can still open a different slot count. Cache size does not change the output tokens in quality mode
  (20/20 identical), but the slot count is not guaranteed bit-identical run to run. Clean refusal (no stall)
  when the reserve cannot be met.
- Backends: **CUDA built and exercised; HIP and SYCL were not built** (no toolchain on this machine). The
  SYCL changes are verified by inspection only, which does not meet `AGENTS.md`'s build-every-touched-backend
  rule; an Intel/HIP machine should build them before this is merged.

## What this leaves alone

- **Defaults:** cap, quality, chunked and route-resident are all opt-in. Two of the determinism commits do
  change the qwen35moe **fast-mode** auto-cache path: the bucketed haircut activates under WDDM for eligible
  native non-indexed models even without `--vram-frac`, and the router lookahead uses the model's active
  expert count (8 instead of 10). qwen4exp keeps its measured-shortfall loop; no other default path changes.
- **qwen4exp:** the route-resident change keeps the 512/10 behavior; the auto-cache fixes keep the
  measured-shortfall loop for qwen4exp.
- **Not included:** #1700 / #1660 / #1659 / #1696 / #1720 (separate PRs) and #1737 (superseded by the
  templated 512/10 + 256/8 commit here).

## Follow-up fixes from an adversarial review (2026-10-10)

Three review findings were fixed on top of the stack:

- `MTP F16: keep NaN NaN in the F16/BF16 conversion` — the rounded addition carried NaN into infinity or a
  signed zero; NaN now keeps a nonzero BF16 mantissa.
- `SYCL: refuse a malformed STRATA_VRAM_FRAC like the CUDA build does` — 0, NaN, empty, trailing junk and
  underflow-to-zero were silently ignored; they now exit 2 as on CUDA.
- `VRAM cap: check the floor at every chunk, at serve decode admission, before pipelined windows` — the
  floor was checked only before the first prompt chunk; a long prefill, a fully reused prompt, and the
  `--pipeline-windows` decode loop could step past it. Prefill now has a per-chunk guard, serve re-checks
  at decode admission, **all five `pl_launch` sites are guarded** (the initial A, the speculative B, the
  promoted A's stage-1 launch, and both prompt-pipeline launches), and the first-use chunked-GDN scratch
  allocation checks the floor before taking its bytes.

Still open from that review (not fixed here): the stack does not meet the repo's one-change-per-PR rule,
and HIP/SYCL builds are not run.

## Known limits

- One machine: Windows, RTX 3080, CUDA. No AMD/Intel or Linux numbers here.
- The F16 draft conversion is bit-checked and end-to-end on the Huihui GGUF; no other F16-draft model was
  available.
- Quality mode requires a native expert pack; on this machine it cannot run the 46.8 GiB Flash-Next arena
  because the whole arena cannot be pinned (a host limit, unrelated to these paths).
- The determinism fixes target the Windows/WDDM auto-cache path; Linux behavior was not re-measured here.

title: serve: probe the SYCL launcher's engine binary for --tail-role-token
body:
Fixes #1781.

## What

`effort_end_args()` decides `--tail-role-token` support by grepping `exe`. On the SYCL port `exe` is `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh`, a launcher that execs `${STRATA_SYCL_BIN:-build-sycl-aot/strata}` inside a container — the script never names the flag, so `"effort_position": "end"` printed the "needs engine 0.1.39" line and stayed off on every SYCL install, exactly as the reporter measured.

A `#!` exe now gets a second read through `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (the config's `env`, then the process environment) or the default `build-sycl-aot/strata`, relative to the repo two levels above the script — the same layout the launcher computes. A binary exe reads exactly as before; a missing/unreadable binary falls back to the launcher's text, so the probe still answers "unsupported" rather than crashing.

## What it leaves alone

- CUDA/HIP paths: `exe` is the engine there, so the new branch never runs.
- The probe's semantics: still a byte-grep of the engine image, still no version parsing, still a silent `None` when the flag is absent.
- The launcher itself: `strata-sycl.sh` is unchanged; this is server-side resolution of the convention it already documents.

## Tests

`serve/test_effort_position.py` (new, 6 tests): binary exe unchanged behavior; the SYCL layout via the default path and via `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (config `env` and process env); a launcher whose binary lacks the flag; an unreadable/missing binary falling back to the script; `start`/invalid-value handling. 6/6 pass, plus `test_runconfig` and `test_frontend` (17 tests) unchanged.

Not tested: a real SYCL container run — the probe only reads files, and the reporter's environment has the actual image; the layout mirrors the launcher's own `${STRATA_SYCL_BIN:-...}` default and `../..` repo resolution.

title: Add shared LaTeX/web math core without a rendering engine
body:
Adds the shared web chat integration for future math renderers. **This PR contains no viewer, typesetting engine, fonts, or TeX compiler.** The placeholder adapter reports unavailable and leaves equations as readable source. Related to #1769 and #1780; rendering support will come in separate follow-up PRs.

- Adds an opt-in **Render math** setting, disabled by default. With it disabled, assistant answers use the existing Markdown path.
- Recognizes inline `\(...\)` and conservative `$...$`, plus display `\[...\]` and `$$...$$`. Protects equation source before Markdown formatting and keeps code and currency literal.
- Preserves source for copying, Markdown export, saved history, and subsequent model requests. Handles streaming and ignores stale asynchronous results.
- Defines the renderer adapter contract, serialized conversion queue, 256-entry cache, 16 KiB UTF-8 input limit, initialization deadline, and asynchronous rendering deadline. Adds restricted same-origin asset serving for later bundled renderers.
- Includes the shared fixture corpus and browser acceptance suite. Separate KaTeX, MathJax, and isolated full TeX branches supply the adapters and dependencies on top of this core.

Core smoke-tested in Chromium for default-off behavior, unavailable-engine source fallback, persistence, API source preservation, and disabling round-trip without engine assets. The shared acceptance suite also passed on the KaTeX implementation in Chromium, Firefox, and Playwright WebKit. Timers cannot interrupt synchronous JavaScript; adapters must bound macro expansion. Macro isolation is an adapter requirement.

See [the interface and branch structure](https://github.com/CC-David-CC/Strata-a5500/blob/feat/web-math-common/docs/WEB_MATH_INTERFACE.md). The full browser acceptance suite requires a real implementation adapter; this foundation deliberately does not typeset equations.

title: HIP (gfx1030): intermittent 'verify: timed out at layer N (#267)' with UD-Q4_K_XL — repro data
body:
## Environment

- RX 6950 XT (gfx1030), ROCm 7.1, HIP backend, engine **0.1.37** and **current main** (99f3dbd) — same behavior on both
- 31 GB RAM, UD-Q4_K_XL (`--native` GGUF-in-place, `--resident-budget-gib`), `--spec 2`, `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=0` (the default hc staging path also hangs on this card)
- Model: the Huihui abliterated re-split of Qwen3.8-Flash-Next UD-Q4_K_XL (needs the split-shard arch-guard fix from #648 to load at all)

## Symptom

Decode usually starts and can generate 24+ tokens correctly, then a verify window dies:

```
strata generate: verify: timed out at layer 11; its GPU waits were released but the GPU did not finish within 5 s (#267)
```

- Always at a full-attention layer (3, 11, 13, 25, 35, 46 seen — every N was (L+1)%4==0).
- **Intermittent**: same command, same budget: one run completes 24 tokens, the next hangs on the first verify round.
- When the release message says 'the GPU finished' the spin ended at release; when it says 'did not finish within 5 s' the graph was still running 25 s in.
- Frequency scales with `--resident-budget-gib`: 12 GiB hung 2/2 runs; 7 GiB roughly 1-in-3.

## Ruled out

- `--sync-every-layer` — still hangs
- `STRATA_ADAPT_NOWAIT=1` (main) — still hangs
- `--no-pool` — different failure (`--spec needs the device residency table`), so the pool interleave cannot be fully bypassed
- It is **not** the #648 loader issue — that is fixed in these runs (prefill + many decode rounds complete before the hang)

## Suspect

Timing-sensitive flag handshake between the CPU expert pool and the verify window's spin kernels — the warm-page-cache runs (fast PLE, fast prefill) hang more often than the first cold run, which completed. Happy to run any instrumented build or capture rocm-smi/rid traces if useful.

title: prefill copy_i32: illegal memory access on long prompts when the prefill chunk is large (auto:32768)
body:
## Summary

`prefill copy_i32` faults with an **illegal memory access** on **long prompts when the prefill chunk is large**, then `check()` calls `std::exit(1)` and the engine dies (the server restarts it, ~100 s). It is **intermittent** (the same prompt sometimes succeeds) and **reproduces on both 0.1.40 and 0.1.40.2**.

The chunk size is the isolated variable:

| `--prefill` | actual chunk | requests | crashes |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| `auto:32768` | 19,200-20,480 | 45 | **11 (~35 %)** |
| `8192` | 8,192 | 20 | **0** |
| `auto:16384` | 16,384 | 16 | **0** |

Removing `--pipeline-windows` did **not** stop it (1 crash in 4 requests), so it is not that path.

## Where it fails

```
src/prefill/kernels.cu:70    void check(const char* what) {
                                 const cudaError_t e = cudaGetLastError();
                                 if (e != cudaSuccess) { std::fprintf(stderr, "prefill %s: %s\n", what,
                                     cudaGetErrorString(e)); std::exit(1); }
                             }
src/prefill/kernels.cu:1677  __global__ void copy_i32_kernel(int32_t* dst, const int32_t* src, int64_t n)
src/prefill/kernels.cu:1695  void copy_i32(int32_t* dst, const int32_t* src, int64_t n, void* stream) {
                                 ... copy_i32_kernel<<<min((n+255)/256, 256), 256, 0, stream>>>(dst, src, n);
                                 check("copy_i32");
                             }
```

Call sites (all pass `T * K` int32, `T` = chunk, `K` = top-k):

```
src/prefill/prefill.cpp:2694  if (grp_mapped) copy_i32(m.grp_dev, m.ids, T * K, m.cs);
src/prefill/prefill.cpp:2829  copy_i32(m.slot_dev, m.grp_dev + m.grp_tk, T * K, m.cs);
src/prefill/prefill.cpp:2830  copy_i32(m.src_dev, m.grp_dev + 2 * m.grp_tk, T * K, m.cs);
```

The engine log line is exactly:

```
prefill copy_i32: an illegal memory access was encountered
```

then the server logs `engine started: ...` (a fresh engine), so the request is lost and the model reloads.

## Reproduce

Engine 0.1.40 (and 0.1.40.2), Windows:

```
strata.exe --serve --pack <iq3_xxs pack> --native <shard1> --ple-gguf <shard2> \
  --expert-profile data/expert-profile.bin --expert-cache auto \
  --prefill auto:32768 --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.70 --mtp <mtp/rt> \
  --max-context 262144 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vision \
  --vram-reserve-mib 690 --pool-workers 8 --trim-stage-weights \
  --pipeline-windows 2 --layer-split 26
```

Send a prompt of ~54 K-114 K tokens. The engine logs `prompt chunk auto: 19968 tokens, a 512-slot ring` at startup, then crashes within a few long-prompt requests. `--prefill auto:16384` (or `8192`) is stable.

## Environment

- Engine: 0.1.40 and 0.1.40.2 (`BUILD.json`, CUDA 13.0, archs 75/86/89/120 + PTX), `source: release`
- GPUs: RTX 3080 Laptop 16 GB + RTX 3070 Laptop 16 GB, driver 616.56, `--layer-split 26` (2 stages)
- CPU: Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4 (14c/28t), 95.8 GiB RAM, Windows
- Model: `Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-abliterated-IQ3_XXS` (47.3 GB shard1 + 28.8 GB shard2, mixed expert types: IQ3_S/IQ4_NL/Q2_0/IQ2_S/IQ2_XS/IQ2_XXS/IQ3_XXS)
- Pack: `native_experts.txt` regenerated with `tools/iq_pack.py --skip-experts` for this image (so the expert offsets match); `dense.bin`/`index.txt` are byte-identical to before
- Other settings: `--trim-stage-weights`, `--pipeline-windows 2`, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.70`, `STRATA_PREFILL_RING=1024`, vision encoder on the CPU (`vision.gpu=false`)

## Question

Is there a buffer in the prefill MoE path sized for a **smaller `T`** than the configured chunk, or a bound that `T * K` can exceed when the chunk is large? The failure being intermittent at the same prompt suggests a size/offset edge rather than a constant out-of-range pointer.

I can attach the engine's own stall dumps (`strata-stall-*.dmp`, written by the issue #29 watchdog) if that helps.

title: sycl: register iq_parity and ple_parity like the top-level build
body:
Fixes #1795.

## What

The port's generic parity loop registered every test as `<test> --selftest`. For `iq_parity` that string became its fixture-directory argument (`argv[1]`), and for `ple_parity` the GGUF/capture-bin relative paths resolved against the build tree — so both failed on every checkout for reasons unrelated to the kernels, exactly as the reporter showed.

This takes `iq` and `ple` out of the `foreach` and gives them the same registrations the top-level `CMakeLists.txt` uses:

- `iq_parity`: the `tools/iq_fixture.py` CTest fixture (generated into the build tree), the same python-with-numpy interpreter probe (`IQ_FIXTURE_PYTHON` overrides it), `FIXTURES_SETUP`/`FIXTURES_REQUIRED`, and exit-3 as a skip. The test itself runs as `iq_parity <build>/iq_fixture`.
- `ple_parity`: `WORKING_DIRECTORY` = the engine root so the binary's documented relative defaults (`pack/full`, `bench/micro`, `../../Q2_0/...`) resolve; `--in`/`--out` from a `STRATA_PLE_FIXTURE_DIR` cache path (default `bench/micro`), plus new `STRATA_PLE_GGUF` and `STRATA_PLE_PACK` configure-time inputs for the artifacts the reporter asked to name.

Missing inputs stay a hard error inside the test, as the top-level build intends — this only makes the error satisfiable, and `docs/INTEL.md`'s parity table now names the variables.

## Checked

- `ctest -N` on the exact parity block (stubbed `strata_resolve`/targets): `iq_parity_fixtures` + `iq_parity` and `ple_parity` each register exactly once; with `-DSTRATA_PLE_GGUF`/`STRATA_PLE_PACK` the command line gains `--gguf`/`--pack`, without them it is clean of stray arguments; the fixtures command is `<python> <root>/tools/iq_fixture.py --out <build>/iq_fixture`.
- Not run: a real `ctest` — this machine has no SYCL toolchain; the registration logic is what changed, and it is verified to mirror the top-level contract. A port user can confirm with the issue's repro (`ctest -R '^(iq|ple)_parity$'`).

title: qsa_select: prompt-path block scores with a thread per query head (below sm_80, same bits)
body:
## What

The prompt path's QSA block scores on cards without the TF32 scorer (below sm_80; measured on Turing, sm_75) run on a
new kernel that is 4.6-5.2x faster per call, with bitwise the same scores. sm_80 and newer, HIP, and decode run the
same code as before. `STRATA_SCORES_THREAD=0` turns it off.

Two commits:

1. **A thread per (query, head)** (`block_scores_thread_kernel`). The old kernel scored every (query, key block) with
   a whole warp: 20 shuffles and five 512-byte loads per score. Now each lane keeps one 128-value query head in
   registers, reads each key once from shared memory as a broadcast, and adds its 32 four-value partials in the
   same tree that lane 0 of the old xor-shuffle sum used. Same pairs, same order, so the same bits. The heads are
   summed 0..3 from 0.0f as before, and the tail block keeps `block_scores_tail_kernel`.
2. **Four lanes per query.** Nsight Compute showed the first version bound by the shared-memory pipe
   (`mio_throttle`): one key load per 4 FMAs. The old shuffle tree splits into four quarters that only meet at the
   end, so now four lanes share a query, each holds one quarter of all four heads, one key load feeds 16 FMAs, and
   two xor shuffles finish the same tree. Still the same bits.

New test: `qsa_scores_parity` checks every score of the new kernel against `block_scores_kernel` (normal values, wide
magnitudes with zeros, small integers with ties; up to 262K context), then times both.

## Measured

CMP 50HX (TU102, sm_75, unlocked to RTX 2080 speed), CUDA 13.3, GCC 14.2.

- `qsa_scores_parity`: 141 M scores bitwise identical on both cards.
- Time per call, old warp kernel -> this PR:

  | queries | context | before | after |
  |---:|---:|---:|---:|
  | 1,024 | 140K | 35.9 ms | 6.2 ms |
  | 1,024 | 200K | 52.4 ms | 8.5 ms |

- Why it matters: in an nsys profile of one +4.4K-token prompt at 140K (Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 2x CMP 50HX,
  `--layer-split auto`), `block_scores_kernel` was the largest prompt kernel: 1,045 ms per card, 17 % of the time.
- Whole engine, same setup: a coding-agent session from 34K to 190K tokens (36 turns, +~4.4K tokens each, greedy,
  fresh server per run) gave word-for-word the same text as before. Time to first token at 190K went from 10.49 s to
  7.13 s, but that number also includes the tokenizer change in #1823; the scorer's own share was not split out.

Note: measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. The patch applies to current `main` without changes; re-measuring on 0.1.41
is still to do. Volta and Pascal (the experimental build) also take this kernel and were not tested.

## How to check

On an sm_75 card: `qsa_scores_parity` (also in ctest). It prints `PASS` when every score matches, and the time of both
kernels.

title: cpu: Q2_0 rows on AVX-only CPUs (q2_avx1.cpp) instead of ggml-cpu's scalar dot
body:
## What

The older-CPU build (`STRATA_ISA_FLOOR=avx`) on an AVX-only CPU (Sandy / Ivy Bridge, Xeon E5 v1/v2): a native pack's
Q2_0 expert rows run on a new AVX kernel (`src/kernels/cpu/q2_avx1.cpp`) instead of ggml-cpu's Q2_0 `vec_dot`, which
is scalar on x86. Bitwise the same results as the scalar reference. AVX2 / AVX-512 CPUs and CPUs without AVX run the
same code as before.

## Why

In the IQ3_XXS pack, Q2_0 is the down projection of 30 of the 48 layers, so on these CPUs most CPU expert work went
through a scalar loop.

## Change

- `q2_native_kernels()` also accepts an AVX-only CPU (`cpu_avx1_ok()`).
- `q2_rows_any`: AVX-512 -> AVX2 -> **AVX1 (new)** -> scalar. `act_quant_any` uses a scalar Q8_1 quantizer without AVX2.
- `q2_0_gguf_rows_multi_avx1`: compiled with `-mavx` / `/arch:AVX` only (no FMA). The 2-bit codes are unpacked once
  per block for all tokens; SSSE3 `maddubs` / `madd` integer dots (exact: a pair sums to at most 762, no saturation);
  an exact half -> float; the float steps in the scalar order, so the bits equal `q2_0_gguf_rows_multi_scalar`.
- The router lookahead keeps 0.1.41's `kq_avx1.cpp`.
- New test `q2_avx1_parity` (ctest; exit 77 without AVX).

## Measured

2x Xeon E5-2670 v2 (Ivy Bridge-EP), GCC 14.2:

- `q2_avx1_parity`: bitwise equal to the scalar reference for all 65,536 half scales and 216 random cases (1-12
  tokens, partial row ranges, padded and unaligned rows, edge and zero-scale activations).
- One expert's down rows (2560 x 640) on one core:

  | tokens | scalar | AVX1 |
  |---:|---:|---:|
  | 1 | 3.86 ms | 0.41 ms (9.4x) |
  | 4 | 13.2 ms | 0.78 ms (16.9x) |

Measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. On current `main` (0.1.41) it was checked on a Ryzen 7 5700X with
`STRATA_FORCE_ISA=avx`: `q2_avx1_parity` passes (12.5x over scalar at 1 token), and so do all CPU tests.

title: tokenizer: a long message's ids remembered whole, on top of the piece cache
body:
## What

`tools/strata_tokenizer.py`: on top of 0.1.41's piece cache, a long piece of text between special tokens (one chat
message, 1,024+ characters) keeps its ids too. The ids are the same; only the work is skipped. At most 256 texts are
kept, and the cache is cleared when full.

## Why

An agent sends its whole conversation again every turn. The piece cache skips the BPE merges of repeated pieces, but
the pre-tokenizer regex still runs over the whole conversation each turn. Text between special tokens is already
encoded on its own, so a message seen before can return its ids directly.

## Measured

2.5 GHz Xeon E5-2670 v2, before the piece cache existed (fork based on 0.1.38): at a 190K-token conversation,
encoding took 1.06 s per turn before and 0.042 s with this cache. The ids were identical on all 36 turns of a
coding-agent session (34K -> 190K tokens).

How much this adds on top of the piece cache alone was **not measured yet**: the piece cache already removes the
merges, so the gain is the regex pass over the old messages.

`tools.test_strata_tokenizer` and `serve.test_detok` pass.

title: prefill: gate/up MMQ reads the experts in place (CUDA; patched copy of llama.cpp mmq.cuh)
body:
## What

CUDA builds, native i-quant packs, prompt path: the gate/up MMQ product reads each expert's weights where they
already are (expert cache slot or stream ring slot) instead of copying them into a group buffer first. Same bytes into
the same kernel, so the same results. `STRATA_MMQ_INPLACE=0` turns it off. HIP builds keep the old path.

## Why

Before MMQ, the prompt path copied every routed expert's gate/up and down rows into a contiguous group buffer,
resident experts included. An expert blob is already "gate rows then up rows", the exact matrix MMQ wants, so the
gate/up copy is only there because MMQ takes one base pointer and a fixed stride.

## Change

- **llama.cpp is not edited.** CMake writes a copy of the pinned `mmq.cuh` into the build tree with one change in its
  three tile loops: a negative expert stride means `x` is a table of expert pointers. The MMQ instance files (and the
  headers that include `mmq.cuh`) compile against that copy. Configure stops if the patched text is not found exactly
  three times (a different llama.cpp). The changed lines are inside kernel templates, so `quantize.cu`, which sees
  the original header, is unaffected.
- **Prompt path:** a complete group's gate/up MMQ gets a table of expert pointers (`m.grp_ptrs`, written on the
  stream by `group_ptrs`). The group's ring slots are released after the gate/up MMQ instead of after the gather.
- **Down rows keep their copy on purpose:** MMQ reads one tile past a 640-value matrix's last row, and that must be
  the zeroed tail (`MMQ_TAIL`), not the next cache slot.
- A flush forced inside a group (a skipped ring entry) copies both, as before.

## Measured

2x CMP 50HX (sm_75), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, `--layer-split auto`, one +4.4K-token prompt at 140K context (nsys):

| | before | after |
|---|---:|---:|
| `copy16_group_kernel`, GPU 0 | 75.5 ms | 31.9 ms |
| `copy16_group_kernel`, GPU 1 | 77.0 ms | 46.4 ms |
| `mul_mat_q` | 803.6 ms | 804.8 ms |
| engine read time | 6,792 ms | 6,746 ms (-0.7 %) |

A coding-agent session from 34K to 190K tokens (36 turns) gave word-for-word the same text as before.

The gain on this box is small because it is PCIe Gen2 and the second GPU waits on PCIe; a card where the copies are
a bigger part of the prompt should gain more, but that was not measured.

Note: measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. The patch applies to current `main` without changes; re-measuring on 0.1.41
is still to do. Only sm_75 was tested.

## How to check

Build (configure must pass the patch check), then compare a prompt's output and read time with
`STRATA_MMQ_INPLACE=0` and without it: the output should be the same.

title: qsa_prompt_attn: int8 K/V prefetched in registers and sharing one buffer (Turing / sm_75)
body:
## What

Turing (sm_75) only, `--kv int8` only: the prompt attention kernel that Turing runs (v1, `qsa_prompt_attn.cu`) gets
faster with the same output bits. Other GPUs and other KV modes run the same code as before.

## Why

On Turing the v1 kernel used 37.9 KB of shared memory per 128-thread block, so only one block fit on an SM (4 warps,
12.5 % of what an SM can hold). Each 32-cell chunk also loaded its scattered K and V rows only after the previous
chunk had finished. Nsight Compute on a CMP 50HX (TU102, RTX 2080 Ti class) showed `long_scoreboard` (waiting on
global loads) as the top stall.

## Change

1. **The next chunk's int8 K/V rows and scales go into registers while the current chunk computes**, then are stored
   where the old gather stored them. (sm_80+ uses `cp.async` for this; Turing does not have it.)
2. **K and V share one shared-memory buffer.** K is read only by the scores and V only by `p·v`, so V is written over
   K after the scores' barrier; the softmax's barrier keeps it before `p·v`. 37.9 -> 29.2 KB per block: **two blocks
   per SM** instead of one.

The same bytes land in the same places and the arithmetic is unchanged, so the results are bitwise the same.

`qsa_prompt_attn_parity` now also prints a checksum of the new kernel's output, so two builds can be compared bit
for bit.

## Measured

CMP 50HX (sm_75, unlocked to RTX 2080 speed, 20 GB), CUDA 13.3, GCC 14.2.

`qsa_prompt_attn_parity`, int8, 2,048 queries:

| context | before | after | change |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 40K | 21.45 ms | 12.91 ms | -40 % |
| 140K | 21.94 ms | 13.31 ms | -39 % |

All output checksums (int8 and fp16, at 4K / 40K / 140K) match the old kernel.

Whole engine: Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, 2x CMP 50HX with `--layer-split auto`, 2x Xeon E5-2670 v2. A coding-agent session
grew from 34K to 190K tokens over 36 turns (+~4.4K tokens per turn, greedy, fresh server per run). The text of all 36
turns was identical to the old build. Incremental prompt read time went down 3.5 % (median per-turn ratio 0.965), and
decode did not change.

Note: these numbers were measured on a fork based on 0.1.38. The patch applies to current `main` without changes;
re-measuring on 0.1.41 is still to do.

## How to check

On an sm_75 card, before and after:

```
qsa_prompt_attn_parity 40000 2048
qsa_prompt_attn_parity 140000 2048
```

The `new output checksum` lines should be equal and the time per chunk lower.

title: fix(cpu): make IQ expert dispatch independent of draft grouping
body:
Adding drafts to an expert group can switch CPU kernels and change the same token's rounding (#152), even with correct window boundaries and rollback. Use the existing STRATA_IQ_MT_MIN=1 behavior by default for IQ gate/up and IQ4_NL down. Explicit 2 retains legacy behavior.

Regression tests now exercise actual default dispatch at widths 1-8 with rotated groups, cover down projection, and remove the override that masked the bug. They fail on the old code and pass on AVX2 and AVX-512. CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds pass; CUDA/HIP synthetic GPU parity passes. All 14 model runs matched full 128-token outputs, including two zero-draft references.

This deliberately changes default rounding for correctness. It is not free: the Zen 4 IQ2_XS one-token expert microbenchmark is 67.9% slower; this is not a measured whole-model slowdown. Remote overlap, deep pipelines and rollback state are outside this fix. No changes from #1748 or #1773 are duplicated.

Full reproduction, raw logs, timings and limitations: bench/results/2026-10-10-draft-independent-iq/README.md.

title: serve: heartbeat a request that waits for the turn (#1619)
body:
Fixes #1619.

## Summary

Queued single-turn requests send an immediate heartbeat, then wait with `Lock.acquire(timeout=FIFO_PING_S)`. The turn can start as soon as the holder releases it, without a polling sleep between requests. Closing a queued generator also returns its queued count.

The heartbeat interval remains 10 s by default (`STRATA_FIFO_PING_S` overrides it). Batch requests and status/history cleanup under the held lock are unchanged. No strict FIFO ordering guarantee is added.

Thanks to DDK00011 for reproducing the regressions and proposing the timed wait and queued cleanup. The test lock now accepts the real lock's `timeout` argument.

## Test plan

- New wake-up and generator-close regressions fail on the previous PR head and pass with the correction.
- `serve.test_quiet_cancel`: 6 failing assertions before the correction; all 5 tests pass afterward.
- Full `serve/` discovery: 596 tests, no failures or errors, 8 skips (Linux, Python 3.14.7).
- Not tested: GPU inference or external clients with idle timeouts. The suite uses CPU mocks and the native-pipe stand-in.

title: Session RESTARTS COMPUTER after 25-30 mins (gfx1100)

Using DeepSeek Harness, IQ3_S quantization, 262144 context. Performance is great, but computer restarts after about 25-30 minutes. No blue screen, no visible motive, just a sudden restart.

I've done stress tests, ran Qwen 27B in llama.cpp while running occt stress test on memory and cpu, pushed the thermals to the limit - nothing happens, system is rock solid, stable, everything works fine. title: Opt-in OTLP traces of every /v1 request (0.1.41), plus the docs pages 0.1.41 left uncovered
body:
## Title
Opt-in OTLP traces of every /v1 request (0.1.41), plus the docs pages 0.1.41 left uncovered

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary
Adds the opt-in OTLP tracing that 0.1.41 shipped in `serve/` as a tested, documented feature, and covers the 0.1.41 behaviors no page documented: one trace per `/v1` request exported as OTLP/HTTP JSON, the switches no page listed, the watchdog/body-cap/batch-groups behaviors, the AMD/Linux card order, and the markdown hygiene around them. Off by default: with no endpoint set, the request path is byte-identical to the release build.

## What changed
**serve/tracing.py (new)** — one OpenTelemetry trace per request, built from the seconds the Monitor already measures (queue, load, prefill, decode) and exported as OTLP/HTTP JSON on its own thread, so a down collector never blocks a request. A client `traceparent` becomes the root span's parent; every answer carries its own `traceparent`. With tracing on and the monitor off, timings and token counts only — no prompt or answer text reaches a collector. OTLP/HTTP is written as JSON by hand: tracing adds no package to the install. Enable with `--trace-otlp`, `"trace_otlp"` in the run config, or `$STRATA_TRACE_OTLP` ("default" = http://localhost:4318/v1/traces).

**serve/server.py, serve/runconfig.py** — the tracing hooks in the request path (begin/finish, the answer's traceparent header, trace-only records with the monitor off) and the runconfig endpoint validation with the same check the server applies at start.

**serve/test_tracing.py (new, 9 tests)** — collector stand-in, per-request span tree, W3C context both ways, dead-collector survival, endpoint precedence (CLI > config > env), off-by-default. 9/9 pass.

**CMakeLists.txt, sycl/CMakeLists.txt** — pin CMP0169 OLD around the FetchContent of strata_llamacpp (CMake 3.30 deprecates FetchContent_Populate(<name>); CMake 4.4 warns every configure), guarded so CMake < 3.30 still configures.

**docs/** — DETAILS.md: the tracing section and the 0.1.41 switches no page listed, card order on AMD/Linux (KFD topology SIMDs x clock), STRATA_DUMP_FIRST_LOGITS next to the research hooks, markdown hygiene (spaced table delimiters, fenced code with a language, the tier figure as a markdown image). TROUBLESHOOTING.md: the tracing row, the watchdog/body-cap/batch-groups behaviors, the gcc/glibc row in the table's two-column shape. BATCHING.md, MULTI_GPU.md, SECOND_GPU.md: the batch-groups and card-order rows they were missing.

## Extra Notes
Tested on Python 3.15 (venv), no GPU: serve.test_tracing 9/9; serve.test_server + test_monitor + test_runconfig + test_request_accounting 297/297; all together 306/306 on this branch's base (fb58e0d). Tracing is opt-in and the default path is untouched. Not tested: the CMake pins on a CMake < 3.30 machine (the guard is by reading; the 3.30+ warning path is seen on every configure of this build), and the OTLP collector round-trip against a real Jaeger/Tempo.

title: [Bug]: gfx1100 (RX 7900 XTX): verify timeouts and prefill "no progress" from host-page reclaim; HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0 ends them (#649 mechanism, second GPU)
body:
## What happened

Long-context serving on an RX 7900 XTX (gfx1100, Linux) died repeatedly with the two paths this engine already
instruments: the prompt watchdog (`no progress for 60 s … (issue #29)`) and the verify window, whose #649 trace ended in
`RELEASE-NOT-DRAINED`. **Nine engine deaths in one day** (2026-10-08, 10:16 to 23:42), all during long-context work
(positions 31 860 to 200 523 in the trace dumps), all while the box was under memory reclaim. Adding
`"HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM": "0"` to the server JSON `env` block stopped them: the next long run did **283 requests in
4 h 54 m, up to 245 625 tokens, with no hang, no timeout and no watchdog event**.

This is the mechanism already documented in `docs/AMD_HIP.md` ("Linux: verify timeouts while the kernel reclaims host
memory") and reported for the R9700 in #750 — reported here as a second machine, on a different GPU and ROCm version,
with the extra evidence that the two published workarounds are the same mechanism seen from two ends, and with one
detail that is not in the docs: on this box the trigger was Pop!_OS's default `vm.swappiness=180` zram setup.

Two code-level observations at the end, which are the parts that may want a change in Strata rather than in the config.

### Environment

- Engine **0.1.41** for seven of the nine events (the 0.1.40.3 build hung twice earlier the same day, at 10:16 and
  12:47; the upgrade to 0.1.41 was at 16:40), HIP backend
- **RX 7900 XTX 24 GiB (gfx1100)**, one GPU, 125.7 GiB system RAM
- **Pop!_OS 24.04, kernel 7.1.5-76070105-generic**, ROCm from the pip wheels: `7.10.0a20251120`
  (`_rocm_sdk_core` / `_rocm_sdk_devel` / `_rocm_sdk_libraries_gfx110X_dgpu`), hipBLASLt tuning table
  `tools/hip/gfx1100-hipblaslt-100200.txt`
- Model: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next **UD-IQ4_XS** (unsloth-UD), 48 layers, 12 full-attention (`layer % 4 == 3`), native GGUF in
  place, `--resident-budget-gib 55` (resident RAM mode: 40.65 GiB page-locked experts), `--max-context 262144`,
  `--kv q4_0 --kv-resident 32768`, `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --batch-mtp`, `parallel: 2`, `--batch 2`
- `env` at the time of the failures: `STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING`, `GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576` (already set from
  the #920 note), plus the diagnostics named below

### Symptom — two distinct classes, both fatal

Class A, the prompt path (watchdog stops the engine, exit `-6`):

```
strata serve: no progress for 60 s during a request (reading the prompt (batched): waiting for the GPU (attention,
  router) at layer 9 of the prompt chunk from token 106496) - stopping the engine so the server starts it again (issue #29)
strata serve: stall report (engine 0.1.41): stage "reading the prompt (batched): waiting for the GPU (attention, router)
  at layer 9 of the prompt chunk from token 106496" for 60 s; 0 layers …
  expert pool: epoch 610306, batch epoch 610306: 48 of 48 jobs claimed, 48 done; 15 of 15 workers parked, 15 sleeping
  verify window (last window, not the current stage): 4 tokens at position 192288, host at layer step 48; the GPU rang
  48; flags: served 48, plan (A) 48, copies (B) 48
strata verify trace: GPU breadcrumbs (us after the window's first), the GPU got as far as layer 48:
```

The device had completed all 48 layers (`48 of 48 jobs claimed, 48 done`, `the GPU rang 48`) while the host sat in the
prompt path for 60 s.

Class B, the verify window (the server ends the engine; the console adds that the waits were released and the GPU did not
finish within 5 s):

```
   5000640.1 TIMEOUT              v0x7ffd21865680 window 331 step 4 layer 4 aux 600 | seq 4 flag 4 A 4 B 4
   5000130.7 RELEASE              v0x7ffd21865680 window 331 step -1 layer -1 aux 5000 | seq 4 flag 4 A 4 B 4
         0.0 RELEASE-NOT-DRAINED  v0x7ffd21865680 window 331 step -1 layer -1 aux 5000 | seq 4 flag 4294967295 A … B …
strata verify trace: GPU breadcrumbs (us after the window's first), the GPU got as far as layer 4:
```

Nine events on 2026-10-08 (times are the restart the server did right after each):

| restart after | engine | class | where it stopped |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10:16:24 | 0.1.40.3 | A | stage `(request -1)` |
| 12:47:43 | 0.1.40.3 | A | prefill layer 43, chunk from token 82 501 |
| 17:31:54 | 0.1.41 | A | prefill layer 19, chunk from token 8 192 |
| 18:43:46 | 0.1.41 | A | stage `(request -1)` |
| 19:47:18 | 0.1.41 | A | stage `(decode -1)` |
| 20:56:01 | 0.1.41 | B | window 3761 — **RELEASE-DRAINED** (the GPU finished the rest after release) |
| 22:57:39 | 0.1.41 | B | window 919, layer 10 — RELEASE-NOT-DRAINED |
| 23:21:22 | 0.1.41 | A | prefill layer 9, chunk from token 106 496 |
| 23:48:59 | 0.1.41 | B | window 331, layer 4 — RELEASE-NOT-DRAINED |

The two classes differ in one measurable way, which is what makes them worth separating: after the sentinel release,
class A's GPU work is already done (the host had not seen the ring), class B's never drains (the device was still inside
the step).

### Evidence

1. **Where class B freezes.** Both `RELEASE-NOT-DRAINED` events stopped at the same point in the layer, and the trace
   names it. At 22:57 the same window recorded `out-proj(16)=20628.0 router+ring(…)` for layer 8 and
   `out-proj(16)=22180.5 router+ring(…)` for layer 9, then layer 10 recorded
   `pre(0)=23267.0 … out-proj(16)=23468.0` and **no `router+ring` marker at all** — i.e. it stopped inside the publish of
   that layer's ring to host memory (`verify.cpp:310` names marker 17 `router+ring`). At 23:42 the same: layers 2 and 3
   recorded their markers, layer 4 ended at `out-proj(16)=5636.6` with no `router+ring`. The stall was 23.5 ms and 5.6 ms
   into the window respectively, then nothing for the whole timeout.
2. **The host was not blocked.** A 250 ms sampler over `/proc/<pid>/task/*/stat` (30 MB of dumps) shows the main thread
   `STATE=R WCHAN=0` with ~100 jiffies/turn during every class-A stall: spinning on a ring the device had already
   written, one core saturated, no thread in `D`, `io wait causes` all zero.
3. **Reclaim was happening.** `PSI memory some avg10=5.55%` at the 23:42 hang (0.00% now); the engine reported
   `32 838 major page faults` and `687 MiB in swap`; ~9.4 GiB of the box was in zram swap; `vm.swappiness=180`
   (Pop!_OS default via `/usr/bin/pop-zram-config`).
4. **The driver said so too.** `journalctl -k` carries `amdgpu_amdkfd_restore_userptr_worker 3884: restore worker
   triggers a page restore failed` and `svm_range_restore_pages ... invalid node` in clusters at 10:11, 11:27–11:37,
   12:43 and 17:22 — each before a hang. **Zero since 23:48.** (Caveat: those lines print on count doubling, so silence
   is weak evidence.)
5. **Not context length.** The verify-window dumps of these events carry positions from 31 860 up to 200 523, while 320
   requests in 128–192 k and 8 above 192 k succeeded that day, and the longest clean prompt that evening was 203 908
   tokens. Failure counts track tokens processed, not context size.

## What was ruled out, one variable at a time

Each row is a separate restart of the server with one change, judged on the same workload.

| change | result | what it rules out |
|---|---|---|
| `STRATA_PF_STEP_SYNC=1` (diagnostic) | hangs continued; it named the stalls: 19 585 ms and 8 718 ms prompt steps against a 250 ms log threshold | nothing — but it produced the step names above |
| `STRATA_VERIFY_TRACE=1` (#649 trace) | produced the TIMEOUT / RELEASE breadcrumbs and the layer markers | nothing — it is the instrument |
| ZFS ARC capped to 16 GiB (`zfs_arc_max`) | the 22:57 event was still RELEASE-NOT-DRAINED, `MemAvailable` 87 GiB at the time | ARC growth / ZFS reclaim as the only trigger |
| `STRATA_DOORBELL_STORE=1` | class B returned (23:42) | the read-modify-write ring increment as the whole story — and see observation 2: it cannot reach the class-A path |
| `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=0` (plain hc read) | class B returned (23:42) | the split hc staging path (same finding as #649, which sets this too) |
| `HIP_HOST_COHERENT=1` | class B returned (23:42) | non-coherent host mappings as the mechanism |
| single request, no concurrency | the 18:43 event happened on a single request anyway | `parallel: 2` / `--batch 2` / `--batch-mtp` as a precondition |
| disk I/O left saturated (`PSI io` 63–85% for 18 h from an unrelated `git lfs pull`) | clean for 4 h 54 m under it | block I/O contention as the trigger |
| `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0` | **clean** | — |

## The fix, and the paired numbers

```json
"env": {
  "STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING": "tools/hip/gfx1100-hipblaslt-100200.txt",
  "GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE": "1048576",
  "HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM": "0"
}
```

Before (same machine, same model, same args, 17:22–23:42): 7 engine deaths in ~6 h 20 m, longest clean gap 74 min,
prompt reads 614–1 128 tok/s, prompt-step outliers to 19 585 ms.

After (engine 0.1.41, 06:11:21 → 11:05): **4 h 54 m, 283 requests, median prompt 72 242 tokens, largest 245 625,
25 requests above 150 k, zero hangs, zero timeouts, zero prompt-step outliers, zero engine deaths.** Four cold full
prompts in that window: 203 272 tokens in 209 982 ms (968 tok/s), 204 295 in 211 431 ms (966), 205 311 in 211 132 ms
(972), 212 721 in 229 558 ms (927). Decode 34.8–40.4 tok/s with `--spec 4` drafts accepted (e.g. 266 of 320), which
matches the pre-change decode rate. `PSI memory` 0.00%, kernel userptr-restore warnings 0.

Two honest caveats about attribution:

1. **Two changes landed 12 seconds apart.** `swapoff -a` at 23:48:28 and the `env` edit, with the engine starting at
   23:48:58. Both act on the same mechanism — the kernel moving host pages the GPU can see — so the finding is
   "one mechanism, two mitigations", not "switch X". Swap was re-enabled at 11:49 with `vm.swappiness=20` and the
   switch left in; that run was clean for its first 29 minutes, which is the useful configuration and still short.
2. **Speed parity was not measured as a pair.** The switch has not been removed since, so I cannot quote a
   with/against number like the #750 report does; the 927–972 tok/s above is a before/after comparison across
   different prompt mixes, not an interleaved A/B.

A structural change I can see from userland, which supports the mechanism: with the switch on, the engine's `VmRSS`
fell from 78–94 GiB to 6.3 GiB while the log still reports `resident RAM mode: 40.65 GiB of experts in RAM
(page-locked)` and the decode hit rate stays 84–89.5%, and `Unevictable`/`Mlocked` stay at 8 MiB. The 40 GiB appears to
be held outside the process's page tables now (about 57 GiB of `used` memory is not attributed to any process or to
`/proc/meminfo` categories), i.e. it is no longer paged host memory the kernel may move. That is an inference from
accounting, not a driver counter.

## Two things in Strata that look like bugs

1. **`death_note()` only scans the last 4096 bytes of the log** (`serve/server.py:781-796`). With
   `STRATA_VERIFY_TRACE=1` the trace dumps are ~30 KB, so the `issue #29` line is pushed out of the tail and the server
   reports the fallback "running out of RAM" note for what was a caught hang. It sent me chasing memory for an hour.
   Either scan further back or keep the last watchdog line as state.
2. **`STRATA_DOORBELL_STORE` only covers the verify path.** `g_doorbell_store` is read in `src/core/verify.cpp:130` and
   applied at `:1339`, but the prompt path publishes through `doorbell_ring()` (`src/core/layer.cpp:391` →
   `src/kernels/cuda/elementwise.cu:428`, kernel at `:209`), which is an unconditional increment. So the A/B switch
   cannot test the class-A path at all, and the banner ("doorbell stored") reads as if it had. The comment at
   `elementwise.cu:189` about the cloned-literal host expression suggests the same fix applies there.

## What I did not test

- No second machine, no other ROCm version, no other card; one box, one GPU, one model.
- No controlled speed A/B for the switch (see caveat 2), and no output-equality check like the #750 report's five paired
  runs — I did not verify byte-identical answers with and without it.
- No GPU regression suite, no `rocm-smi` reset comparison, no driver downgrade/upgrade test.
- Windows: not applicable (this is the Linux/HIP path).
- Whether class A and class B are one fault or two; the breadcrumb evidence points at the same publish-to-host-memory
  point, but class A never produced a `RELEASE-` line to compare against.

## Suggested doc addition

`docs/AMD_HIP.md` lists the two workarounds separately. On zram distributions they are one thing: Pop!_OS ships
`vm.swappiness=180` via `/usr/bin/pop-zram-config`, which maximises exactly the page movement that suspends the queues.
Worth a line: "on a zram box, check `vm.swappiness` too — and note that `swapoff -a` on Pop!_OS leaves swap disabled
until reboot, because `pop-zram-config` exits early when `/dev/zram0` already exists."

## Related

#649 (same symptom, gfx1030, same model family, also runs `STRATA_HC_SPLIT=0`), #1103 (gfx1030 verify timeouts fixed by
a ROCm wheel change), #884 / #1691 (gfx906), #872 (gfx1100 7900 XTX, IQ3_S at 262 144, whole-machine restarts on
Windows), #750 and #920 in `docs/AMD_HIP.md`.

## Engine log

`strata-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs.log` attached: 14 565 lines, 2026-10-08 00:00:51 → 2026-10-09 11:18:43, covering all nine
events and the clean run after the fix. Checked before attaching: it holds prompt token counts, layer numbers, timings
and the engine command line (so, file paths) — no prompt or completion text.

title: Add Jetson Orin ARM64 support and shared-memory budgeting
body:
ARM64 hosts currently encounter x86-specific build and CPU assumptions, and Jetson Orin needs cache sizing that accounts for CPU and GPU sharing physical RAM. This adds native ARM64 build/setup support, portable CPU paths, and integrated-device memory handling, validated on a Jetson AGX Orin Developer Kit 32 GB with JetPack 6.2, CUDA 12.6 and SM87.

Related: #1306. This validates Orin; GB10 hardware was not tested.

## Changes

- Select ARM64 CPU sources and guard x86 intrinsics; retain the existing x86 paths and activation contracts.
- Discover ARM CUDA devices through the driver API and preserve JetPack CUDA libraries during local installation.
- Budget integrated-device expert caches against physical RAM, leaving six GiB headroom and a separate three GiB late-workspace reserve under automatic sizing; retain explicit user overrides.
- Handle mapped/pinned memory limitations, add portable tests and platform probes, and fix the position-zero single-token execution sentinel.
- Include reproducible validation and same-day context comparison evidence under `bench/results/2026-10-07-jetson-orin` and `bench/results/2026-10-08-jetson-orin`.

## Validation

- Full Release CUDA SM87 build on upstream 0.1.41; 102 eligible CTest cases passed across the initial suite and targeted rerun. Three legacy fixture-dependent cases are excluded.
- Real Coder IQ1_M native expert checks across all 48 layers and seven real-model API checks passed, including streaming and cancellation recovery.
- Jetson setup: 15 cases; desktop setup: 111 cases; x86 CPU/router cross-build passed.
- Full Release HIP gfx1100 build with MMQ and tests enabled, and full Release SYCL SPIR-V build with parity targets enabled, passed on `maestro1` (Celeron N3450, x86-64 Ubuntu 22.04). Toolchains: AMD TheRock `7.10.0a20251120` / Clang 22 and Intel DPC++ 2026.1.1 / oneMKL 2026.1.0. Both binaries loaded and printed help. The HIP shared-memory budget test passed; three AVX-512-dependent CPU checks skipped on this host.
- Same-day original-port versus rebased-port sweep: all 18 cells at context capacities 1K–256K preserved six GiB physical headroom. 156 matched throughput requests, nine near-limit requests and nine recovery checks completed.
- At 256K, the rebased build read 261,936 prompt tokens in 4,480.2 seconds and generated 64 tokens at 6.6 tokens/s, with at least 9.33 GiB available physical RAM. Swap was in use; clocks were not locked. Automatic cache allocations differed, so these are configuration observations rather than isolated kernel comparisons.

Detailed methods, raw outputs and limitations: [validation report](https://github.com/calvinvette/strata-inference-orin/blob/feat/jetson-orin-arm64/bench/results/2026-10-08-jetson-orin/README.md).

Backend compiler versions, complete build logs, commands, library loading checks and setup fixture exclusions: [maestro1 build report](https://github.com/calvinvette/strata-inference-orin/blob/feat/jetson-orin-arm64/bench/results/2026-10-08-maestro1-builds/README.md). These checks required no engine source changes.

## Remaining validation

HIP/SYCL GPU tests and model execution, desktop GPU runtime, Windows, other models and GB10 were not tested. The x86 builds check compilation and linking; they do not validate ARM HIP/SYCL hosts or extend the Orin performance results to other GPUs. Desktop inference output byte identity remains unverified. Long-context execution does not establish recall accuracy or numerical equivalence across the full window.

title: Windows: cap conversation-memory admission at the commit limit too (#1607)
body:
Fixes #1607.

The conversation-cache/checkpoint admission reads `ullAvailPhys` only, so it admits allocations the **commit limit** (RAM + page file) then refuses — the engine exits `0xC0000409` with no message even with GiB of physical RAM free. Under WDDM the card's VRAM is charged to the commit too (#141), and the reporter reproduced the crash 6 times, every time within 0.1 GiB of the limit.

## Change

`conversation_available_memory()` on Windows now returns `min(ullAvailPhys, ullAvailPageFile)` — the same pair `host_available_memory` already exposes to the expert-source path. It never admits *more* than today (when the page file is generous, physical RAM is still the bound); the admission floor logic is untouched, and Linux still reads `MemAvailable`. The two parking log lines drop the word "physical" since the bound can now be the commit charge.

## Test plan

- `x86_64-w64-mingw32-g++ -fsyntax-only` on `conversation_memory.cpp` and `_conversation_memory_test.cpp`: the `_WIN32` TU type-checks against real windows.h.
- Native build + run of `conversation_memory_test`: 23 checks pass; the Windows-specific check (`*available <= ullTotalPhys`) still holds since the bound only tightens.
- `g++ -fsyntax-only` on the Linux path: unchanged, clean.

Not tested: the actual 0xC0000409 crash on Windows (no Windows box here) — the change only tightens admission, and the reporter's trace ties every crash to the commit boundary this now respects.

title: setup: images on Windows AMD with a hand-built encoder, CPU or Vulkan (#1155)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1155

## Summary
Images on Windows AMD with an image encoder built from `tools/vision`. The CPU build is used for `--vision cpu`. A Vulkan build (`-DGGML_VULKAN=ON`) runs on the Radeon and is used for `--vision gpu`. The ready-made zip still carries no encoder (shipping one in the zip is a separate step). Measured on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S, Windows 11.

This PR now carries only this part. The other changes it had are in their own PRs: #1803, #1804, #1805, #1806, #1807.

## What changed
- **`setup.py`:**
  - `hip_vision()` accepts `--vision cpu` on Windows when a hand-built encoder exists (`engine\`, `build-vision\bin`, `engine\.previous` or `build-vision-vulkan\bin`), and `yes`/`gpu` when the Vulkan build exists.
  - After the engine step, `place_windows_encoder()` puts the right build beside the engine, including after an engine update replaces the folder.
  - Without an encoder, images stay off as before, with a message pointing to the docs.
- **`docs/AMD_HIP.md`:** a new "Images on Windows" section with both builds and the measurements below; the "Differences" line no longer says images are Linux-only.
- **`tools/test_setup_amd.py`:**
  - a hand-built encoder in each place is used;
  - the Vulkan build gives `gpu` and replaces a CPU build beside the engine;
  - no encoder anywhere leaves images off.

Measured (UD-IQ4_XS, 1224 x 1584 phone photos of documents, 1024 image tokens, first read of each picture):

| Photo | CPU encoder | Vulkan encoder |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 5-column settlement statement | 31.7 s, 44/44 amounts | 9.8 s, 44/44 |
| permit list | 27.7 s, permit number exact | 6.2 s, exact |

At the CPU default of 300 tokens, the same statement photo read only 32/44 amounts in the right column, and misread the year.

## Extra Notes
- **Defaults:** without a hand-built encoder setup does exactly what it did before; images are still refused for Windows AMD. Setup-only: no engine, server or CUDA/HIP/SYCL code changes.
- **Related:** #1792 (Hugua700) makes `find_vcvars()` see Visual Studio 2026 for non-CUDA builds; the CPU encoder build needs it on such machines. #1156 was closed in favour of this PR.
- **Tests:** all `serve` and `tools/test_setup_*` test files pass on `main` fb58e0d.

title: Strata on 2x RX 7900 XTX (HIP, AVX-only CPU): Memory access fault by GPU node-2 ... Page not present with concurrent requests  Dates below are day/month (2026), times are local (CEST, UTC+2).
body:
## Summary
With **2 or more concurrent requests** (`"parallel": N`, layer split on two RX 7900 XTX) the engine dies with
`Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: ...) on address 0x7e74...000. Reason: Page not present or supervisor
privilege.` (exit code -6). The server restarts it by itself in 1-2 minutes. The faulting address is always a **host
(system RAM) virtual address**, and the fault always happens **when a conversation enters or leaves a batch slot**: right
after `strata batch: slot N takes ... tokens (copied in ... ms)`, `conversation cache: restored N tokens (checkpoint)` or
`strata batch: slot N gave back N tokens of this conversation (its turn checkpoint)`.
With 4 concurrent sessions it happens every 6-29 minutes. **It still happens on 0.1.41, with the copy engine off
(`HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0`), with `STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1`, and with the KV cache fully in VRAM (no `--kv-resident`).**
With one request at a time it was ~0.5/hour on the old two-socket placement, and 0 in ~3.5 h after moving both GPUs under
the same CPU.

**Side effect: the fault ends in a hardware reset of the card.** Right after the page fault the card's MES firmware stops
answering (`MES failed to response msg=3`, `failed to remove hardware queue from MES`), and amdgpu does a **MODE1 reset**
of that XTX (`VRAM is lost due to GPU reset!`; 9 resets of that card in ~22 h). The reset is then reported to **every ROCm
process on the machine**: four unrelated processes that only use the two MI50s (llama.cpp servers and a PyTorch service,
in other containers that cannot see the XTX) print `HW Exception by GPU node-4 (Agent handle: ...) reason :GPU Hang` at
the same second and exit (status 139 / SIGABRT). So one fault in Strata takes down every GPU service on the box for 1-2
minutes. The MES hang and the reset fan-out are driver/runtime behavior, not Strata's, but they make the fault expensive.
Kernel log below.

## Environment
| | |
|---|---|
| Strata | 0.1.40 / 0.1.40.1 (tests 06-09/10); 0.1.41 (fb58e0d) from 09/10 10:34 |
| Build | `local-hip`, archs gfx1100, `isa_floor: avx` (EXPERIMENTAL older-CPU build), vision cpu |
| GPUs used | 2x Radeon RX 7900 XTX 24 GB (gfx1100), layer split 27 (0-26 / 27-47), `--trim-stage-weights` |
| Other GPUs in the box | 2x Instinct MI50 32 GB (gfx906) running llama.cpp (ROCm 6.1.2), not visible to Strata's container |
| PCIe | Intel S2600CP (C602), PCIe 3.0 x8 slots; each XTX sits behind its own Navi switch |
| CPU / RAM | 2x Xeon E5-2630 v2 (Ivy Bridge, AVX, no AVX2), 12 cores, 2 NUMA nodes, 125 GB DDR3 |
| OS / kernel | Ubuntu 22.04.5, kernel 6.8.0-138-generic, in-kernel amdgpu, `iommu=pt`, `amdgpu.ppfeaturemask=0xffffffff` |
| ROCm | container `rocm/dev-ubuntu-24.04:7.2.4-complete` (engine built and run inside it, `--device /dev/kfd` + 2 render nodes) |
| Model | Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS (ISTA-DASLab), native pack `iq3_xxs`, MTP rt, `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768` |
| Server config | `reasoning_budget_tokens 4096`, `--max-context` 65536 / 131072 / 262144, `parallel` 1-4, `--batch-groups` 1/2/3/auto, optionally `--conversation-cache-mib 16384 --conversation-cache-slots N` |
| THP / NUMA | THP madvise; `kernel.numa_balancing` 1 (also tested with 0) |

## What we measured
| date | config | concurrent | duration | faults |
|---|---|---:|---|---:|
| 06-07/10 | 0.1.39-0.1.40, 64k, parallel 1, XTX on **two sockets** (node 0 + node 1) | 1 | ~15 h | 7 (~0.5/h), always at the start of a request after a pause |
| 08/10 day | 0.1.40, XTX moved under the **same socket**, 64k-262k, parallel 1/2/4, batch-groups 1-2, no parking | 1-4, short tests | ~3.5 h engine time | **0** |
| 08/10 17:38 | 262k, parallel 4, batch-groups 2, **parking 4x16 GiB** | 4 agent sessions | 75 min | **2** (17:58, 18:39), both right after `conversation cache: restored ... (checkpoint)` |
| 09/10 08:38 | same, **no parking** | 4 | ~35 min | **1** after ~15 min, right after `strata batch: slot 2 takes 21599 tokens` |
| 09/10 09:25 | same as 08/10 17:38 (parking) with **`kernel.numa_balancing=0`** | 4 | ~15 min | **1** after ~6 min, right after `conversation cache: parked/restored` |
| 09/10 09:52 | 262k, parallel 3, batch-groups 3, parking 3 | 3 | 22 min | **1** after 22 min |
| 09/10 10:34 | **0.1.41**, 262k, parallel 4, batch-groups auto, parking 4x16 GiB, without `--remote-expert-opt` | 4 | 29 min | **1** after 29 min, right after `conversation cache: restored 26338 tokens (checkpoint)` |
| 09/10 11:06 | 0.1.41, same, parallel 3 | 3 | 24 min | **1** after 24 min, right after `conversation cache: parked` |
| 09/10 11:37 | 0.1.41, 4 at 262k + `STRATA_HIP_ADAPT_KERNEL_COPY=1` (its startup line was in the log) | 4 | 25 min | **1** after 25 min, right after `conversation cache: restored 26552 tokens (checkpoint)` |
| 09/10 12:14 | 0.1.41, 4 at 262k + `HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0` (checked in the engine's `/proc/<pid>/environ`) | 4 | 19 min | **1** after 19 min, right after `conversation cache: restored 30664 tokens (checkpoint)` |
| 09/10 12:42 | 0.1.41, 4 at 262k, **no `--kv-resident`** (KV fully in VRAM, 0 `KV streaming` lines; slot sessions 7.5 GiB per card) | 4 | 30 min | **0** (37 restores, 116 slot admissions) |
| 09/10 13:15 | 0.1.41, same (KV in VRAM) at **131k** | 4 | 27 min | **1** after 27 min, right after `strata batch: slot 2 gave back 25734 tokens of this conversation (its turn checkpoint)` |

Excluded so far: GPUs on different sockets (both XTX now on NUMA node 0), conversation parking (09/10 08:38), automatic
NUMA balancing, the SDMA copy engine (both switches), KV streaming, the 0.1.40 -> 0.1.41 update. With the KV in VRAM the
faults may be somewhat rarer (1 in 57 min of 4-session load, ~120 restores) but they do not stop.

Not yet tested: `HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM=0`, `GPU_PINNED_MIN_XFER_SIZE=1048576`, `--mmap-experts`.
One instance per card (no layer split) could not be judged: it runs, but too slowly on this CPU (see below), so in 10
minutes there were too few slot admissions to say anything about the fault.

## Log excerpts
0.1.41, KV fully in VRAM (no `--kv-resident`), 131k, 4 sessions (09/10 13:42 local):
```
strata batch: slot 0 takes 31592 tokens (copied in 278.8 ms)
strata serve: prompt 31592 tokens = 31591 reused + 1 read in 6 ms (179.1 tok/s), 1 generated in 27 ms (37.5 tok/s), drafts accepted 0 of 0, 0 checkpoints
strata serve: decode expert cache hit rate: 100.0% (480 hits / 480 lookups)
strata serve: conversation cache: parked 31592 tokens in 200.5 ms; parked=4 bytes=4109642032 evictions=46 snapshot_bytes=600915304 reused_kv_bytes=0
strata batch: slot 2 gave back 25734 tokens of this conversation (its turn checkpoint) in 253.1 ms
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x94e5490) on address 0x732b48cce000. Reason: Page not present or supervisor privilege.
```
0.1.41, `HSA_ENABLE_SDMA=0`, 262k with KV streaming (09/10 12:33 local):
```
strata serve: conversation cache: dropped 1 superseded copy of this conversation; parked=2
strata serve: conversation cache: parked 56599 tokens in 787.4 ms; parked=3 bytes=3569736360 evictions=15 snapshot_bytes=1220564336 reused_kv_bytes=0
strata serve: conversation cache: restored 30664 tokens (checkpoint) in 230.0 ms; parked=3 bytes=4586586976
Memory access fault by GPU node-2 (Agent handle: 0x8b054a0) on address 0x7a39932e1000. Reason: Page not present or supervisor privilege.
```
0.1.40, numa_balancing=0 (09/10 09:34 local):
```
strata serve: conversation cache: restored 30012 tokens (checkpoint) in 192.5 ms; parked=4 bytes=7663099208
strata batch: slot 0 takes 31087 tokens (copied in 540.8 ms)
```

title: sycl: pin the PCIe probe's source buffer (fixes multi gpu layer split)
body:
Relates to #485 (the probe's reading sets `pcie_frac`). Not a fix for #1054: that startup wedge on a 2-card split has a different mechanism (the host-mirror fill).

## Summary
`probe_pcie_h2d_gbps` copies from a pageable 256 MiB source. On two Arc Pro B60s with `--layer-split auto` the copy engine faults at a fixed VA in the driver's pool region (`0xffffc001ffa10000`): hundreds of `bcs VM_NOT_FOUND` faults at FaultLevel 4 (the top-level page-table entry is absent, so the VA range was never mapped in that VM), the load wedges, and no window ever starts. Measured 755 and 747 faults in two runs; intermittent on fresh boots, and observed on a layer split (a single-card start was not exercised).

## What changed
`sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`, `probe_pcie_h2d_gbps`: allocate the source with `sycl::malloc_host` and free it with the matching `sycl::free`. The function's own comment already says it times "copies from pinned host memory, as the expert arena's reads are" - a pageable source contradicted that, and is what the driver stages through its bounce path.

This moves a number the default path uses: the probe feeds `pcie_frac_for_gbps`, so the share of missed experts the GPU reads over PCIe follows the reading. Same build otherwise, one variable changed:

| source | probe | `pcie_frac` | runs |
|---|---|---|---|
| pageable (before) | 13.8 GB/s, best of 13.5-13.8 over 4 bursts | 0.38 | nine |
| pinned (after) | 14.4 GB/s, best of 14.4 over 4 bursts | 0.40 | two |

Both cards sit in x8 slots; above 20 GB/s the share is unchanged, so no x16 machine's default moves.

The buffer is allocated, used and freed inside the probe, so the page-locked footprint is transient (256 MiB for ~0.1 s). On a device without host USM the allocation throws, `DPCT_CHECK_ERROR` catches it, the probe returns `-1.0` and the caller keeps the default share - no new hard failure.

## Extra Notes
Two consecutive loads reached the window cleanly with the pin (2/2); the run log shows the 256 MiB host USM allocation the pageable version never made. Not tested: the AMD SYCL path, a single-card start, an x16 slot. Also removes the now-stale DPCT1124 note above the timed memcpy in the same function (that call waits explicitly).

All the split-fault instrumentation (guard watch, stage stamps and the `STRATA_STAGE_WAIT` serial gate, terminate dumps, coredump grabbers) lives on https://github.com/maxious/Strata_SYCL/tree/scratch/split-fault-instruments
