title: serve/web: add English / Simplified Chinese (zh-CN) UI localization
body:
## Summary / 概述

Adds a lightweight, dependency-free i18n layer to the Strata web control panel (`serve/web/`), so the UI can render in **English** or **Simplified Chinese (zh-CN)**.

为 Strata 网页控制面板（`serve/web/`）加入一套轻量、无依赖的国际化层，界面可显示 **英文** 或 **简体中文（zh-CN）**。

- Default language is auto-detected: `localStorage["strata.lang"]`, else `navigator.language` starting with `zh` → zh-CN, otherwise English.
- A toggle button in the header (next to the theme button) switches languages at runtime; the choice is remembered.
- **English output is byte-identical to before** — English strings are kept as the fallback text, so nothing changes for existing users.

## Files / 改动文件

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `serve/web/i18n.js` | new — runtime (`t`, `apply`, `setLang`, `onChange`) |
| `serve/web/i18n.en.js` | new — English dictionary |
| `serve/web/i18n.zh-CN.js` | new — Simplified Chinese dictionary |
| `serve/web/index.html` | `data-i18n*` attributes, script tags, language button |
| `serve/web/app.js` | dynamic strings via `t()`; `/config` help via `about.cfg.help.<key>` |
| `serve/web/monitor.html` | `data-i18n*` attributes + script tags |
| `serve/web/monitor.js` | dynamic strings via `t()` |

`tokens.css`, `components.css`, `app.css`, `sprite.svg` are **untouched** (SHA-256 identical to upstream).

## Runtime API

```js
window.StrataI18N = {
  lang,                       // "en" | "zh-CN"
  available: ["en", "zh-CN"],
  t(key, vars),               // current dict -> en fallback -> key; {name} interpolation
  apply(root = document),     // data-i18n / -html / -title / -placeholder / -aria; sets <html lang>
  setLang(lang),              // persists to localStorage, applies, dispatches "strata:lang"
  onChange(cb)                // document listener for "strata:lang"
};
```

## Verification / 验证

- Playwright (Chromium): `document.documentElement.lang === "zh-CN"`; header tabs, chat, monitor, about and the runtime-generated **Model settings** form all render Chinese; English still renders exactly as before.
- `node --check` clean on all five JS files.
- Only console message is a pre-existing `favicon.ico` 404.
- All 90 element ids in `index.html` preserved; one id added (`lang-btn`); no class changes, so no layout regression.

## Patch

A `git format-patch` patch (against `main` `82f46a8c8f475f001ad76d92f58f4a4f8ffb0253`, v0.1.40.1) is available — 7 files changed, +1227 / -269.

```sh
git checkout -b i18n-zh-cn 82f46a8c8f475f001ad76d92f58f4a4f8ffb0253
git am 0001-serve-web-add-en-zh-CN-i18n-with-automatic-language-.patch
git push -u origin i18n-zh-cn
```

I can attach the patch file here or open a PR if you prefer.

---

Happy to adjust naming, split the dictionaries, or add more languages if you want.

title: Windows AMD: image input on the CPU and on the GPU through Vulkan, te…
body:
## Title
Windows AMD: image input on the CPU and on the GPU through Vulkan (tested on RX 9070 XT Nitro+)

Issue: N/A (AMD on Windows had no way to enable images)

## Summary
AMD cards on Windows could not use images: setup refused `--vision cpu`, never asked the "Images?" question, and the ready-made HIP engine ships no `strata-vision.exe`. The encoder was also CUDA-only, so there was no GPU option on AMD. This PR lets AMD users on Windows (and Linux) choose no images, the CPU encoder, or a GPU encoder built with Vulkan, compiled locally once.

Tested on an RX 9070 XT Nitro+ (gfx1201), Windows, Ryzen 9 5900X, 80 GB RAM, Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS, Visual Studio 2026 and the Vulkan SDK. Setup with `--vision gpu` compiled the encoder and the server started with images on. The model correctly read `TS20 CP77` and `QUADRA` from a test picture. Text speed stayed at about 50 tok/s with a 70-76% expert-cache hit rate, with and without images. Unit tests pass (102 in `test_setup_amd`, `test_setup_choices`, `test_strata_mcp`).

## What changed
- `setup.py`
  - `hip_vision()` now accepts `cpu` on Windows and returns `gpu` for `gpu`/`yes` (Vulkan encoder) instead of refusing.
  - New `win_hip_vision()`: compiles the encoder once beside the ready-made AMD engine. If the Visual Studio C++ tools or the Vulkan SDK are missing it warns and continues with images off.
  - New `build_vision_vulkan()` and `find_vulkan_sdk()`.
  - Windows AMD setup asks "Images?" (no / CPU / GPU through Vulkan).
  - `build_engine_hip()` dispatches to the CPU or Vulkan encoder build, and its readiness check compares the encoder mode so switching cpu to gpu rebuilds it.
  - The encoder builds call `find_vcvars((13, 3))`, because the Visual Studio version cap exists for CUDA and doesn't apply here. This lets Visual Studio 2026 work.
- `tools/vision/CMakeLists.txt`: new `STRATA_VISION_VULKAN` option (builds ggml-vulkan).
- `tools/strata_mcp.py`: removed the check that rejected `--vision` choices for the AMD backend.
- `tools/test_setup_amd.py`, `tools/test_setup_choices.py`, `tools/test_strata_mcp.py`: updated and added tests.
- `docs/AMD_HIP.md`: images are now supported on Windows AMD.
- `.gitignore`: added the generated `build-vision-vk.bat`.

## Extra Notes
- Compiling needs the Visual Studio C++ tools, and for GPU vision the Vulkan SDK. The first build takes 10-20 minutes. `--vision cpu` needs no SDK.
- Only tested on one machine. Not tested: Linux AMD with the Vulkan encoder, other Radeon cards, or a PC with an integrated GPU. On such a PC Vulkan may pick the wrong device, and `GGML_VK_VISIBLE_DEVICES` may help, but I haven't verified that.
- The install tool in `strata_mcp.py` still rejects AMD on Windows. I left that out of this PR.

title: serve: a queue cap (max_queue) answers 429 + Retry-After instead of queueing without end
body:
Issue: Resolves #1809

## Summary
`"max_queue": N` in `strata-<model>.json` (or `--max-queue N`) lets at most N generation requests wait beyond the running slots. One more gets an immediate **429** with a whole-second `Retry-After` (1-60 s), sent before any byte of the answer, so a streamed request never starts a stream it cannot finish. If it is unset, the queue has no limit, as before; `0` rejects whatever cannot start at once.

The status is 429 and not 503 because litellm and the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs retry a 429 and read it as "busy". litellm cools the deployment down for `Retry-After` and moves to another deployment in the group, or waits and retries when Strata is the only one. A 503 counts as a server failure there.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`
  - **Admission:** `Service.admit()` / `release()` count admitted requests (running and waiting) under `status_lock`. They use a new counter instead of `status["queued"]`, which reads about 0 while `--batch` requests wait on the slots. The counter lives on the Service, so an engine restart (#1012) keeps it.
  - **Where the check runs:** `do_POST` checks right after `begin_request` for `/v1/chat/completions`, `/v1/messages` and `/v1/responses` only, and releases in its `finally`, so every way out (disconnect, `EngineDied`, a 400) frees the place.
  - **Retry-After:** `Service.retry_after()` is the mean `duration_s` of the last 8 finished requests divided by the slots, rounded up and clamped to 1-60 s, or 10 s before any request has finished. It is a whole number because litellm reads it with `int()`.
  - **429 body:** each dialect gets its own error shape (OpenAI `rate_limit_error` / `rate_limit_exceeded`, Anthropic `rate_limit_error`, the Responses error body). `_json` gains an optional `headers` argument for the `Retry-After` header.
  - **Metrics:** `/metrics` gains `totals.rejected`, `live.inflight` and `live.max_queue`, and `/v1/status` `activity` gains `admitted`, `max_queue` and `rejected`. No field was renamed.
  - **Settings:** `--max-queue`; a bad config value stops the start with a message, and the start prints one line when the cap is on.
- `serve/runconfig.py`: `max_queue` is editable from the web page's Model settings (`int>=0`, empty means no limit).
- `serve/test_queue_cap.py`: 25 tests.
  - Unit tests: the capacity, max_queue 0, the release floor, and the Retry-After estimate and clamps.
  - Over HTTP with the fake batch engine: a 429 with an integer `Retry-After` and the right body for all three dialects; a streamed request over the cap gets a JSON 429, not a stream; count_tokens and status are not limited; no limit when unset; the count returns to 0 after a finished, streamed, 400, `EngineDied` and disconnected request.
- `docs/DETAILS.md`: a "Limiting the queue" section with measurements and notes for litellm, the `/metrics` field, and the web-editable key.

## Extra Notes
- **Tests:** `python -m unittest serve.test_queue_cap serve.test_runconfig serve.test_parallel` gives 57 OK on this branch, which is current `main` with the commit on top. The full `serve` suite runs 622 tests; its 7 errors are all `No module named 'regex'` in my Python, in `test_detok` and `test_server`, and none come from this change.
- **Measured** on two RTX 3090s (layer split), UD-Q4_K_XL, 0.1.40.1 with this change, one request at a time:
  - With `max_queue` 2: of 5 requests sent at once, 3 were answered in 5.1, 7.7 and 10.1 s, and 2 got the 429 in under 2 ms.
  - Behind litellm with live traffic and `max_queue` 4: the `Retry-After` it sent over 5,379 rejections had a median of 8 s and a maximum of 31 s.
  - Over 10.6 hours it answered 3,885 requests and rejected 3,154 attempts, litellm's retries included.
- **Related:** #1619 / #1673 (a ping while a request waits for the turn) tackles the other side of the same wait. #1673 keeps a waiting client alive, and this PR limits how many can wait. They merge without conflicts, and with both applied, `serve.test_queue_cap`, `serve.test_parallel` and `serve.test_server` (including #1673's `QueuedHeartbeat`) pass; the only errors are the same `regex` ones.
- **Open questions:**
  - Requests from Strata's own web page count toward the cap. The page already shows the server's message ("the queue is full ...; retry after N s").
  - The estimate ignores how long the running requests have already gone. Under load they are often past the mean, so subtracting it would give 1 s and spend a client's retries in seconds.
  - With several slots, prompts are still read one at a time, so the estimate is rough there.

title: [Feature]: a queue cap that answers 429 + Retry-After instead of queueing without end
body:
### What do you want to do?

Run Strata behind a proxy (litellm) that sends it more requests than it can serve, and have Strata say "busy, come back in N s" once its queue is long enough, instead of queueing every request without end.

Today every request waits its turn, however many there are. On two RTX 3090s (Unsloth UD-Q4_K_XL, 0.1.40.1, `"parallel": 4`) with live agent traffic (about 16K prompt tokens and 240 output tokens per request), the queue reached about 22 requests and one 45K-token prompt waited more than 6 minutes. Clients time out while they wait, and a proxy in front cannot tell "busy" from "slow", so it cannot send the overflow to another server.

The workaround today is to limit concurrency in the proxy, e.g. litellm's `max_parallel_requests`. That has to be tuned per box, it knows nothing about Strata's slots, and it does not cover clients that talk to Strata directly.

What would help: a setting such as `"max_queue": N`, so that a request beyond the running slots + N gets an immediate HTTP 429 with a `Retry-After` header. A 429 is what litellm and the OpenAI and Anthropic SDKs already retry, and litellm also uses it to fail over to another deployment. A 503 would make litellm treat the server as broken. The default would stay "no limit".

PR #1808 implements this; it runs on that box now.

title: bench: RX 9060 XT IQ2_XS and IQ3_XXS community results
body:
## Summary
Community measurements on a Windows desktop with an RX 9060 XT 16 GB, Ryzen 7 9800X3D and 64 GB RAM, using the packaged Strata 0.1.40.3 HIP engine and Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS / IQ3_XXS.

- IQ2_XS prefill sweep: 2,048 / 4,096 / 8,192 / 16,384, with three measured runs per prompt size and configuration.
- Matched 32K-context coding comparison: three synthetic fixtures, three runs each per model; both completed 9/9 tasks and 243/243 acceptance checks.
- One 113,501-token recall request with a 122,880-token context limit, plus conversation-prefix reuse and tool-call smoke checks.

## Tested models and settings

Models: **ISTA-DASLab Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO IQ2_XS and IQ3_XXS**, using existing prepared packs and a Q2_0 MTP runtime pack. Engine: **Strata 0.1.40.3, native Windows HIP**, not Vulkan or WSL inference. OpenCode 1.18.34 / OpenChamber 1.24.2 were the clients.

Common settings (portable arguments; model paths omitted):

```text
STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1
--expert-cache auto --prefill 8192
--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5
--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --vram-reserve-mib 2048
```

**Context:** 32,768 for both models in the matched coding comparison; 122,880 for the IQ2_XS prefill sweep and near-limit recall. The sweep varied prefill only. One parallel request; vision and speed projection off. Sampling: temperature 1.0, top-p 0.95, top-k 20, min-p 0, seed 42, repeat penalty 1.0, presence/frequency penalties 0. Coding used medium reasoning with an 8,192-token output allowance; recall used low reasoning with a 1,024-token cap.

## Measured results

### Matched 32K coding: IQ2_XS versus IQ3_XXS

Three synthetic TypeScript fixtures, three runs each per model:

| Measurement | IQ2_XS | IQ3_XXS |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Tasks passed | 9/9 | 9/9 |
| Acceptance checks across repetitions | 243/243 | 243/243 |
| Median task time, seconds | 99.988 | 136.321 |
| Task time range, seconds | 55.463–145.326 | 81.012–166.632 |
| Weighted engine decode, tok/s | **49.61** | **42.52** |
| Minimum available host RAM, GiB | 8.92 | 3.11 |
| Peak dedicated adapter counter, GiB | 14.88 | 15.04 |
| Peak shared adapter counter, GiB | 34.16 | 41.12 |

IQ2_XS had about **27% lower median task time** and **17% higher weighted decode throughput** on these tasks. Both passed the limited checks; this does not establish equal general answer quality. The 243 checks are 81 across the three fixtures repeated three times. Weighted decode includes reasoning and can include client helper requests. Shared GPU memory is system RAM, not extra VRAM; adapter peaks must not be added together. IQ2 ran first, then IQ3; order was not randomized.

### IQ2_XS prefill tuning at 122,880 configured context

Median results over three fresh-prompt requests per size and setting (no prefix reuse; loading excluded):

| Prefill | 8,019-token input: prompt / decode tok/s | 8K wall seconds | 28,180-token input: prompt / decode tok/s | 28K wall seconds |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 2,048 | 346.3 / 53.2 | 25.400 | 347.0 / 57.9 | 83.355 |
| 4,096 | 593.3 / 52.7 | 15.703 | 593.1 / 57.0 | 49.558 |
| **8,192** | **879.4 / 56.3** | **11.212** | **807.4 / 57.6** | **37.008** |
| 16,384 | 876.3 / 55.3 | 11.384 | 811.2 / 57.8 | 36.778 |

Prefill 8,192 reduced median wall time by about **56%** versus 2,048 at both lengths; 16,384 gave no meaningful further benefit. Recall content passed 24/24, but strict plain JSON passed 0/24 because responses used Markdown fences. Outputs were only 111–120 tokens, and adaptive expert/OS caches remained within each arm.

### IQ2_XS large-context recall

**One run**, context 122,880, prefill 8,192; **113,501 input / 119 output / 0 reused tokens**:

| Measurement | Result |
| --- | ---: |
| Engine prompt processing | **789.9 tok/s** |
| Engine decode | **46.9 tok/s** |
| First streamed token (includes reasoning) | 144.157 s |
| Total wall time | 146.629 s |
| Minimum available host RAM | 9.49 GiB |

All three start/middle/end markers were recovered, with the same Markdown-fenced JSON issue. This is a single simple recall test, **not validated 120K coding or an 8K answer at the limit**.

**Configuration retained on this desktop:** IQ2_XS, prefill 8,192, context 122,880, with normal client compaction retained; IQ3_XXS remains a fallback. This is not a comparison against the previous dense Qwen 27B llama.cpp setup.

Full ranges, per-run data, cache/tool checks and reproduction details: [benchmark report](https://github.com/isoux35/Strata/blob/33b9505360b3921d712e448660df0fd86cf05b7c/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt/README.md) and [methods](https://github.com/isoux35/Strata/blob/33b9505360b3921d712e448660df0fd86cf05b7c/bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt/METHODS.md).

## What changed
Adds only `bench/results/2026-10-10-community-rx-9060-xt/`: a short report, detailed methods, per-run JSON, synthetic fixtures and generated solutions, and reproduction scripts. No engine, backend, installer or default-setting changes.

## Extra notes
All 18 exported solutions were independently rechecked (486 passing acceptance checks, zero failures), and all 42 solution-file hashes verified. The 70 committed files match the reviewed export byte for byte. Credentials, private configurations, personal paths, conversation logs, model binaries and executable hashes are excluded.

Limitations are explicit: one machine, fixed arm order, adaptive expert caches, short decode outputs in the prefill sweep, fenced JSON failures, and a single large-context recall test rather than complex long-context coding. Memory readings are whole-host/whole-adapter observations; the short stability window is not an overnight guarantee.

title: config: forward - POSTs to a path answered by another server (embeddings, reranking)
body:
## Title
Config: "forward", POSTs to a path answered by another server (embeddings, reranking)

## Summary
Clients that expect `/v1/embeddings` and `/v1/rerank` beside the chat model, as llama-server or LM Studio provide, can't use them with Strata today (404). `"forward": {"/v1/embeddings": "http://127.0.0.1:8081/v1/embeddings"}` passes POSTs to those paths to another server and its answer back as it came, so those clients keep one base URL. Split out of #1789 (which now only carries the Windows AMD images), as AGENTS.md asks: one change per PR, a new feature opt-in.

## What changed
- **`serve/server.py`:**
  - `forward_of()`: paths start with `/` and can't be Strata's own (`OWN_API_PATHS`, `/v1/responses*`); URLs are http(s); anything else is a config error at start.
  - The handler's `_forward()` runs after Strata's Host, API-key and web-page checks, and does not send Strata's API key on.
  - A server that doesn't answer gives `502` with `code: forward_failed`. The start log names each forward.
- **Docs:** `docs/DETAILS.md`.

## Extra Notes
- **Checked on Windows:** `llama-server --embedding` with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B at 127.0.0.1:8081, reached through Strata from the host and from a Docker container. A client's search by meaning found the right document for 8 of 8 test questions.
- **Default path:** without the key nothing is forwarded, and unknown paths still give 404 (tested).
- **Tests:** `serve/test_server.py` `Forward`, against a local side server: status and body passed back, no Authorization sent on, 502 when down, the config checks. All `serve` and setup test files pass on `main` fb58e0d.

## Title
Config: "user_args", engine options of the user's own that setup keeps

## Title
Structured output: a one-string-field schema answered as plain text (opt-in), and progress in structured keep-alives

## Summary
Split out of #1789 (which now only carries the Windows AMD images), as AGENTS.md asks: one change per PR, a new feature opt-in.

## What changed
- **`"structured_plain_string": true` (opt-in):** a `json_schema` that is one required string field, with an optional description/title and no enum, pattern or length limit, is answered as plain text, and the server builds the object around it.

    | --- | --- |

- **Structured SSE keep-alives** now say how far the answer is (`: keep-alive: structured output buffered until it is validated, N pieces (M characters) written so far`), so a long answer can be told from a stuck one. They are SSE comments, which clients ignore.

title: serve: opt-in guard for a repeated phrase (repeat_stop_period), and name repetition stops (stop_cause)
body:
## Title
Issue: relates to #606 and #728

## Summary
Two things about replies Strata ends because they repeat:
- **Opt-in:** a guard for a short phrase repeated back to back.
- **Always:** the stop is named.

Split out of #1789 (which now only carries the Windows AMD images), as AGENTS.md asks: one change per PR, a new feature opt-in.

## What changed
- **`serve/server.py`, `"repeat_stop_period": N`** (opt-in; default 1 = only #606's one-token rule):
  - a run of `repeat_stop_tokens` tokens that repeats with a period of 2..N tokens ends the reply like #606;
  - O(N) per token;
  - seen on a scanned page: `[unclear] ` written until `max_tokens` ran out (12,000 tokens, 229 s), which the one-token rule never sees;
  - 16 is a good value.
- **`choices[0].stop_cause`:** a reply ended by either guard (or by #728's `reasoning_loop_recovery: "stop"`) keeps `finish_reason: "length"` and adds Strata's own `"stop_cause": "repetition"` / `"reasoning_loop"`. On the OpenAI chat API, streamed and not.
- **`serve/structured.py`:** a structured answer ended that way fails with a message that says the reply repeated itself, instead of "increase the output budget", which a larger `max_tokens` cannot fix. Responses API too.
  - Seen with a one-field `json_schema` on a scanned rent roll: the model wrote the escaped newline 256 times, #606 stopped it, and the client was told to raise the budget.
- **Docs:** `docs/DETAILS.md`.

## Extra Notes
- **Default path:** with the default `repeat_stop_period` 1, the guard code is skipped. Replies that end normally, or at `max_tokens`, are unchanged. `stop_cause` and the new message appear only when #606 or #728 already end a reply, which are replies that were already cut short.
- **Tests:**
  - `serve/test_server.py` `RepeatStop`: off by default, a phrase ended with period 16, period 1, a long varied reply runs to its end;
  - `serve/test_structured.py`: the message, `stop_cause` streamed and not, and no cause for a real budget stop.

title: telemetry: GPU load, VRAM, temperature and power for AMD cards on Windows (#1380)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1380

## Summary
On Windows, the Monitor shows no GPU load, VRAM, temperature or power for AMD cards: the AMD reader used the amdgpu driver's Linux sysfs files only. This adds a Windows reader that gets the same four values from what every Adrenalin install already has. It uses ctypes like the NVML reader, so there's no new dependency.

Checked on a Ryzen AI Max+ 395 / Radeon 8060S (Strix Halo), Windows 11 Pro 10.0.26300, driver 32.0.31041.1004, engine 0.1.40.2. The Monitor now shows load, VRAM `63.2 / 64 GB` with `24,576 experts cached`, temperature and power, all with sparklines.

## What changed
- **`serve/telemetry.py`:** new `_AmdWindows` reader with `_Nvml`'s interface. `gpu_reader(index, amd=True)` picks it when `WINDOWS`; on Linux it's still `_Amd` (sysfs).

  | Value | Source |
  | --- | --- |
  | Load | ADL PMLog sensor 19 (`PMLOG_INFO_ACTIVITY_GFX`) |
  | Temperature | First supported of 28 / 8 / 27 / 29 (GFX, edge, hotspot, SoC) |
  | Power | 23 (`PMLOG_ASIC_POWER`), else 30 (GFX power) |
  | VRAM size | `ADL2_Adapter_MemoryInfo2_Get` |
  | VRAM in use | OS counter `\GPU Adapter Memory(<luid>)\Dedicated Usage` through `pdh.dll` (`PdhAddEnglishCounterW`, so any Windows language) |

  - **Adapter match:** the counter's adapter is matched to ADL's card by PCI bus number, through `D3DKMTEnumAdapters2` + `KMTQAITYPE_ADAPTERADDRESS`. ADL's own `ADL2_Adapter_VRAMUsage_Get` returned 3,748,023 MB on the 8060S, so it isn't used.
  - **Card numbering:** AMD cards in PCI bus order, one per bus (ADL lists one entry per display output).
  - **Errors:** a missing ADL, or no such card, gives `ok() == False`, as before.
- **The #1380 note:** it now says why readings are missing ("AMD's ADL library … did not answer for this card", or "the amdgpu driver's sysfs files were not found"), instead of "not available on Windows AMD yet". `app.js` shows "not available" in the VRAM tile in that case.
- **`serve/test_server.py`:**
  - `AmdTelemetry` pins `WINDOWS = False`, so the sysfs tests also pass when run on Windows.
  - New `AmdWindowsTelemetry`: sensor choice, LUID instance names, and no-card behaviour (Windows only), including the note.
  - The sysfs no-card case now checks its note.
  - `serve.test_server`, `serve.test_monitor` and `serve.test_frontend` pass on Windows: 283 tests.
- **`docs/AMD_HIP.md`:** the Monitor line names the Windows sources.

## Extra Notes
- **Sensor check:** while a 14K-token prompt was read, activity went 6 → 85-96 %, GFX temperature 48 → 53-81 °C, ASIC power 45 → 80-110 W, and GFX power alone 4 → 22-31 W. On an APU, ASIC power is the whole chip (CPU, GPU and memory share the package). It's the counterpart of NVML's board power, so it's the one shown.
- **Power limit:** no power-limit sensor answers on the 8060S (47/48), so `power_limit` stays None, and the tile shows no "of … W limit".
- **Not tested on a discrete Radeon** (e.g. the 9070 XT in #1380). The sensor ids are ADL's standard ones and the code falls back across them, but a report from a discrete card would be good.
- **`free_vram_mib(amd=True)`** now also returns a value on Windows: total minus dedicated usage. So `min_free_vram_mib` works there too.

title: Remote stage: run the later layers of a layer split on other PCs, over TCP (opt-in; Linux and Windows; Qwen3.8-Flash-Next)
body:
## Summary

A layer split already hands a token from one stage to the next once per verify window, and each prompt chunk's rows
once per chunk. This branch puts that hand-off on a TCP link, so the later layers can run on cards in **other PCs**:

- the main process runs layers [0, K), the head, the draft layer, sampling and the server:
  `--layer-split K --split-device 0 --remote-stage HOST:PORT`;
- a worker process on another PC runs [K, 48) without the head: `strata --serve --stage-worker PORT --stage-begin K`;
  relay workers (`--stage-end K2 --stage-next HOST:PORT`) make three or more stages;
- each process loads only its own layers' experts (a ranged expert arena) and dense weights, keeps an expert cache and
  an adaptive tier for its own layers, and its own part of the session;
- the link builds on Linux (POSIX sockets) and Windows (Winsock); a Windows PC can be a worker natively or under WSL2;
- `STRATA_REMOTE_TIMING=1` prints each stage's own time per prompt chunk and per window (a worker's split into GPU
  wait, CPU pool + plan and host staging);
- three standard-library Python tools: a node agent that starts workers on each PC (`tools/stage_node.py`), a
  splitter that ships a node only its layers' bytes as sparse files (`tools/stage_ship.py`: several 64 MiB pieces in
  flight on keep-alive connections, each checked by sha256 on the node, resumable), and a tuner that measures
  configurations for real and writes the split, the prompt chunk and the configs (`tools/stage_tune.py`).

Docs: `docs/REMOTE_STAGE.md` (use), `docs/remote-stage/ENGINEERING.md` (design, process, every number). Raw numbers:
`bench/results/2026-10-10-remote-stage/`.

About #1256: I saw that splitting a model across machines was closed there as not planned. This is fully opt-in and
self-contained (a new source file, hooks that are inert by default, three tools, docs), and the measurements below
show where it pays. If it is not wanted upstream, that is fine: I will keep maintaining it in my fork, and the Windows
clock finding below may be useful on its own.

## Results

PC A: RTX 3080 10 GB (PCIe 4.0 at x8), Ryzen 9 5900XT, 128 GB DDR4-3200, Linux. PC B: RTX 2080 Ti 11 GB, Ryzen 9
5900X, 64 GB DDR4-2400, Linux. PC C: RTX 3070 8 GB, Ryzen 7 5700X3D, 64 GB DDR4-3600, Windows 11. Links 1 GbE, and
10 GbE between A and B (~400 MB/s, slot-limited). `--kv int8 --kv-resident 32768 --max-context 131072 --spec 4`,
greedy, one run per row. Prefill / decode tok/s; prompts of 7.5K / 30K / 57K / 91K tokens with 320-token answers.

| configuration | short decode | 8K | 32K | 100K |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| RVN IQ3_S, 3080 alone | 39.9 | 791 / 38.1 | 1,118 / 37.2 | 1,120 / 38.0 |
| RVN IQ3_S, A + B (1 GbE), K=26, chunk 5888 | 53.5 | 655 / 48.1 | 1,231 / 49.7 | 1,521 / 45.6 |
| RVN IQ3_S, A + B + C (A-B 10 GbE), 24 / 16 / 8, C clocks locked | 51.3 | 658 / 47.8 | 1,110 / 46.5 | 1,640 / 44.7 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, 3080 alone (each number the better of two single-card runs: prefill with a RAM budget, decode without) | 27.3 | 302 / 25.4 | 324 / 24.5 | 326 / 23.7 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, A + B (10 GbE), K=26, chunk 5888 | 38.8 | 659 / 34.4 | 1,147 / 36.9 | 1,164 / 33.6 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, A + B + C, 24 / 16 / 8, C locked | 38.4 | 549 / 35.3 | 945 / 36.6 | 1,334 / 35.2 |
| UD-Q4_K_XL, A + B + C, the tuner's pick (24 / 16 / 8 again of 8 splits; its own prompts, C with 1,248 cache slots) | 36.8 | 552 / 33.1 | 975 / 35.2 | 1,383 / 33.6 |

- Two PCs: decode +18-44% on IQ3_S; on UD-Q4_K_XL, which one 10 GB card caches poorly (571-620 cache slots, auto
  chunk 1280-2048), decode +42% and a 100K prompt in 88 s instead of 293.
- Long prompts need a large chunk (5888-8192): at 2048 every split read them slower than one card.
- A third PC adds a hop to every window: it paid for long prompts (100K) and cost 1-8% of decode on IQ3_S. On
  UD-Q4_K_XL the tuner tried eight splits of the three stages (from 18 / 16 / 14 to 26 / 14 / 8): all within 45.7-48.0
  s for a 32K request, a tie within the run-to-run spread. Over a 30% 8K / 50% 32K / 20% 100K workload (computed from
  the rows) two PCs take 46.3 s a request and three 47.6-49.1 s; one card ~133 s.

**Windows lowers a worker GPU's clocks between decode windows.** A worker idles while the other stages run (25-45 ms a
window). Sampled every 100 ms, the RTX 3070 under Windows spent 6% of a decode run in P2 (51% in P5, memory at
810 MHz) and waited 12-22 ms for its 8 layers per window; with `nvidia-smi -lgc 1500,1905 -lmc 7001,7001` it held P2
and waited 3.7-4.1 ms (short decode 33.8 -> 41.8). The 2080 Ti under Linux held P2 throughout (4.6-5.9 ms). WSL2
behaved the same as native Windows. The node agent can lock and reset the clocks around a worker (`"gpu_clocks"`,
agent run as administrator) and the tuner's report says when a Windows node has not. This may also affect cards in
one Windows PC with an in-process split; I have not measured that.

## What changed

| file | change |
|---|---|
| `include/strata/net/stage_link.hpp`, `src/net/stage_link.cpp` (new) | the protocol (version 3: hello, window, commit, prompt chunk, reset, error), `StageClient`, `StageRelay`, `serve_stage` (a receiving thread, two input and two output buffers, replies on their own thread); POSIX and Winsock behind one small socket layer |
| `src/program/generate.cpp` | the flags `--remote-stage`, `--stage-worker`, `--stage-begin`, `--stage-bind`, `--stage-end`, `--stage-next` and their checks; the layer range for the arena, dense weights, profile and session; the worker's serve loop and relay; the main process's head-only stage; the hello (geometry, K, K/V type, pack fingerprint, `STRATA_STAGE_TOKEN`); timing lines; the lend/refill code moved out of the request loop so the worker can call it |
| `include/strata/core/verify.hpp`, `src/core/verify.cpp` | `Verifier::set_no_head` and `set_remote` |
| `include/strata/prefill/prefill.hpp`, `src/prefill/prefill.cpp` | `Prefill::remote_send` / `remote_recv` (the pipelined chunk hand-off), `set_remote_rows_from`, `set_hand_in` / `set_single_chunk` |
| `include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp`, `src/core/expert_source.cpp` | `ArenaExpertSource::set_layer_range` and a layer range in `load_experts_gguf` (buffered and Windows unbuffered readers) |
| `CMakeLists.txt` | `src/net/stage_link.cpp` in the `strata` executable; `ws2_32` on Windows |
| `tools/stage_node.py`, `tools/stage_ship.py`, `tools/stage_tune.py`, `tools/test_stage_node.py` (new) | the agent, the splitter, the tuner, their tests (`python -m unittest tools.test_stage_node`) |
| `docs/REMOTE_STAGE.md`, `docs/remote-stage/ENGINEERING.md` (new), `docs/MULTI_GPU.md` | the docs; a pointer paragraph in MULTI_GPU.md |
| `bench/results/2026-10-10-remote-stage/` (new) | every run's JSONL, the timing lines, the clock samples, the benchmark scripts |

**What it leaves alone.** Without `--remote-stage` or `--stage-worker` no new code path runs: the new `Verifier`,
`Prefill` and arena hooks are inert at their defaults (no range, no remote callbacks, `no_head` false). Checked: one
single-GPU config (RVN IQ3_S on the RTX 3080, auto chunk, draft layer on) served by this branch's build twice and by
`main`'s build (the merge base) once; greedy answers to five prompts (one of 9,364 tokens, two chunks) were
byte-identical across the three (text, token counts, finish reasons). Not compared: an in-process multi-GPU split, other
models, Windows against an upstream Windows build.
With the flags, these are refused at start: `--batch`, `--pipeline-windows`, `--vision`, `--peer-device`,
`--control-vector` (and the speed projection), `--expert-cache-remote`; the prompt cache, the conversation cache,
mid-prompt checkpoints and `--kv-grow` are turned off. Not touched: the server, setup, the SYCL port's copies, the
HIP-specific code.

## How it was tested

- **Builds:** CUDA 13.0 on Linux (GCC, sm_75 + sm_86) and on Windows (MSVC 2022, sm_86); HIP (ROCm 7.0, gfx1100) and
  the SYCL port (oneAPI 2026.1.1; it compiles the shared `prefill.hpp` this branch changed) in containers. The remote
  stage itself ran on NVIDIA cards only.
- **Two and three PCs** as above, two models, single-card baselines on the same day with the same build. The start of
  every benchmark answer (100-160 characters kept) was coherent and on topic in every configuration; full answers
  were not compared against the in-process split.
- **Tools end to end:** layers shipped to a Linux host, a WSL2 VM and native Windows, workers started from the shipped
  sparse files by the agents (one agent serving two models), the Windows agent locking and resetting the clocks (run
  as administrator during the benchmarks; the final version also run without, where it starts the worker and says
  "NOT locked"), and the tuner run on two PCs (RVN IQ3_S: it picked the same split as the hand sweep) and three PCs
  (UD-Q4_K_XL).
- `python -m unittest tools.test_stage_node`: 35 tests, on Windows (ReFS) and Linux. The shipper's tests include
  pieces in flight at once, a damaged piece that is not recorded and is sent again, and an older agent or shipper.
- **Shipper through a link emulator** on one Windows PC (30 MB/s shared, 5 ms added each way, 1 GiB): one piece at a
  time 28.1 MB/s, pieces in flight 29.4 (the link full); with a node that takes 1 s more per piece, 19.4 MB/s before
  and 28.2 with `--parallel 4`.
- **Probes:** a wrong token is refused; a peer that sends no hello is closed after 10 s.

## Not tested

- Running on AMD or Intel cards (HIP and SYCL were built, not run); the SYCL port keeps its own copies of the engine
  files and has no remote stage.
- Windows as the main PC; an in-process split on Windows with locked clocks.
- Other quantizations of the family (official IQ3_S, IQ3_XXS, IQ2_XS, UD-IQ4_XS); a pack with `experts.bin` is
  refused at start.
- Correctness against the in-process split with fixed caches; more than one run per configuration (decode moved by up
  to ~14% between two runs of one configuration).
- Reconnecting without restarting the main engine; a ring topology; a bf16 hand-off.
- The shipper's pieces in flight over a real WAN (only the emulator above).

## Extra notes

- Plain TCP, not encrypted: token ids and hidden states cross the network in clear. The shared token only keeps other
  LAN hosts from driving a worker. The docs say to use it on a trusted LAN or inside a tunnel.
- The node agent's token lets a request start the engine with whitelisted flags and write files under its data
  directory: a credential, LAN only.
- One feature in one PR; I can split it into the engine hooks, the network stage and the tools if that is easier to
  review.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: fix(setup): discard damaged llama.cpp source archives
body:
## Title
Issue: Fixes #1797

## Summary
A damaged cached llama.cpp source ZIP can keep its `.done` mark after `get_llama_cpp()` raises `BadZipFile`. Every later setup run then reuses the same bad archive. Remove that archive and its mark so the next run can download it again.

Kept as a draft: CUDA/HIP/SYCL builds have not been run, so the backend-build requirement in AGENTS.md has not been met. The applicability of that requirement to this installer-only change still needs clarification before requesting review.

## What changed
- Catch `zipfile.BadZipFile` only around opening and extracting the llama.cpp source archive, and reuse `drop_archive()` for that exact ZIP and its `.done` mark.
- Re-raise the original exception. If cleanup raises `OSError`, warn about manual cleanup without replacing the original archive error.
- Add isolated local-file regressions for invalid/truncated archives, extraction-time CRC failure and recovery, cleanup edge cases, successful reuse, and non-corruption errors that must retain their cache.

The download strategy, retries, source pin, archive member filtering, successful extraction path, and engine/backend code are unchanged. This does not add checksums or change archive-security policy.

Related: #1126 changes the same function to use `safe_extract()`, but its current implementation does not remove this damaged source cache. These changes address different behavior; any future integration must preserve that safe-extraction work. #424 covers the analogous engine-archive path.

## Extra Notes
Local validation on Linux x86_64 (kernel 6.18.44), Python 3.12.14, at `cdb17c717260bdb9122099bac055df82ef197f0e`:
- Real production `get_llama_cpp()` / `download(file://...)` reproduction: two calls on unchanged base `fb58e0d` keep reusing the bad ZIP and mark. With the fix, the first call removes them and the second installs a valid local archive. Network calls are prohibited in these regressions.
- `python tools/test_setup_llama_archive.py -v`: 10 tests passed. The same final suite fails on the unchanged base.
- Independent review: 9 additional boundary checks passed.
- `python tools/test_setup_golden.py -v`: 4 passed, including saved-configuration byte consistency.
- 33 selected adjacent archive checks passed through an offline runner with socket calls blocked: `tools.test_setup_pins.Engine`; `tools.test_setup_engine_hash` classes `ArchiveVerification`, `DigestLookup`, `WhereTheHashComesFrom`, `Wiring`; and `WhatARefusalDoesToTheCaller.test_the_cuda_and_amd_paths_both_verify`.
- `python tools/test_setup_choices.py -v`: 39 passed, 1 environment error (`RotationalDisk.test_sysfs`: missing `/sys/block`), identical on base and patch.
- `python -m py_compile setup.py tools/test_setup_llama_archive.py`, `git diff --check`, and exact-base patch replay checks passed.

Validation limits: no CUDA/HIP/SYCL build, Windows run, GPU/model execution, or real remote llama.cpp download. Three existing adjacent checks with unmocked HEAD requests were excluded from the final offline selection. An earlier broad engine-hash run made release-asset HEAD requests, received HTTP 404, and was interrupted; the full suite is not reported as passing. No online CI success is assumed.

title: bench: community report, 2x PH402 SKU 200 (4x GP100, sm_60), Swift 1.5 IQ3_XXS at 1M, --pipeline-windows off vs on over four stages, engine 0.1.41 + patches
body:
Results-only submission, no engine changes. Adds bench/results/2026-10-09-community-2x-ph402-sku200/ following docs/COMMUNITY_BENCHMARKS.md.

**Headline.** `--pipeline-windows 2` (#1656 + #1674) on a four-stage layer split of four GP100 dies raises decode by **+14.6% to +28.8%** on 9 prompts of 87 to 301,147 tokens. Some examples:
- 40.5 → 51.2 tok/s on a 256-token code answer.
- 47.6 → 61.3 on a 512-token one.
- 43.2 → 53.7 after a fresh 301,108-token read.
- 41.7 → 50.3 on a follow-up at 301K.

Prompt reads are unchanged by the flag. Replies are identical bit for bit in all three arms on all 9 prompts.

Hardware:
- **GPUs:** 2× NVIDIA PH402 SKU 200, i.e. four GP100 dies (sm_60, 48 SMs, 31.91 GiB each, TCC). Each die has a 140 W cap and an application clock of 1050 MHz.
- **Links:** the two dies of a board copy peer-to-peer at 73.0–73.2 GB/s; across boards 3.3 GB/s; host to device 3.3 GB/s per die.
- **Host:** Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 256 GiB DDR5, ASUS ProArt B850-CREATOR WIFI NEO, NVMe SSD.
- **OS:** Windows 11 (build 26300), driver 581.80, CUDA 12.9.

Software: source builds for sm_60 (`-DSTRATA_EXPERIMENTAL_SM60=ON`). The server is `serve/server.py` from v0.1.41.
- **next8:** v0.1.41 + #1674 + #1656 + the PH402 patch set. That set is #1424, #1441, #1660, #1368 and #1525, plus local sm_60 commits. The commit list is in the README.
- **next7:** the same patch set on v0.1.40.4, without pipelined windows.
- **next9:** next8 linked against ggml-cuda with a local sm_60 MMQ patch ([diff in my comment on #1639](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1639#issuecomment-6086238713)).

Model:
- [`ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF`](https://huggingface.co/ukisai/Swift-1.5-Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-GGUF) IQ3_XXS. The dense projections and head were converted to Q8_0 with `tools/q8_dense_gguf.py` (#1424).
- Context 1,048,576 tokens (yarn ×4), int8 KV, layer split `12,24,36`, all 24,576 experts in VRAM.
- MTP `--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.85 --mtp-window 8192`, greedy.

Configurations tested (every reply is hashed):
1. **Pipelined windows:** next7, next8 without the flag, and next8 with `--pipeline-windows 2`. One engine start each, the same 9 requests. These include a follow-up at 301K and a return to that conversation from the conversation cache.
2. **Prompt path:** next8 vs next9 (the MMQ patch), and `STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE` 768 / 290 / 450 on next9. Eight starts in bracketed order, 5 requests each (3 in the one start with the prefill timer).
3. **Draft floor:** `spec_min_p` 0.5 / 0.7 / 0.85 / 0.95 per request with pipelining on. 3 prompts × 2 rounds.

Other results:
- **MMQ patch:** the batched reads take 2.5–6.0% less time (bracketed next8 / next9 / next8 starts, one run each), and replies are identical.
- **`STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE` 768 → 290:**
  - The 1,158-token read goes from 4.627 / 4.632 s to 4.018 s.
  - The 34,835-token read goes from 48.967 / 49.195 s to 46.545 s.
  - 1,027 tokens appended to that conversation go from 4.339 / 4.348 s to 4.419 s (+1.7%).
  - The changed chunking changes the output bits.
- **Draft floor:** 0.85 is the fastest value on both code prompts.
- **Driver check:** `bench.py` (plan `ab`), run again on next9 at 290, reproduced that arm's 5 reply hashes.

Limitations:
- **Runs:** one run per arm for the pipelining A/B, 1–3 runs for the prompt-path arms, and 2 rounds for the floor sweep.
- **Baselines:** no stock v0.1.41 arm, and #1656 was not run without #1674.
- **Timers:** the prefill and decode timers were on in the three pipelining arms.
- **Not measured:** reply quality (replies were not graded, and every one ran to its cap), TTFT and peak memory.
- **Scope:** one model.
- **Hashes:** the sha256 of the converted Q8_0 shards and the pack/MTP preparation commands were not recorded. The README marks them.

Context:
- #1656 (@Cass67) and #1674 (@CC-David-CC): this adds four stages on CUDA sm_60 with reply hashes, at contexts up to 301K tokens. A trace breakdown is in [my comment on #1656](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/pull/1656#issuecomment-6086159617).
- #1441: `STRATA_PREFILL_PIPE`.
- #1639 (@thedrzinger, 5× P100): a PRMT dp4a emulation for the sm_60 MMQ path; [my reply there](https://github.com/Niko1221/Strata/issues/1639#issuecomment-6086238713) has the patch and its numbers.

title: Community benchmark: 2x Tesla P40, IQ3_S, 131K ctx (engine 0.1.41)
body:
Full report in **bench/results/2026-10-10-community-2x-p40-iq3_s/** (`README.md` + raw engine timings).

Two Tesla P40 24 GB (sm_61), Xeon E5-2699 v3 (18c/36t, AVX2), 125 GB RAM, Ubuntu 22.04, driver 550.144.03. Engine **0.1.41** (fb58e0d), CUDA 12 source build (`--cuda 12`, sm_61 experimental path), layer split **K=24**, IQ3_S @131,072 ctx, int8 KV + kv-resident 32768, `--pcie-frac 0.34 --spec-min-p 0.70` (calibrated), 9,820/24,576 experts resident (17.69 GiB), 46.84 GiB expert arena, 17 pool workers.

Headlines (engine timings, temp 0, reasoning none, prefill legs fresh `cache_n=0`; medians of 3, all values + raw lines in the report):

- decode **35.0 tok/s** short-prompt (34.8 / 35.0 / 35.1; draft acceptance 69% post-calibration, 51% before)
- prompt **350 tok/s @3,918 tok** · **558 tok/s @21,858 tok** (TTFT 11.2 s / 39.2 s)
- needles **6/6** — lengths 32k + 128k, depths 10/50/90 (128K reads 172-192 s wall)
- golden-prefix parking (`--conversation-cache-mib 2048`): 5.2K omp-style system prefix reads cold in 15.7 s, later conversations mount in **0.43-0.83 s** cross-session; a 21.9K prompt re-mounts in 0.30 s TTFT
- `slot save/restore` is refused on the layer split ("session files do not support --layer-split") — restart persistence is one warm request after READY

llama.cpp context on the same machine (Qwen3.8-27B-AP-Q4_K_XL, `-sm tensor` both P40s):
decode **22.7 tok/s** (v0.4.0-dev and v0.5.0 agree exactly), prompt ≈388/390 tok/s at the same token counts; v0.5.0 `--spec-type draft-mtp --spec-draft-n-max 4` → **24.9 tok/s** (+9.8%, acceptance 33% on prose). So Flash-Next IQ3_S is **+54% decode vs the best 27B config** on this pair, −10% prefill at 4K, +43% at 22K, 131K vs 393K ctx. (Flash-Next itself via stock llama.cpp collapses on prefill — 13-18 tok/s — per sarge18/p40-llm-engine-bakeoff on identical GPUs.)

Not tested: batching (`--parallel`), CPU vision, ctx >131K, quality suites, adaptive-swap arms beyond calibrate's.

Method: 3 reps per number, all values + medians, engine `prompt_per_second`/`predicted_per_second`, client stream cross-check, greedy decode, needles via `tools/needle_bench.py`.

Only adds two files under `bench/results/`; no code, docs, or defaults touched. Related: #1028 #1029 #1469 (no sign of the #1469 decode regression on this pair — our 34.9 matches #1028's 34.8).

title: sycl: --expert-parallel-device N, two Arc cards compute each layer's experts together
body:
## Title
Issue: none.

## Summary
An opt-in way for the SYCL port to use two Arc cards for each layer's experts: `--expert-parallel-device N`. Card 0 runs every layer, card N holds the experts card 0 does not, and for each layer of a decode window both cards compute their own experts at the same time. Without the option nothing changes.

This branch has two commits. c245661 is #1589 (the Verifier's null-stream sentinel, issue #1555), which this needs: without it card N's verifier takes card 0's queue and its first capture fails. The change itself is bc72506. Once #1589 is in main, this rebases to the one commit.

### Measured
2x Arc Pro B70 (32 GB each, xe, Linux), Flash-Next IQ3_XXS, Ryzen 9 9950X3D, 60 GB RAM, through the server (`sycl/serve/server_intel.py`, 131,072 context, INT8 KV with `--kv-resident 32768`, `--vram-reserve-mib 2048`, the default drafting), greedy, thinking off, the same request 3 times (the 2nd and 3rd; the 1st reads the prompt):

| | `--layer-split auto` | `--expert-parallel-device 1` |
|---|---|---|
| where the experts live | layers 0-28 on card 0, 29-47 on card 1, every expert in VRAM | card 0: 283 per layer, card 1: the other 229, every expert in VRAM |
| decode, a BST class (600 tokens) | 94.3 tok/s | 107.9 tok/s (+14.4%) |
| decode, a 300-word explanation (384 tokens) | 64.2 tok/s | 72.6 tok/s (+13.1%) |
| output | | byte-identical to the layer split, all 6 requests of each |


### Why not 2x
Only the experts run on both cards. Stage times of a 4-token window (`STRATA_VERIFY_EAGER=1 STRATA_VERIFY_PROFILE=1`): the experts take 11.8 ms with the layer split and 8.2 ms with expert parallelism, the rest 41.0 and 40.7 ms. These run without the graph (the port's in-graph timestamps read 0), every kernel launched and timed from the host, so they are larger than with the graph and their ratio (52.8 / 48.9 = 1.08x) is not the decode's gain; they show which part got shorter. A unitrace of 96 decoded tokens shows what the handshake still costs card 0 per layer: its wait for card N's rows 26 us (card N's inbox copy, plan and row send are on its path), the send 3.5 us. In the same trace each card's expert kernels take 160-170 ms of the trace's 1.1 s.

## What changed
- `sycl/src/program/generate.cpp`: the option and its checks (a second card, `--stream-experts`; not with `--layer-split`, `--peer-device` or `--pipeline-windows`). Each card's set of experts is fixed at the start: each layer's experts are dealt to the two cards hottest first, in pairs alternating 0,1 / 1,0, until card 0's per-layer quota is full, so both cards serve about the same share of each layer's routing. Card N gets an `ExpertCache` of its own, filled from the GGUF. Per-layer slots, no prompt loans and no adaptive swaps, since either would leave an expert on neither card mid-request.
- `sycl/src/core/verify.cpp`, `sycl/include/strata/core/verify.hpp`: `Verifier::set_ep`. Card N's half of each window is a graph of its own, recorded beside card 0's and launched just before it; the same for the `--batch` graphs. Per layer, card 0 pushes the routed ids and the q8_1 MoE input into card N's inbox; card N plans and computes its entries and writes their rows straight into card 0's `parts_`; card 0 waits for that before its combine, which is the single-card one. After each window, `ep_check` reports a wait that ran to its bound or an expert on neither card.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/ep_kernels.dp.cpp`, `sycl/include/strata/kernels/ep_kernels.hpp` (new): the handshake kernels. The flags hold an epoch each card's graph advances on the device (a host value would freeze at capture), and every spin is bounded. Two orderings mattered, each found by a greedy answer that changed between identical requests: data the other card wrote is read past the caches (an inbound PCIe write does not invalidate the reader's caches), and card N writes its rows and raises its flag in one kernel (`ep_send_rows`); with the flag in a later kernel, 2 of 6 requests read a row that was not all there yet.
- `sycl/include/strata/core/ep_mem.hpp` (new): the regions one card writes and the other reads. dpct gives each device its own `sycl::context`, so each region is a Level Zero allocation of its own on its owner, opened on the other card through an IPC handle in the same process.
- `sycl/src/kernels/cuda/verify_kernels.dp.cpp`: `resident_plan_ep`, the device plan for one card of the pair. It reuses `resident_plan_kernel` with two new parameters; with them, entries the other card owns are left out of the groups instead of being a plan error. Their defaults keep the old behaviour, and the existing calls do not pass them, so `resident_plan` is unchanged.
- `sycl/src/kernels/resident_plan_ep_parity.cpp` (new, in the parity tests): both cards' plans against a host replay.
- `sycl/CMakeLists.txt`: the new kernel file and the parity test.
- `docs/INTEL.md`: a section with the table above, how it works, what it needs and the checks.

## How it was checked
- `resident_plan_ep_parity`: 420 cases, 0 failures; `resident_plan_parity`: 641 cases, 0 failures (GPU, synthetic, no model). It checks that the two plans together cover every entry once, an expert on neither card sets the plan error, and with every expert on card 0 the plan is `resident_plan`'s word for word.
- `STRATA_EP_VERIFY=1` (with `STRATA_EP_MIRROR=1`) has card 0 compute every row itself and compare card N's rows with them word for word: no row differed in the 448 windows the three runs reported. `STRATA_EP_SELF=1` runs the window on card 0's own rows only; its output is byte-identical to the expert-parallel one.
- Output with the option: byte-identical to `--layer-split` for both prompts, all 6 requests of each (table above).
- `--batch 4` with the option (server, 128K context, this branch's build): 4 requests at once (512 tokens each) gave the same output as one request alone.
- Without the option: the same tokens as main's binary, one card with the RAM mirror, `--tokens` with a 40-token prompt, greedy, 32K context: T=1 (`--spec 2 --mtp-max-t 1 --suffix-draft 0`, 256 tokens) and MTP (`--spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --mtp`, 512 tokens), identical output hashes.
- SYCL build (AOT `bmg-g31`): all targets including the parity tests, and `strata` again after the last change (a comment and the docs).

## Extra Notes
- The whole diff was reviewed by a human (the author).
- Only the SYCL port is touched; CUDA and HIP are unchanged.
- The prompt path reads card N's experts from the GGUF on card 0 (a 1,996-token prompt: 719 tok/s against 768 on one card with the RAM mirror). `STRATA_EP_MIRROR=1` also mirrors them in pinned RAM (18 GB for IQ3_XXS).
- A run without `--mtp` ends with an error at exit after its output, as on main; #1642 fixes that and is separate.
- Tested only on 2x B70 under xe on Linux; not on Arc A-series cards (i915), on Windows, or with cards of two different kinds.
