title: fix(serve): retain watchdog causes after HIP traces; request gfx1100 testing
body:
Related: #1705, #872. Draft for community testing; neither issue is claimed resolved.

### Problem and evidence
Thanks to @foomip for the engine log in #1705. Large verify traces pushed the watchdog cause beyond `death_note()`'s 4 KB tail, producing a misleading RAM explanation. Replaying its 24 engine-run segments: the old lookup missed 2 of 6 watchdog events; this branch finds all six without attributing an earlier run's watchdog to a later exit. These are log-replay results, not new inference runs.

### Changes
- Search this engine run backward for its watchdog, including across read boundaries.
- Clarify that `STRATA_DOORBELL_STORE` affects verify windows only.
- Document the reported Linux host-page-reclaim workaround and its limits. No GPU handshake, inference default, or swap setting is changed.

### Please test
@foomip @vletu-ghub: could you test this draft with your usual long-context workload? Other RX 7900 XTX/gfx1100 and Linux HIP reports are welcome. Check that a watchdog exit retains its actual cause despite a large trace, and report whether long-context serving still hangs or the entire machine restarts.

For a separate **Linux-only runtime mitigation** test, merge this into your existing server JSON `env`, retaining other entries, then restart the engine:
```json
"HSA_USERPTR_FOR_PAGED_MEM": "0"
```
Keep swap and other settings fixed. Foomip's nearly five-hour clean run followed both this setting and `swapoff`; it cannot isolate either effect. This PR does not itself fix that driver/runtime mechanism or establish a fix for #872's reboots.

Please report commit, OS/ROCm, model, context, run duration/request count, swap/reclaim state, and engine-exit versus whole-machine-reboot behavior. Include engine logs and, after a reboot, the previous boot's kernel log if available. Paired prefill/decode timings and exact token-ID parity on matched greedy prompts would help assess the runtime setting.

### Validation
275 Python server tests passed. The HIP engine build and `hip_handoff` passed on RX 7900 XTX/ROCm 7.15. Sustained long-context stability and whole-machine restart recovery remain unverified.

title: [Bug] Windows HIP (Radeon AI PRO R9700, gfx1201): engine hangs at verify-window capture at `--max-context 262144` — LiveKernelEvent 141 (TDR); 229376 and below start and serve fine
body:
## Summary

On Windows 10 with the prebuilt HIP engine, **every start at `--max-context 262144` dies during the verify-window capture phase** at serve init: the GPU wedges, Windows logs `LiveKernelEvent 141` (watchdog reset) twice, and the engine exits. Four consecutive starts at 262144 all failed the same way (across two engine versions). The same config at `--max-context 229376` starts normally, captures all six windows, and served a real 119,136-token prompt without issue. Free VRAM at the failure point is identical between the two settings (2308 vs 2306 MiB), so this is not VRAM pressure — something about 262144 specifically wedges the driver during capture.

## Environment

- **OS:** Windows 10 Professional 22H2 (10.0.19045)
- **Engine:** ready-made `strata-windows-x64-hip.zip` — `BUILD.json`: prebuilt, hip, windows-x64, **0.1.41**, rocm 10.2.0a20260930, hipblaslt_version 100500, archs gfx1100/1101/1102/1200/1201/1030/1151
- **GPU:** Radeon AI PRO R9700 32 GB (gfx1201); a second card (RX 9070 XT, gfx1201) present and idle; 9070XT card drive 2 monitors (2560 px / 1920 px)
- **AMD driver:** 32.0.23033.1002, dated 2026-03-09 — deliberately kept: newer Adrenalin builds are reported (community) to have a bug that empties/resets VRAM while it is used by an LLM workload, so I have not updated. The driver predates the bundled ROCm 10.2.0a20260930; if a specific driver version is known-good with this ROCm, please name it.
- **RAM:** 96 GB RAM, page file 96 GB (commit limit ≈ 192 GB, ~68 GB free at crash time)
- **TDR:** `TdrDelay=20`, `TdrDdiDelay=10` already set in `GraphicsDrivers` (the hang exceeds 20 s)
- **Model:** Qwen3.8-Flash-Next GSQ-RCO **IQ3_S** native pack, MTP rt, expert-profile
  - flags: `--expert-cache auto --prefill auto --spec 4 --spec-min-p 0.5 --kv int8 --kv-resident 32768`, hipBLASLt table `gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt`

## Steps to reproduce

The server restarts the engine each time (see timeline). Exact json:

```bash
{
 "exe": "J:\\Strata-main\\engine\\strata.exe",
 "args": [
  "--pack",
  "J:\\Strata-data\\packs\\iq3_s",
  "--native",
  "J:\\Strata-data\\models\\IQ3_S\\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00001-of-00002.gguf",
  "--ple-gguf",
  "J:\\Strata-data\\models\\IQ3_S\\Qwen3.8-Flash-Next-GSQ-RCO-IQ3_S-00002-of-00002.gguf",
  "--expert-profile",
  "J:\\Strata-main\\data\\expert-profile.bin",
  "--expert-cache",
  "auto",
  "--prefill",
  "auto",
  "--spec",
  "4",
  "--spec-min-p",
  "0.5",
  "--mtp",
  "J:\\Strata-data\\mtp\\rt",
  "--max-context",
  "229376",
  "--kv",
  "int8",
  "--kv-resident",
  "32768"
 ],
 "cwd": "J:\\Strata-main",
 "tokenizer": "J:\\Strata-data\\packs\\iq3_s\\tokenizer",
 "model_name": "qwen3.8-flash-next-iq3_s",
 "log": "J:\\Strata-main\\strata-iq3_s.log",
 "lib_dirs": [
  "J:\\Strata-main\\engine\\rocm\\bin"
 ],
 "port": 8080,
 "host": "0.0.0.0",
 "backend": "hip",
 "env": {
  "STRATA_HIPBLASLT_TUNING": "J:\\Strata-main\\tools\\hip\\gfx1201-hipblaslt-100500.txt"
 },
 "gpu": 1,
 "gpus_asked": true
}
```

## Symptom (engine log, 0.1.41, 262144)

The line `strata verify: capturing the N-token window` never prints — the engine dies before/at the first capture.

```text
strata generate: expert cache auto: 25.10 GiB free, 2560 MiB reserved (+218 MiB for the draft head) -> 9029 slots
strata generate: session is up (engine 0.1.41)
strata serve: prompt chunk auto: 8192 tokens, a 384-slot ring
strata serve: the prompt path borrows 2302 CUDA0 cache slots (4.38 GiB)
pref gemm: hipBLASLt tuning enabled (32 rows, gfx1201, version 100500)
strata verify: window up to 6 tokens, 75.8 MiB of device buffers
strata mtp: draft head over 106299 tokens (212.9 MiB)
strata serve: 2308 MiB of VRAM free with everything loaded
hipModuleUnload failed:
 error: unspecified launch failure
Exception Code: 0xC00000FD
```

Windows Error Reporting for the same minute:

- `LiveKernelEvent` **141** at 20:37:10 and 20:37:38 (dump `WATCHDOG-20261009-2037.dmp`)
- `APPCRASH`: `strata.exe`, faulting module `Dbghelp.dll` 10.0.19041.7725, exception `0xc0000005` (the engine's own crash handler faulting; the `0xC00000FD` in the log looks secondary)

## Timeline (2026-10-09, server auto-restarts the engine each time)

| Start | Engine | max-context | Outcome |
|---|---|---|---|
| 20:26:08 | 0.1.40.2 | 262144 | died at serve init; log printed its own warning: `447 MiB of VRAM free … that is little room for the verify windows' buffers under WDDM` (the #1275 shape, 700 MiB default reserve) |
| 20:32:43 | 0.1.41 | 262144 | 2308 MiB free → died at first capture, `unspecified launch failure` + `0xC00000FD` |
| 20:37:10 | 0.1.41 | 262144 | same; LiveKernelEvent 141 ×2 |
| 20:38:07 | 0.1.41 | 262144 | same (died within ~50 s) |
| 20:39:00 | 0.1.41 | 196608 | fine, served for hours |
| 21:05:58 | 0.1.41 | **229376** | **fine**: all six windows captured (`upload no error, sync no error`), then a real prompt of 119,136 fresh tokens read at 305 tok/s, a second 121,020-token prompt with 119,403 reused, decode 52 tok/s, expert-cache hit 92.6 %, KV streaming 96 % VRAM hit |

## What rules out the obvious suspects

- **Not VRAM pressure:** 2308 MiB free at the 262144 crash vs 2306 MiB free at the working 229376 start — identical headroom; the 0.1.41 2560 MiB auto-reserve (#1376) is active in both.
- **Not the commit limit (#1607/#1630):** ~68 GB of commit free at the crash time; the crash is at serve init, before any prompt.
- **Not TDR being too short:** `TdrDelay` is already 20 s; the GPU is wedged for more than that.
- **Not model/context infeasible on this card:** the docs' own R9700 runs IQ3_S at 431072 ctx on Linux, and #1565 ran IQ3_S @ 262144 on gfx1201 (ROCm). It's the Windows/WDDM capture path.


## Not yet tried (happy to run anything)

`--prefill auto:4096` at 262144 (expect little given the identical VRAM), `--vram-reserve-mib 3584`,  `STRATA_HIP_WMMA=1`, a newer AMD driver — held back for the VRAM-clearing bug described above.

## Related

#961 (WDDM verify window wedges the driver → 0x141 → TDR; there on NVIDIA), #1275 (the VRAM-tight variant, matches my first 0.1.40.2 start), #1630, #1644 (GPU faults on native IQ packs on Windows HIP).

## Question

If a specific AMD driver version is known-good with ROCm 10.2.0a20260930, please name it.

title: bench: add RTX 5060 Ti / Xeon E5-2680 v4 community results
body:
## Summary

Adds a results-only Strata 0.1.41 community benchmark submission for a Windows 10 machine with:

- NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5060 Ti 16 GB
- Intel Xeon E5-2680 v4, 14 cores / 28 threads
- 64 GB RAM
- PCIe Gen 3 x8

Two optimized, text-only Qwen3.8-Flash-Next configurations were measured: Coder IQ1_M and an abliterated Q2_0 derivative.

No engine, server, or Web UI code is changed by this PR.

## Method

The submitted `benchmark.py` is byte-for-byte unchanged from the repository's community benchmark script.

For each model:

- one warm-up request was excluded
- three fresh requests were run serially at 4,096 / 32,768 / 128,000 prompt tokens
- every measured request generated exactly 256 tokens
- temperature was 0
- reasoning was disabled
- every prompt used a unique nonce
- Strata reported **zero reused prompt tokens** in all 18 measured requests
- loading time was excluded; each model remained loaded for its complete nine-request sweep

The compact submission includes results, summaries, initial server status, Strata BUILD metadata, sanitized measured configs, and a README. Bulky raw request/chunk dumps were intentionally omitted and are documented in `TRIMMED.md`.

## Results — Coder IQ1_M

Median of three runs:

| Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | **1,179.7** | **47.46** | **3.529 s** |
| 32,768 | **1,600.6** | **51.02** | **20.558 s** |
| 128,000 | **1,859.5** | **49.13** | **69.047 s** |

## Results — abliterated Q2_0

Median of three runs:

| Prompt tokens | Prompt tok/s | Decode tok/s | TTFT |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 4,096 | **782.2** | **68.02** | **5.273 s** |
| 32,768 | **1,549.4** | **73.39** | **21.224 s** |
| 128,000 | **1,513.8** | **68.54** | **84.751 s** |

## Notes

- Both are optimized local configurations rather than Strata setup defaults.
- Both use a 262,144-token context limit, INT8 KV, resident KV, and MTP speculative decoding.
- No vision projector was loaded for either accepted run.
- The Q2 arm is an abliterated derivative with a workload-trained expert profile; the benchmark reports throughput, not a quality comparison.
- The 128K test does not fill the full 262K context window.
- The accepted benchmark runs were single-client, serial, and uncontaminated.

Full min/max ranges, total timings, exact measured settings, limitations, and hardware/software details are in the submitted `README.md`, `results.json`, and `summary.json`.

title: web: add persistent chats and MCP management
body:
## Summary

Adds a native-feeling persistence and MCP-management layer to Strata's existing Web UI without changing the inference engine or model-specific defaults.

## What changed

- Persist Web UI conversations as JSON under `conversations/`, with a docked conversation list, switching, New Chat creating a new conversation instead of clearing history, and delete confirmation.
- Add a dedicated **MCP** tab between Monitor and About.
- Manage any number of MCP servers using either transport Strata already supports:
  - Streamable HTTP via `url`.
  - stdio via `command`, JSON `args`, optional `cwd`, and JSON `env`.
- Show per-server connection state, transport, and enumerated tools.
- Add exact context usage through Strata's current template/tokenizer path, displayed as a semi-circular used/total gauge.
- Add dependency-free syntax highlighting for fenced code blocks while preserving the existing Markdown renderer and Strata styling.

### MCP configuration safety

The UI is a frontend for Strata's existing MCP backend rather than a parallel protocol implementation.

- HTTP header values and stdio environment values are never returned to the browser.
- Hidden HTTP headers are preserved only while the URL is unchanged.
- Hidden stdio env values are preserved only while command/args/cwd are unchanged; changing the launch identity drops them instead of silently forwarding credentials to a different process.
- Editing/removing one named server leaves the others untouched.
- stdio is explicitly described as starting a local process with the user's rights.
- Changes are persisted to the current run config and take effect after restarting Strata.

### Conversation persistence

- UUID-backed IDs are validated before becoming paths.
- Writes use a unique temporary file followed by atomic replace.
- Conversation files are capped at 64 MiB.
- `/conversations/` is gitignored.
- The existing browser-local chat remains only as a fallback/migration path.

### Context meter

`/context-count` runs the current OpenAI-shaped Web UI history through Strata's own conversion/template/tokenizer path, including MCP tool schemas when enabled. The displayed count is therefore the actual prompt shape Strata will send, not a character estimate.

## Validation

Clean worktree based on current `origin/main`:

- `serve.test_local_ui`: **9/9 passed**
- `serve.test_server`: **271/271 passed**
- `serve.test_mcp`: **25/25 passed**
- `serve.test_runconfig`: **9/9 passed**
- `node --check serve/web/app.js`: passed
- Python compile checks: passed
- `git diff --check`: passed

A live acceptance test also added a stdio server beside an existing HTTP server, verified both were listed together, confirmed secret env values were not returned to the browser, verified the preserve/drop rules across edits, removed only the temporary server, and confirmed the original server remained unchanged.

## Screenshots

![Persistent conversations, syntax highlighting, and context gauge](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VykosX/Strata/pr-assets/screenshots/PR_CHAT.png)

![Multiple MCP servers using HTTP and stdio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/VykosX/Strata/pr-assets/screenshots/PR_MCP.png)

title: On-disk conversations and the system prompt: spill tier, prefill cache, layer-split plumbing - tested against v0.1.41
body:
## Title
On-disk conversations and the system prompt: spill tier, prefill cache, layer-split plumbing - tested against `v0.1.41`

Issue: Resolves #

## Summary
An opt-in **on-disk layer** for long conversations: a disk tier that parks a conversation's K/V image when the RAM cache fills and restores it on a later request, a **system-prompt prefill cache**, both working across a **layer split**, plus `--head-device` card placement and acceptance reporting for `--batch-mtp`.

This is the same on-disk layer as the previous version of this PR, **rebased and re-verified against upstream `v0.1.41` (`fb58e0d`)** - and, since that version, **run live against it**. Every statement below is about that base.

## What changed
- **The whole series is rebased onto `v0.1.41`** - 17 commits, original authorship preserved, including the #1271/#1269 cherry-picks.
- **The `make_room` conflict is resolved semantically, not textually**: the spill hook now lives in `evict_oldest()`, which gained a `template<class Spill>` overload. The zero-argument overload stays, so **with the layer's flags off the code is upstream's byte for byte**, and the hook sees the real eviction victim (which can be evicted from the middle of the deque) instead of a fixed `entries_.front()`.
- **The `put()` re-reservation hole is closed**: `put()` re-reserves with the real post-capture `image.bytes()`, which typically exceeds the estimate `make_room()` balanced against - so eviction at `put()` is the **normal** path of a large insert, not an edge case. `put()` gained a spill-callback overload and the park path propagates it. (`drop_superseded()` is deliberately left without a hook, and documented as considered-and-declined.)
- **Docs**: `docs/FLAGS.md` (every flag, its scope, its non-claim, and a section on the upstream mechanisms this layer lives beside without fusing with - `pin=N`, `--peer-device`, `STRATA_KV_GROW_HOLD`), `docs/SPILL_AND_PROMPT_CACHE.md` (how it works, its limits, what was verified and what was not, now including the live run), a README section, and the host-only tests for the pure classes.
- **One known limitation ships declared rather than fixed** - the divergence-discard path can name a sibling conversation's copy under a chat template that puts few-shot turns inside the system prompt. It is stated in `docs/SPILL_AND_PROMPT_CACHE.md` and in Extra Notes below; the fix is the next stacked PR on this branch.

## Extra Notes
### Evidence - static, against `v0.1.41`
CUDA build exit 0 - the `strata.exe` verified here is sha256 `C1D54A4F5A405F076A0D5F1EB0384DECB5A5E422C3A109A7AD6CD7B86A26FB99`; its `--help` lists all 17 flags of the layer; an unknown flag is fatal (`unknown argument`, exit 2); the host-only test battery passes **12/12** (`ctest` exit 0); the layer's anchor/flag verifier (39 anchors, 17 flags) exits 0.

### Evidence - live, against `v0.1.41`
That same binary served `127.0.0.1:5012` on the verification machine on a clone of the production serve config (production stays on 5011 and was not touched) and reported `/props` `build_info='Strata 0.1.41'`, `n_ctx=196608`, model `qwen3.8-flash-next-unsloth-ud-iq4_xs`, ready in **156.6 s** in both runs. A four-test battery (smoke, streamed throughput, repeated system prompt, two conversations that spill) ran **twice**, with a server restart between runs and the tier's folders left in place. The second run passed all four tests (`OVERALL: PASS`); the first reported `OVERALL: FAIL` for one reason only - its harness (v1.0.0) could not compute a throughput figure at `max_tokens=256`.

- **Cold prefill against a restore after a restart.** Two ~8k-token conversations (`prompt_tokens=8016`) took **29.76 s** and **30.10 s** in the first run (a fresh process, nothing on disk for them) and **1.98 s** each in the second (a new process, both already on disk), with the engine counting `restores=4` in that second run against `restores=0` in the first. The 33,409-character system-prompt test has the same shape: **30.296 s** for its first call in the first run (nothing reused) against **2.298 s** for the same call in the second.
- **The tier's counters, read from the running engine:** `disk: enabled=True spills=2 bytes=2153775104 restores=4` over a folder of 19 files / 2,154,484,304 bytes, and `sysprompt: enabled=True variants=3 hits=1 misses=0 bytes=719323136`.
- **What the build serves** (a property of the build, not of the layer): with no output cap and a natural stop, three reps produced 472 / 480 / 458 tokens (`finish=stop`) at a median TTFT of **0.452 s**, at **28.11 tok/s** decoding (27.39 tok/s end to end).

**What the live numbers are not.** Both runs used the same binary with the layer **on**, so what is measured is **cold prefill against a restore from disk after a process restart** - nothing more. It is not a comparison against upstream, not a speedup ratio for the layer, and not a throughput claim about it. `restores=4` and `hits=1` are **one run each**: a working signal, not a rate. The `conversations=0` on that same counter line is what the engine reports and is not interpreted here. The system-prompt test of the second run (TTFT 1.096 s then 1.52 s, with `reused=7920/7925` already warm) is one sample of a warm prefix, not a regression - and the **-92.6 %** of the first run is a cold-prefill KV-reuse figure (that run read `sysprompt hits=0`), so it is not a property of the system-prompt cache either.

### What this PR does not claim
The previous version of this PR said "not tested live against `v0.1.41`". That non-claim is **withdrawn** - the runs above happened. What is still not claimed:

- **No layer-versus-no-layer run.** Both live runs had the layer on, so nothing here is a measured speedup over upstream, and no performance number anywhere in the diff is one.
- **Two runs of one harness on one machine.** One `restores=4`, one `hits=1`, one median TTFT, one conversation length. Both runs read `tokens_saved=0`, so there is no hit rate and no tokens-saved total.
- **Not every flag was reached.** The battery did not exercise `--head-device` card order, a layer split, `--batch-mtp`, a cancelled request, the GC's age and budget levers, or the compaction path (when a rewrite happens is the harness's decision, and this delivery carries no archive tier). That the layer is inert with the flags off under load is likewise still unshown.
- The host-only tests cover the pure classes (cache, spill, file, prompt cache, stage plan); the live battery covers the `--serve` loop for those four scenarios and nothing beyond them.

### Known limitation: the divergence discard can name a sibling's copy
`discard_diverged_impl` (`src/core/conversation_spill.cpp`) decides which stored copy a rewritten tail belongs to from the end of the stored conversation's header - `conversation_header_length`, the start of its first assistant turn - and keeps a copy whose shared prefix reaches past that marker (`header == 0 || common < header` skips it). **Few-shot turns inside the system prompt** move that marker into the root the conversations share, so a **sibling** conversation (same system prompt, a different first exchange) also satisfies the guard, and its copy is the one removed - **discarded from disk, not archived**, in this version.

The fix is a property guard: only the copy sharing the **longest prefix** with the prompt is a rewrite candidate, a tie between copies that disagree discards nothing, and a trace line names the `conversation_key` of the copy removed. It is written and tested on a sibling branch and arrives as the **next stacked PR against this branch**; this delta ships without it. Being straight about the scope of the evidence: the reproducing test was written against the sibling base `v0.1.40.1`, **not** against `v0.1.41`, and has not been re-run here. The live battery above does not reach that path.

### Collaboration
This overlaps in territory with **#1529** (a disk tier for parked conversations) - it looks like the two efforts are complementary rather than competing, and I'm glad to align on naming or split the series so both can land; the `put()` re-reservation fix here is made against `v0.1.41` and may be useful to that effort too. It also sits beside the supersession fix in **konijiwa110/Strata#1**; this series does not depend on its outcome. I haven't verified either PR's contents beyond their threads, so I won't claim more than "same area, happy to coordinate" - whatever split the maintainers prefer works for me.

### Credits
This layer is authored and directed by **Shahrokh Zargarpour**. It was written and verified with the **Grok TUI Build** coding agent - first on **DeepSeek Flash**, currently on **Qwen3.8 flash-next UD iq4_xs**, the local inference runtime the layer was developed and verified against.

title: serve: effort_position "end" reads the SYCL engine binary, not its launcher script (#1781)
body:
## Title
Issue: Resolves #1781

## Summary
`"effort_position": "end"` (#458) never turned on with the Intel port: the server checked the launcher script `sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh` for `--tail-role-token` instead of the engine binary it runs, and fell back to the top-of-prompt effort with "needs engine 0.1.39 or newer". This resolves the launcher to its binary before the check. CUDA and HIP are untouched: their `exe` is the engine and is read as before.

## What changed
- `serve/server.py`: new `engine_binary(exe, cfg)`. For an `exe` named `strata-sycl.sh` it returns the launcher's repo + `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` (from the config's `env`, else the environment, else `build-sycl-aot/strata`, the launcher's own default) when that file exists; otherwise `exe` unchanged. `effort_end_args()` reads that file instead of `exe`. Nothing else uses it.
- `tools/test_effort_end_args.py` (new, no GPU, fake files in a temp repo): launcher + binary with the option -> args; binary without it -> None; `STRATA_SYCL_BIN` from the config's `env`; launcher with no binary -> falls back to reading the launcher (old behaviour); a plain engine `exe` with and without the option (unchanged path); `start`/unset stays off.

## How it was checked
- `python -m unittest tools.test_effort_end_args`: 6 pass on `fb58e0d` + this commit. Without the `server.py` change the two launcher tests fail (2 failures), so they test the fix.
- On an Arc Pro B65 (engine 0.1.41 built with `sycl/tools/build.sh`), `engine_binary(".../sycl/serve/strata-sycl.sh", {})` resolves to `.../build-sycl-aot/strata`, which contains `--tail-role-token`.
- Not tested: a full server start with `effort_position: end` on this exact commit (the card was busy with a benchmark); the default path (`effort_position` unset or `start`) returns before the new code, so it is unchanged.

## Extra Notes
Only the Python server is touched; no engine rebuild needed. Assisted-by: Claude Code.
